name: Taxi zone partition
description: The city is split into the TLC's 263 taxi zones (plus 2 unknown codes), the spatial unit of every public trip record.
values_or_range: 263 zones: Manhattan 69, Queens 69, Brooklyn 61, Bronx 43, Staten Island 20, EWR 1; IDs 264/265 = unknown / outside NYC [corrected by fact-check: in the current TLC lookup 264 = Unknown and 265 = 'Outside of NYC'; older copies label both Unknown (NV / NA)]
impact_evidence: [P] Counted 265 rows in taxi_zone_lookup.csv (GitHub copy of the TLC file; borough and service-zone counts reproduced); all trip data is keyed to these IDs; [S] dataset ID 755u-8jsi confirmed by many GitHub pipelines that download it [corrected by fact-check: impact high -> medium; the partition is a structural layer whose profit effect flows through R01-003, R01-004 and R01-009]
data_source: NYC Taxi Zones, NYC Open Data 755u-8jsi (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/755u-8jsi); TLC lookup + shapefile (https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page)
how_to_model: Load zone polygons; map every car and request position to a zone ID; demand, fares and stats keyed by zone

name: Service-zone class
description: Each zone belongs to a TLC service class that decides who may street-hail there and which fare rules apply.
values_or_range: Yellow Zone 55 (Manhattan core) / Boro Zone 205 (14 upper Manhattan + 191 outer borough) / Airports 2 (JFK 132, LGA 138) / EWR 1
impact_evidence: [P] Lookup counts; 89.0% of yellow pickups were in the 55 Yellow Zone zones (Oct 2019, own computation)
how_to_model: Zone attribute checked by hail-eligibility and fare rules

name: Pickup concentration (spatial skew)
description: How unevenly trip origins are spread across zones; the more concentrated, the more location choice matters.
values_or_range: Yellow Oct 2019: 16 zones = 50% of pickups, 32 = 80%, 48 = 95%; HVFHV Jun 2021: 60 / 125 / 188 zones
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation on TLC yellow (Oct 2019, 7.08M trips) and HVFHV (Jun 2021, 14.96M trips) records
data_source: TLC trip records (yellow, green, FHV, HVFHV)
how_to_model: Demand generator samples origins from a zone x hour intensity fitted to trip records; historic heatmap can be given to the agent as public info

name: Zone pickup/drop-off imbalance
description: Ratio of pickups to drop-offs per zone; zones well below 1 are 'sinks' where a driver lands with few nearby requests.
values_or_range: Yellow Oct 2019 PU/DO: Manhattan 1.02, Queens 1.30, Brooklyn 0.27, Bronx 0.24, Staten Island 0.14; zone extremes JFK 3.81, Windsor Terrace 0.08, Washington Heights North 0.09 [corrected by fact-check: Windsor Terrace, not Washington Heights North, is the lowest zone with >3,000 drop-offs; JFK is 3.53 under a lighter cleaning filter that keeps zero-distance trips]. HVFHV Jun 2021: every borough 1.02-1.06
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019 and HVFHV Jun 2021 (reproduced by fact-check)
how_to_model: Emerges from the OD matrix; expose historic PU/DO ratio per zone x hour as a public layer

name: Taxi vs app geographic footprint
description: Street-hail demand sits in the Manhattan core while app demand is spread over the outer boroughs, so the same map rewards different positioning by driver type.
values_or_range: Share of pickups in Yellow Zone: yellow 89.0% vs HVFHV 32.2%; outer boroughs: 2.2% vs 59.5%. Manhattan HV trips fell 6.1% Jan 2025 to Jan 2026 while other boroughs grew
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation (yellow Oct 2019 vs HVFHV Jun 2021); [S] TLC license pause report Feb 2026 [uncertain: the -6.1% Manhattan figure from the Feb 2026 licence pause report was not re-checked; nyc.gov blocked]
data_source: TLC trip records; TLC license pause reports (https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/license-pause-report-2026-02.pdf)
how_to_model: Separate demand layers per channel (street hail, e-hail) with their own zone weights

name: Green taxi hail exclusionary zone
description: Green (boro) taxis may not accept street hails or e-hails in Manhattan south of E 96th St and W 110th St or at JFK and LGA, and may not begin base-dispatched (pre-arranged) trips in that part of Manhattan; they may drop off anywhere. [corrected by fact-check: the rule also bans pre-arranged starts in Manhattan south of E 96th / W 110th, and an e-hail counts as a hail]
values_or_range: Excluded: 55 Yellow Zone zones + 2 airports. Green Oct 2019 pickups: 64.6% outer boroughs, 32.3% upper Manhattan, 3.1% Yellow Zone; 18.5% of drop-offs in Yellow Zone; fine $500 plus suspension for a first violation
impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 51-03 (Hail Exclusionary Zone and Pre-Arranged Exclusionary Zone definitions), 82-13 and 80-20(b)(11), read from a verbatim copy current through 13 Aug 2026; [P] own computation, green Oct 2019 (473,824 trips, reproduced)
data_source: 35 RCNY 51-03 and 82-13 (verbatim copy https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive); TLC green cab page (https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/businesses/green-cab.page); TLC green trip records
how_to_model: Street-hail and e-hail generation disabled for green cars inside the excluded polygons; base-dispatched trips may not start in excluded Manhattan but may start at JFK/LGA [corrected by fact-check: the original said e-hail was still allowed]

name: Licensing jurisdiction boundary
description: The area where the vehicle's licence allows pickups (NYC for TLC vehicles); trips may end outside it, but pickups outside are effectively unavailable.
values_or_range: Inside five boroughs: pickups allowed. Outside: drop-off only. EWR: yellow 57 pickups vs 15,829 drop-offs (Oct 2019); HVFHV 228 vs 63,278 (Jun 2021). Uber JFK pickups only for TLC-licensed drivers
impact_evidence: [P] Own counts from TLC records; [S] Uber JFK driver-information page
data_source: TLC trip records; Uber airport driver pages; county taxi rules [U]
how_to_model: Pickup-eligibility mask by polygon and licence type

name: Spatial resolution
description: The unit at which positions and demand are represented: taxi zone, hex grid or road segment.
values_or_range: Taxi zone (~3 km2 mean, 263 units) / H3 hex res 8 (~0.7 km2) / OSM drivable road graph (tens of thousands of nodes)
impact_evidence: [design] Finer resolution lets positioning skill show but costs compute and data; zone level matches public trip data
data_source: TLC zones; OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org); NYC DCP LION
how_to_model: Start at zone level with a random point inside the zone; upgrade to a road graph for routing, curbs and hails

name: Zone adjacency and travel-time skim
description: A zone-to-zone neighbour list and travel-time matrix used for repositioning and fleet rebalancing.
values_or_range: 263 x 263 matrix of travel times by hour (minutes); neighbour lists
impact_evidence: [design] Needed by both single-car repositioning and fleet rebalancing; R10 supplies the times
data_source: Derived from OSM graph + TLC trip durations; NYC DOT traffic speeds (cross-link R10)
how_to_model: Precompute skims per hour band; agent tools query ETA between zones

name: Road hierarchy class
description: Each road segment's class (expressway or parkway, arterial avenue, collector, local) sets its speed, capacity and how good it is for finding hails.
values_or_range: OSM highway = motorway / trunk / primary / secondary / tertiary / residential. Mean in-trip speed: ~10.2 mph for Yellow Zone pickups vs ~20.9 mph for airport pickups (yellow Oct 2019)
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation (distance / duration) from TLC yellow Oct 2019
data_source: OpenStreetMap; NYC DCP LION street centerline (lanes, width, direction)
how_to_model: Graph edges carry class: free-flow speed and capacity; congestion handled in R10

name: One-way streets and circuity
description: Manhattan's mostly one-way grid and the rivers make driving distance longer than straight-line distance, and a pickup on the wrong side costs a loop.
values_or_range: Most avenues and most cross streets one-way [corrected by fact-check: some avenues are two-way, e.g. Park Ave, Central Park West, West End Ave, York Ave [U]]; major two-way crosstown streets (14th, 23rd, 34th, 42nd, 57th, 72nd, 79th, 86th, 96th, 110th, 125th); circuity ~1.2-1.4; turn-around loop ~2-4 blocks
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge of the NYC grid; LION has a traffic-direction field
data_source: NYC DCP LION (TrafDir); OSM oneway tag
how_to_model: Directed graph; car heading matters for pickup ETA

name: Road access by vehicle class
description: Some roads are closed to some vehicles: parkways ban commercial vehicles (taxis and FHVs count as passenger cars) and robotaxis may be kept off freeways.
values_or_range: Parkway allowed yes/no; robotaxi freeway allowed yes/no (scenario)
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; medium for robotaxi if freeways are excluded
data_source: OSM access tags; NYSDOT parkway rules [U]
how_to_model: Edge mask per vehicle class

name: Elevation and grade
description: Hills slightly raise energy use; NYC is mostly flat with steep spots (Washington Heights, Staten Island, parts of the Bronx).
values_or_range: Grade 0-10%+; elevation 0 to ~125 m
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge
data_source: USGS 3DEP; NYC 1-ft DEM on NYC Open Data [U]
how_to_model: Edge grade feeds an energy multiplier in R08

name: River crossings as chokepoints
description: Manhattan and Staten Island are islands and the Bronx is cut off from Manhattan and Queens by water, so most links between boroughs and all links to New Jersey are bridges or tunnels; they concentrate delay, incidents and tolls. [corrected by fact-check: Brooklyn and Queens share a land border and the Bronx joins Westchester by land, so bridges and tunnels are not the only links]
values_or_range: East River: Brooklyn, Manhattan, Williamsburg, Queensboro bridges (free), Queens-Midtown and Hugh Carey tunnels and RFK (tolled); Hudson: GWB, Lincoln, Holland (PANYNJ); Harlem River bridges free except the MTA Henry Hudson Bridge (tolled); Verrazzano, Throgs Neck, Whitestone, Cross Bay, Marine Pkwy (MTA, tolled); Staten Island to NJ: Goethals, Bayonne, Outerbridge (PANYNJ, tolled) [corrected by fact-check: added the Henry Hudson Bridge and the Staten Island-NJ crossings [U]]
impact_evidence: [P] 5.9% of yellow trips paid a toll, mean $6.63 (Oct 2019, own computation, reproduced); [U] network facts [corrected by fact-check: impact high -> medium; tolls are mostly passed to riders and crossing delay is modelled in R10]
data_source: OpenStreetMap; NYC DOT bridge traffic volumes [U]
how_to_model: Crossing edges with their own capacity, incident probability (R03) and travel-time variance (R10)

name: Busways and transit-priority streets
description: Streets where through car traffic is banned for set hours, but taxis and FHVs may enter for local pickups and must turn off at the next street.
values_or_range: 14th St busway (3rd to 9th Ave, 6am-10pm daily; cars may enter to pick up or drop off and must turn right within a block or two, no left turns) [corrected by fact-check: the original said 3rd to 8th Ave]; others such as Main St Flushing, Jamaica Ave, Archer Ave, 181st St [U]; 34th St bus priority (2025)
impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-12(m)(2): only buses and Access-A-Ride vans during restricted hours except where signs allow; [S] NYT (Oct 2019, GitHub copy) and Village Sun / amNY on 14th St busway rules; NYC DOT 34th St documents
how_to_model: Edges with through-traffic ban + forced turn after a stop

name: Car-free park drives and plazas
description: Roads closed to cars inside demand areas, so pickups move to the edges and routes detour.
values_or_range: Central Park loop drives car-free since 27 Jun 2018 (transverses open); Prospect Park loop car-free; Times Square / Broadway plazas; Open Streets time windows
impact_evidence: [S] ABC7, Central Park Conservancy (2018)
data_source: OSM; NYC DOT Open Streets data [U]
how_to_model: Remove edges (permanently or by time); snap pickups to the nearest legal curb

name: Gated and single-access destinations
description: Destinations behind gates or ID checks, or reachable by only one road, add a security wait or a long detour that a zone-level map misses. The examples are NYC places; other cities can be generalised from OSM tags.
values_or_range: Brooklyn Navy Yard (gated); Fort Hamilton (military ID check); Rikers Island (single bridge, security); Breezy Point (gated private cooperative); Roosevelt Island (cars only via the bridge from Queens); City Island (single bridge); JFK cargo areas. Gate delay 2-15 min. Detour up to 10-20 min, e.g. reaching Roosevelt Island from Manhattan [design].
impact_evidence: [U] Local geography; [design]. Could be measured from OSM barrier and access tags.
how_to_model: Gate nodes with a delay distribution and an access class per vehicle type. Single-access zones are routed only through their one link.

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Curb regulation at the stop point
description: The sign type at the curb decides whether a quick pickup or drop-off is legal.
values_or_range: No Parking (stop OK) / No Standing (quick passenger pickup OK, no waiting) / No Stopping (not allowed) / bus stop (OK if no bus is blocked) / taxi stand (taxis only; other cars may only briefly load, and TLC fines an FHV driver $350 for a first pickup at a taxi stand) / 'For-Hire Vehicles Only' curb ($115 if standing beyond a quick pickup [uncertain: fine amount not checked]) [corrected by fact-check: added the taxi-stand pickup ban for FHVs]
impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-11(c): taxis and FHVs may briefly stop to pick up or drop off where standing or parking is banned, within 12 in of the curb, but not where stopping is banned, in a bike lane or in a crosswalk; 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(1); 35 RCNY 80-19(d)(2); [S] NYC DOT parking sign legend; NYC DOF violation codes
data_source: NYC DOT Parking Regulation Locations and Signs (NYC Open Data) [U]
how_to_model: Curb-segment attribute; illegal stop = fine probability or forced re-loop

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Taxi stands and hotel queues
description: Designated stands (hotels, transit hubs) where only taxis may wait in line for passengers.
values_or_range: Stand present yes/no; queue length 0-30 cabs [U]; the first two cabs must stay in the driver's seat; green cabs may use stands only in the Hail Zone
impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(1): only taxis may stand at a taxi stand; 35 RCNY 80-19(d): queue rules and green-cab limits; [S] NYC DOT sign legend
how_to_model: FIFO queue node fed by hotel or hub demand

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Taxi/FHV relief stands
description: Curb spaces where taxi and FHV drivers may park for up to one hour to take a break.
values_or_range: 113 stands: Manhattan 70, Queens 28, Bronx 12, Brooklyn 3, Staten Island 0 [uncertain: count not re-checked]; one-hour limit
impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(2): taxis and FHVs may park at a relief stand for no more than one hour; [S] Manhattan CB1 letter (2026) citing NYC DOT; NYC DOT relief-stand page
data_source: NYC Open Data 'Taxi and For-Hire Vehicle (FHV) Relief Stands' (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/taxi-and-for-hire-vehicle-fhv-relief-stands)
how_to_model: POI layer; a break elsewhere costs parking search time or ticket risk

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Legal waiting spots (staging)
description: Whether the car can legally sit still near a hotspot while waiting for the next request instead of cruising.
values_or_range: Share of curb where standing is legal per zone; parking $0-15+/h [U]; NYC anti-idling limit 3 min (1 min next to schools); a taxi awaiting a fare may stand only at a taxi stand (or at a hydrant with the driver in the seat); non-taxis may not cruise for passengers [corrected by fact-check: idling limits confirmed and staging rules added]
impact_evidence: [P*] NYC Admin Code 24-163(a), (f); 34 RCNY 4-11(a)-(b); [S] Schaller (2017): in the Manhattan CBD, app cars had 55K passenger hours vs 37K empty hours (60% busy), and utilisation fell from 67% (taxis, 2013) to 62% (taxis and apps, 2017) [uncertain: the '11 min vs 8 min empty between trips' figures were not found in the checked excerpts]
data_source: NYC DOT parking regulations; licensed garages on NYC Open Data [U]
how_to_model: Per-zone wait cost (fuel, ticket risk, parking fee) vs cruise cost; agent chooses wait, cruise or reposition

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Idle staging capacity
description: Number of legal places in a zone where idle fleet cars can wait without circling, double parking or paying a garage.
values_or_range: 0-50 cars per zone [design]; garage cost per hour; robotaxis need a legal stop.
impact_evidence: [design]; legal waiting spots (R01-032) and hotspot curb queues (R10-040).
data_source: NYC parking regulations and licensed garages on NYC Open Data [U]
how_to_model: Staging capacity per zone; extra idle cars must circle (miles) or use a paid lot.

sub_box: Curbs, stands and legal waiting spots
name: Doorman and hotel-starter relationships
description: Doormen and hotel starters may steer the best fares, such as airport runs, to cabs or black cars they know, sometimes for a tip.
values_or_range: 0-20% of hotel-stand airport fares steered to 'regular' drivers [design]; $5-20 tip to the starter [U].
impact_evidence: [U] Industry lore and press; no data found.
applies_to: taxi; human black-car driver (not app pool, not robotaxi)
how_to_model: At hotel stands (R05-044), a 'regular' state, built by repeat visits and tips, raises the chance of getting a long fare.

name: Pedestrian volume by location
description: How many people walk past a point; drives street-hail chances and is a proxy for latent ride demand.
values_or_range: DOT counts at 114 locations (100 on-street, mainly retail corridors; 13 bridges; Hudson River Greenway), counted each May and September
impact_evidence: [S] NYC Open Data dataset description (confirmed via GitHub copies: 114 locations, 100 on-street mostly retail corridors, 13 East River and Harlem River bridge points, Hudson River Greenway); Buchholz (2022, REStud): taxis are drawn to search in the most concentrated pedestrian areas [uncertain: this paraphrase of Buchholz was not checked against the paper]
how_to_model: Street-hail arrival rate per edge proportional to pedestrian intensity x hour profile, calibrated to yellow pickups

name: Pedestrian demand class of each street
description: NYC DOT's Pedestrian Mobility Plan puts every street in one of five pedestrian-demand classes.
values_or_range: Baseline (~60% of roads), Community Connector (~25%) [uncertain: shares not re-checked], Neighborhood Corridor, Regional Corridor, Global Corridor (mostly Manhattan)
impact_evidence: [S] NYC DOT Pedestrian Mobility Plan and data.gov dataset (modified Mar 2026); class names confirmed in GitHub uses of the Pedestrian_Demand file; [P*] 34 RCNY 5-11 uses the plan's corridor categories; MIT critique that some outer-borough streets are under-classified
how_to_model: Categorical edge attribute feeding hail rate and curb friction

name: Subway entries and exits by hour
description: Hourly subway ridership per station shows where crowds appear and when transit thins out, shaping first/last-mile and substitute demand.
values_or_range: Hourly counts by station complex: 2017-19 (t69i-h2me), 2020-24 (wujg-7c2s), 2025+ (5wq4-mkjj); OD estimates (jsu2-fbtj) [uncertain: one GitHub project reports wujg-7c2s data starting in Feb 2022; t69i-h2me and jsu2-fbtj exist in the MTA catalog but their titles were not confirmed]
impact_evidence: [S] data.ny.gov catalog entries; IDs 5wq4-mkjj (2025+) and wujg-7c2s (2020-24) confirmed by several GitHub pipelines
how_to_model: Demand covariate; subway outages (R03) move demand to cars near affected stations

name: Road-to-pedestrian ratio ('pickup-ability')
description: The user's idea: compare how many pedestrians gather on a block with how much drivable road and stoppable curb it has; busy but curb-starved streets mean many riders but slow, congested pickups.
values_or_range: Index = legal-stop curb metres / pedestrians per hour (or lanes / pedestrian class); bands low / medium / high; low examples Times Sq, SoHo
impact_evidence: [design]; Buchholz (2022): competition pushes taxis to spread search beyond the densest pedestrian areas [S] [uncertain: paraphrase not checked against the paper]
data_source: DOT pedestrian counts + Pedestrian Mobility Plan + LION width/lanes + DOT parking signs
how_to_model: Per-edge index raises hail rate (+) and pickup dwell / lowers through-speed (-)

name: Transit accessibility
description: Distance from a zone to the nearest subway station; areas far from rail rely more on cars for hire.
values_or_range: 0-3+ km to nearest station; transit-desert flag
impact_evidence: [P] Top HVFHV pickup zones include East New York, Crown Heights North, Bushwick South (Jun 2021); [U] transit-substitution mechanism
data_source: MTA GTFS static (https://new.mta.info/developers); NYC subway entrances (NYC Open Data)
how_to_model: Demand covariate; raises late-night demand when subway headways lengthen

name: Population and job density
description: Residents and workers per zone are the base of trip generation.
values_or_range: Residents/km2 and jobs/km2 per zone
impact_evidence: [U] Standard trip-generation practice; Correa, Chow and Ozbay model demand from the spatial distribution of activities [S]
how_to_model: Demand-generator covariates when extrapolating beyond replayed data

name: Hail visibility by street type
description: Street hails happen mostly on avenues and busy corridors that cabs pass often; side streets yield few hails.
values_or_range: Hail multiplier: avenue 1.0, cross street 0.2-0.5 [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design] / [U]; yellow records carry exact coordinates only until June 2016 (zone IDs from July 2016) [S] toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data README
data_source: Pre-2016 TLC yellow records with lat/lon
how_to_model: Generate hails per edge; a cruising agent only sees hails on edges it drives

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Land-use mix per zone
description: Share of residential, office, retail, nightlife, industrial and park land; sets the daily shape of demand.
values_or_range: MapPLUTO land-use classes (11) by lot area per zone
impact_evidence: [P] Share of core yellow pickups ending in outer boroughs: 1.4% at 8am vs 17.7% at 4am (Oct 2019), showing home-bound night flows
how_to_model: Zone feature vector; demand time profile depends on land-use mix

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Office and business districts
description: Midtown, Financial District, Hudson Yards, Downtown Brooklyn and Long Island City pull weekday daytime trips.
values_or_range: Jobs per zone; weekday vs weekend ratio
impact_evidence: [P] Midtown Center 4.2% and Midtown East 3.7% of all yellow pickups (Oct 2019)
how_to_model: Work-hour peaks per zone (remote-work days in R02)

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Nightlife density
description: Bars, clubs and late restaurants create late-night demand and longer, outbound trips.
values_or_range: On-premises liquor licences per zone; key areas LES, East Village, Meatpacking, Williamsburg, Bushwick
impact_evidence: [P] East Village is the #2 HVFHV pickup zone (Jun 2021); Meatpacking among the highest-tip drop-off zones (27%)
data_source: NYS Liquor Authority licences (data.ny.gov) [U]; DOHMH restaurant inspections [U]
how_to_model: Late-night demand multiplier; destinations drawn toward residential zones

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Tourist and hotel density
description: Hotels and attractions create airport trips, taxi-stand queues and riders less likely to use transit.
values_or_range: Hotel rooms per zone; attraction POIs
impact_evidence: [P] Times Sq/Theatre District = 3.5% of yellow pickups (Oct 2019)
data_source: OSM tourism tags; NYC hotel lists on NYC Open Data [U]
how_to_model: Hotel POIs as taxi-stand queues and airport-bound demand

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Hospitals, universities and institutions
description: Large hospitals produce steady trips around shift changes and discharges (plus paratransit rides); campuses shift demand with the academic calendar.
values_or_range: Beds per site; shift changes ~7am / 7pm [U]; enrolment per campus, term on/off
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; [P*] HVFHV records carry access_a_ride_flag (confirmed in the Jan 2023 schema)
data_source: NYS DOH health facility data (health.data.ny.gov) [U]; NCES IPEDS (campuses)
how_to_model: POI with a daily time profile and seasonal multiplier (R02)

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Venues, stadiums and convention centres
description: Fixed big venues whose location, capacity and exits shape event surges (the events themselves are in R03).
values_or_range: Capacity 2k-50k (MSG, Barclays, Yankee Stadium, Citi Field, USTA, UBS Arena, Javits, Lincoln Center); exit curb capacity
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; MSG sits on Penn Station (zone 186, top-5 yellow pickup zone) [P]
how_to_model: Venue nodes with capacity; R03 schedules events on them

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Retail and shopping corridors
description: Shopping streets create daytime and weekend short trips.
values_or_range: Retail floor area per zone
impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; most DOT pedestrian count sites are retail corridors [S]
data_source: MapPLUTO retail area; DOT pedestrian counts
how_to_model: Daytime / weekend demand covariate

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Neighbourhood income
description: Median household income of pickup and drop-off areas, which tracks card use, trip length and tipping.
values_or_range: ACS median income per tract mapped to zone; card-trip tip/fare 25.9% for Yellow Zone pickups vs 19.3% outer boroughs; lowest drop-off zones 18.8-19.2% (Stuyvesant Heights, Central Harlem North, Crown Heights North) vs ~27% (UES, UWS, West Village)
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, yellow Oct 2019 card trips (tips are recorded only for card payments); reproduced, and robust alternatives give the same gap (tip/fare ratio of sums 23.9% vs 17.9%; medians 26.3% vs 22.2%)
data_source: US Census ACS; TLC tips (yellow card trips; HVFHV tips column)
how_to_model: Zone covariate for tip probability and size (behaviour owned by R05)

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Payment mix by zone
description: Share of cash vs card trips by area; affects recorded tips and cash handling for taxis (app trips are cashless).
values_or_range: Card share, yellow Oct 2019: Yellow Zone 74.2%, upper Manhattan 58.8%, outer boroughs 51.7%, airports 64.7%
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
how_to_model: Per-zone payment-type probability

sub_box: Land use, trip generators and neighbourhood character
name: Perceived safety and crime
description: Crime and drivers' sense of risk make some drivers avoid areas at night, thinning supply there and raising surge for those who stay, with a small real incident risk.
values_or_range: Complaints per 1,000 residents by precinct and hour; avoidance probability 0-1 [design]
impact_evidence: [U] / [design]; benchmark must not reward illegal refusal
how_to_model: Lower competitor supply in high-perceived-risk zones at night; small incident probability

name: Intercity rail and bus hubs
description: Penn Station/Moynihan, Grand Central, Port Authority Bus Terminal, Atlantic Terminal and Jamaica produce rider pulses timed to public train and bus arrivals.
values_or_range: Penn Station/Madison Sq West = 3.6% of yellow pickups, PU/DO 1.40 (Oct 2019); arrival schedules public in GTFS
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019
data_source: GTFS feeds (MTA, NJ Transit, Amtrak); TLC records
how_to_model: Hub nodes with arrival-driven pulses + taxi-stand queues

name: Airport trip share and value
description: Airport trips are few but long and lucrative.
values_or_range: Yellow Oct 2019: 7.9% of trips, 22.2% of driver revenue (fare + extras + tips); JFK pickup mean $51.19 over 15.3 mi, LGA $37.81 over 9.1 mi. HVFHV Jun 2021: 5.4% of trips touch an airport
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019 and HVFHV Jun 2021
how_to_model: Airport zones with their own demand profile tied to flight schedules (R03/R12)

name: Airport pickup/drop-off asymmetry
description: For yellow cabs airport pickups far exceed drop-offs, while app trips are roughly balanced.
values_or_range: Yellow PU/DO: JFK 3.81, LGA 2.06 (Oct 2019); HVFHV: JFK 0.84, LGA 0.88 (Jun 2021)
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
how_to_model: Emerges from the OD matrix; decides whether an airport drop-off can be followed by an airport pickup

name: Airport terminal layout and pickup rules
description: Where at the airport pickups are allowed (terminal curbs, FHV zones, remote lots), adding minutes and confusion.
values_or_range: JFK: FHV pickups barred at Terminals 5 and 7 'until further notice' [uncertain: from 2021-era driver guides; may be outdated], with Howard Beach FHV Hold Lot 3; arrivals-level pickups only; JFK rebuilding (New Terminal One) changes roads [U]
impact_evidence: [S] Uber JFK driver page (French version); Inshur driver guide (2021)
applies_to: all; robotaxi airport access needs Port Authority approval [U]
data_source: PANYNJ ground transport pages; Uber airport driver pages
how_to_model: Airport sub-graph with pickup nodes per terminal and extra walk/drive time

name: Newark Airport (EWR) special status
description: EWR is in New Jersey: NYC drivers drop off there but almost never pick up, so each EWR drop-off implies an empty return. [corrected by fact-check: for taxis the passenger pays a $20 Newark surcharge and tolls both ways (35 RCNY 58-26(c)(3)), so the return toll is reimbursed; app drivers are paid the out-of-town rate]
values_or_range: Yellow: 15,829 drop-offs vs 57 pickups (Oct 2019; 829 pickups under a lighter filter, mostly zero-distance records), rate code 3 = 0.24% of trips; HVFHV: 63,278 vs 228 (Jun 2021); return toll $14.79-16.79 E-ZPass; a taxi may refuse an EWR trip after 8 h of operation
impact_evidence: [P] Own counts (reproduced); [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c)(3), 80-20(b)(8); [S] PANYNJ 2026 tolls
how_to_model: EWR zone = drop-off only for NYC-licensed cars; forced deadhead; inbound toll paid by the driver for app cars and reimbursed by the passenger for taxis

name: Cruise-ship terminal days
description: On ship days, thousands of passengers with luggage leave the Manhattan (Piers 88-90) and Brooklyn (Red Hook) cruise terminals in a morning wave, with a high airport share. Generalises to any cruise port (Miami, Seattle) through a ship-call calendar.
values_or_range: 2024: about 1.5M passengers and 238 ship calls across both terminals. Manhattan had 159 calls (down from 183 in 2023) and about 1M passengers, which leaves about 79 calls for Brooklyn. Manhattan can berth two ships of up to about 4,000 passengers at once. About 2-6k passengers disembark per ship, mostly 07:00-11:00 [U]. Red Hook (zone 195), yellow pickups 07-11h: median 51 on 53 'ship-like' days (>= 30 pickups, Jan 2023-Jan 2024) vs 1 on other days. Ship-like days are mostly in Jul-Dec (6-9 a month) and mostly on Saturdays and Sundays. The threshold catches only part of the calls. The Manhattan terminal sits in Clinton West (zone 50), where other demand hides the signal (07-11h median 170 pickups, no visible ship pattern).
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on TLC yellow Jan 2023-Jan 2024 pickups by zone-hour (g1/a3.py, a5.py), re-run in this fact-check. [corrected: 'peak Jul-Oct' -> spread over Jul-Dec, mostly weekends]. [S] NYCEDC Cruise NYC page, Crain's (2024 record year) and an EDC Community Board 4 deck (Jan 2026) for passenger, call and berth counts. Impact is medium on ship-day mornings for a car near a terminal, and low citywide.
applies_to: all (taxi stand at the terminals, app pickups, robotaxi if in ODD); fleet pre-positioning
data_source: NYCEDC Cruise NYC https://edc.nyc/project/cruise-nyc ; WorldShipNY arrivals table https://worldshipny.com [U] ; CruiseMapper port schedule https://www.cruisemapper.com/ports/new-york-port-98 [U] ; TLC trip records (zones 50 and 195)
how_to_model: One event object per ship call (terminal, ship capacity, arrival time). Each creates a disembarkation pulse 07:00-11:00 with an airport-heavy destination mix and a high XL share [design]. Pulse size is fitted from zone-195 morning residuals.

name: Ferry terminals and heliports
description: Staten Island Ferry terminals, NYC Ferry and NY Waterway landings, and Manhattan heliports produce small, timed pulses of pickup demand.
values_or_range: The Staten Island Ferry runs 24/7, every 15-20 min at rush hours and at least every 30 min at other times (2015 city policy; cut to hourly during COVID, later restored to half-hourly) [S; corrected by fact-check, was 'every 15-60 min [U]']. NYC Ferry hourly boardings by landing are public [S]. Heliports: Downtown Manhattan (Pier 6), E 34th St, W 30th St [U]. Each arrival yields from a few to tens of pickups [design].
impact_evidence: [S] The NYC Ferry Ridership dataset (t5n6-gx8c) gives hourly boardings by date, route, direction and landing. [S] Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts (6eng-46dm) give daily riders at Whitehall and St. George. Whitehall late at night is a known taxi spot [U].
applies_to: all (taxi via hails and the stand at Whitehall)
data_source: NYC Ferry Ridership, NYC Open Data t5n6-gx8c https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/t5n6-gx8c; Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts, NYC Open Data 6eng-46dm (daily; trip-level counts only in an NYC DOT folder) [S, corrected: was 'none found']; NYC Ferry and Staten Island Ferry GTFS [U]
how_to_model: Treat ferry landings and heliports as timed trip generators like rail hubs (R01-049): arrivals x riders per boat x car share, released 2-8 min after docking. Split Staten Island Ferry daily counts over boats with the schedule.

sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
name: Out-of-city trip share
description: Share of trips ending outside NYC (NJ, Westchester, Nassau, Long Island, Connecticut).
values_or_range: HVFHV Jun 2021: 3.67% end outside NYC (zone 265) + 0.42% at EWR. Yellow Oct 2019: rate code 4 (Nassau/Westchester) 0.08%, negotiated (code 5) 0.17%, Newark (code 3) 0.24%
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
how_to_model: OD matrix includes external destination nodes by county

sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
name: Out-of-city fare and pay rules
description: How trips leaving the city are priced and paid, which decides whether the empty return is compensated (amounts owned by R07).
values_or_range: Yellow: meter to the city line, then double meter beyond for Westchester/Nassau, plus tolls both ways; other places negotiated flat fare. HVFHV minimum pay from 1 Mar 2026: in-city $1.283/mi + $0.681/min (non-WAV); out-of-town $1.757/mi (non-WAV), $2.193/mi (WAV), $0.725/min [uncertain: 2026 posted values not re-checked; they match the rule's base rates after yearly CPI indexing]
impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c)(1)-(2), (f)(2): double meter and tolls both ways confirmed; 35 RCNY 59D-22(a): out-of-town base rates ($1.700/mi, WAV $2.122, $0.574/min) are double the in-city base and are not divided by the utilisation rate; [S] TLC driver-pay-rates page
applies_to: human app driver, taxi; robotaxi pricing is a setting
how_to_model: Fare-engine branch when the destination is outside the NYC polygon

sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
name: Empty-return distance and legality
description: After an out-of-city drop-off the driver normally returns to NYC empty, because pickups outside the city need a local licence.
values_or_range: Return 10-60+ km; street hails outside NYC not allowed; app pickups outside NYC depend on NJ / county licensing [U]; taxi passengers reimburse tolls both ways for EWR, Westchester and Nassau; taxis may refuse those trips after 8 h of operation
impact_evidence: [P] Near-zero pickups at EWR and zone 265 in TLC records; [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c), 80-20(b)(8); [U] county licensing details [corrected by fact-check: impact high -> medium; such trips are ~0.5% of yellow and ~4% of app trips and are partly compensated, though a single one can cost up to an hour]
how_to_model: Compute deadhead route back to the city line or home; charge time, energy and inbound toll

sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
name: Night outward drift
description: At night more trips leave the core for residential outer boroughs, leaving drivers far from demand.
values_or_range: Share of core yellow pickups ending in outer boroughs: 1.4% at 8am, 9.5% at 10pm, 13.1% at midnight, 17.7% at 4am (Oct 2019)
impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019
how_to_model: Emerges from hour-specific OD matrices; makes 'go home after last trip' and repositioning decisions matter

sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
name: Network extent and off-map trips
description: How far the road graph and travel-time model reach beyond the five boroughs, and how trips that end off the map are timed, located and returned.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: 3.92% of trips end 'Outside of NYC' (zone 265; mean 16.6 mi and 34.4 min) and carry 10.4% of base fare; 0.63% end at EWR (17.2 mi, 39.1 min, 1.8% of fare) [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check]. Pickups from zone 265 are about 0.005% [P]. Zone 265 has no location, so the end point must be imputed from trip_miles and direction [design].
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file: about 4.6% of trips and about 12% of base fare end off the NYC map. A fixed-time or instant-return shortcut misprices exactly these long trips; R01-057 gives only the share.
applies_to: all (taxi out-of-city rate codes; robotaxi only if the ODD allows)
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (zone 265, trip_miles, trip_time); OpenStreetMap roads for NJ, Westchester, Nassau and Suffolk; NJDOT/NYSDOT speed data [U]
how_to_model: Extend the road graph to a buffer of about 50 km around NYC, impute the off-map drop-off point by matching trip_miles to county centroids, and route the empty return (R01-059).

sub_box: Clock, tick and the episode day
name: Simulation clock and hour-of-week key
description: The local wall-clock time (America/New_York) that every other profile is looked up by, stored as date, minute and a 168-slot hour-of-week index.
values_or_range: 1-minute resolution; 168 hour-of-week slots; 365/366 calendar days; time zone UTC-5/UTC-4
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023: same-city demand ranges 4,892 to 48,069 trips/hour depending only on hour and weekday

sub_box: Clock, tick and the episode day
name: Simulation tick granularity
description: The length of one simulation step, which limits how precisely the agent can time pulses like let-outs.
values_or_range: 1 min recommended; 5 or 15 min coarser; pulses last 15-30 min [corrected by fact-check: in zone 230 let-out pickups stay raised for about 45-60 min at 15-min resolution, peaking about 30 min after onset]

sub_box: Clock, tick and the episode day

description: Where one simulated day ends and the next begins; cutting at midnight splits Saturday night.
values_or_range: Boundary at 04:00-05:00 (demand trough) recommended vs 00:00
impact_evidence: [design]; HVFHV trough at 03-05h while Sun 00-01h still carries 41k and 33k trips/h of Saturday night [P*]
how_to_model: Day runs 05:00 to 04:59 next day; multi-day episodes chain days

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Weekday hourly demand curve
description: The number of ride requests per hour on an ordinary Monday-Friday, shaped by commuting and evening activity.
values_or_range: HVFHV citywide trips/hour: 03h 4,892; 08h 36,283; 12h 23,630; 18h 37,694; 23h 25,607 (peak/trough 7.7x). Yellow: 03h 274 vs 18h 7,534 (27x)
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] own calc yellow Jan 2023
how_to_model: Non-homogeneous Poisson arrivals per zone with rate = base(zone) x hour-of-week profile x day-type x month

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Weekend hourly demand curve
description: The hourly shape on Saturday and Sunday, with late mornings, strong evenings and Friday/Saturday nights running into the next morning.
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
how_to_model: Separate Sat and Sun profiles; the 00-04h of Sat/Sun belong to the previous evening

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Morning rush
description: The 7-10 am commuter peak, with short Manhattan-bound trips, slow traffic and the longest rider waits of a weekday.
values_or_range: HVFHV 08h 36.3k trips/h; median request-to-pickup 5.0 min at 07h (vs 3.3 at 10h); 14 mph
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Lunch hour (rider demand)
description: Midday trips around the average lunch time; small in ride-hail because most lunch trips are walked.
values_or_range: Midtown+FiDi weekday pickups per 15 min: 590-613 at 10:00-10:45, 681-696 at 11:30-12:00 (about +12%), dip 12:30-12:45 [corrected by fact-check: 571-613 at 10:00-10:45; pickups recover to 664-700 at 13:00-13:45, so most of the +12% is the late-morning ramp and the lunch-specific bump is under 5%]; lunch typically 12:00-13:00, 30-60 min [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; ATUS eating-time pattern not verified this session [U]
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; BLS American Time Use Survey, https://www.bls.gov/tus/
how_to_model: Small Gaussian bump centred 11:45 on business-zone pickups; slower midday speeds come from R10

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Evening rush
description: The 4-8 pm peak when offices empty, the highest weekday volume but the slowest traffic and lowest pay per engaged hour.
values_or_range: HVFHV 17-18h 35-38k trips/h; 12.3 mph; $49.7-49.9 per engaged hour; yellow adds $2.50 surcharge [corrected by fact-check: 12.3 mph is 17h only (18h 13.3 mph); $49.7-49.9 is 16-17h, 18h pays $52.4]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] surcharge visible in yellow 'extra' field
how_to_model: Profile peak plus outbound OD bias; couples with R10 speed curve

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Bar-closing taper
description: The end-of-night exit when bars close (4 am in NYC; 2 am in many US cities), which in NYC tapers smoothly rather than spiking.
values_or_range: NYC nightlife pickups fall steadily from 1,700/15 min at 01:00 to 590 at 04:00 and 222 at 05:00 (Sat); no spike at 04:00. Close time 04:00 NYC; 02:00 elsewhere [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-computed: 1,699 at 01:00, 992 at 03:00, 591 at 04:00, 222 at 05:00); NY on-premises closing 4 am [U] [uncertain: NY Alcoholic Beverage Control Law hours not read this session] [corrected by fact-check: was medium; in NYC the taper is already inside the late-night curve (R02-012) and has no closing spike, as the dossier summary itself says; medium only for a 2 am city]
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; NY State Liquor Authority hours rules
how_to_model: Exponential decay after 01:00 in nightlife zones; for 2 am cities add a closing pulse

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)

impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)

sub_box: Hourly demand curve (rush, lunch, dinner, nightlife, dead hours)
name: Minute-of-hour request pulses
description: Ride requests bunch slightly at round clock times (on the hour, the half hour, and 10 or 40 past) as meetings, classes and shows end on the clock.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, non-holiday weekdays, requests 07-20h. Midtown/Penn zones (100, 161-164, 186, 230), on-demand requests (wait <= 15 min): minute :10 is 1.15x the mean, :40 1.14x, :30 1.10x, :00 1.09x, :55 1.08x; trough 0.93-0.94x at :19-:23. Citywide (8.4M requests): peaks are 1.06-1.12x (at :40, :10, :45, :15, :30 and :00), and 5-minute block averages stay within about +/-3% (0.98-1.03). Airports peak at :55-:59 (1.04-1.06x). Pickup minutes are almost flat (+/-6%).
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV Jan 2023 request_datetime (g1/a1.py, a2.py), re-run in this fact-check, with 5-minute blocks added. [corrected: pickup minutes +/-6%, not +/-5%]. Median waits are slightly shorter at the peak minutes (3.35-3.43 vs 3.65 min), so the peaks are not just scheduled reservations.
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime to the second)
how_to_model: Optional periodic term on each zone's arrival rate (minute weights per zone class). It matters only with 1-minute ticks (R02-067).

name: DST transition days
description: Clocks jump forward in March (23-h day) and back in November (25-h day), shifting late-night demand in clock time.
values_or_range: Spring 2023: no 02h; 03h yellow trips 4,267 vs ~2,300 normal (1.8x); Fall: 01h 8,435 (two hours) vs 5,400-6,000; 02h 2,217 vs 4,000-5,300

how_to_model: Run the clock in UTC, convert to local for profiles; nightlife demand follows body time across the switch

name: Meal breaks: timing and duration
description: When the driver eats and for how long.
values_or_range: 1-2 meals per 10-12 h shift, 15-45 min each; general-population peaks 12:00-13:00 and 18:00-19:00; drivers often move meals off demand peaks.
impact_evidence: [S] USDA ERS ATUS module 2006-08: over 35% of Americans eat as a main activity at noon-1 pm and 6-7 pm [uncertain: share not re-checkable; the peaks themselves are well established (U)]; ATUS 2024: 74 min/day eating and drinking [uncertain: recent ATUS values are about 1.1-1.25 h (66-75 min) a day (U)]; a Wuhan study detects cab drivers' meal stops from GPS.
applies_to: human app driver, taxi, fleet (per driver)
data_source: BLS ATUS https://www.bls.gov/tus/ ; ERS Eating and Health Module https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/eating-and-health-module-atus/
how_to_model: Hunger timer; after 5-6 h without a meal apply a rising fatigue or discomfort penalty; a meal action takes 15-45 min in a zone with food.

name: Prayer and religious observance
description: Prayer stops, Friday midday prayers and Ramadan fasting that some drivers observe.
values_or_range: 5 daily prayers of about 10-15 min at sun-based times; Friday Jumu'ah about 45-60 min at midday; Ramadan iftar stop of 30-60 min at sunset.
impact_evidence: [S] In The Fray: roughly half of NYC's taxi drivers are Muslim (anecdotal); Religion News Service 2023: drivers combine prayers when they cannot park; CNN: drivers give up '$30 or $40' in the iftar hour.
data_source: Astronomical prayer-time calculation [U]; Islamic calendar for Ramadan dates [U]
how_to_model: Optional persona schedule of fixed-time breaks that need a parking spot or mosque zone; a Friday midday block.

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Day-type classification
description: The category a calendar date falls into, which selects the demand, speed and rule profile for that day.
values_or_range: Mon, Tue-Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, federal holiday, bridge day, major-event day, DST day
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023: holidays run at 0.45-0.90 of a normal same-weekday, bridge days 0.56-0.79
data_source: US federal holiday list (OPM), https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/ ; NYC DOE calendar
how_to_model: Lookup table date -> day_type; profiles fitted per day_type from TLC history

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Day-of-week demand level
description: Total demand differs by weekday, and differently for taxis and app rides.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023 per day: Sat 724k, Fri 662k, Sun 627k, Thu 609k, Wed 563k, Tue 528k, Mon 516k. Yellow 2023: Thu 121k, Wed 117k, Fri 114k, Sat 112k, Tue 111k, Mon 98k, Sun 95k
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
how_to_model: Day-of-week multiplier on base demand per sector

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Hybrid-work office days
description: Office attendance concentrates on Tuesday-Thursday, raising morning business demand on those days.
values_or_range: Yellow 7-10 am trips/day: Tue 14.9k, Wed 15.2k, Thu 15.3k vs Mon 13.4k and Fri 12.3k (-12% and -19% vs Thu); office occupancy ~55% midweek vs ~32% Fri [S] [uncertain: Kastle figure not re-read; whether it is NYC or the 10-city average, and for which year, is not stated]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023; Kastle Back to Work Barometer via repo note D02 [S]
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; Kastle Back to Work Barometer, https://www.kastle.com/safety-wellness/getting-america-back-to-work/
how_to_model: Weekday x business-zone multiplier on AM and PM commute layers

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Thursday-Saturday nights
description: Leisure nights start on Thursday and peak on Friday and Saturday [corrected by fact-check: true for app rides; for yellow taxis Thursday 21-24h (20.0k) is the busiest night, ahead of Friday and Saturday].
values_or_range: Yellow 21-24h per day: Thu 20.0k, Fri 19.0k, Sat 18.7k vs Mon 12.4k; HVFHV 21-24h: Sat 133k, Fri 120k, Thu 93k, Mon 64k
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023; [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
how_to_model: Night layer multipliers by weekday and zone

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Sunday pattern
description: Sunday mornings are the quietest daytime of the week and Sunday evenings bring airport returns.
values_or_range: Yellow 7-10 am Sun 6.2k vs ~15k weekdays; HVFHV airport pickup share 6.2-7.6% at Sun 21-23h vs mostly 1-5% at other times [corrected by fact-check: weekday 23-01h shares are similar (5.5-8.2%); the Sunday-evening signal is in volume, about 1,770-1,790 airport pickups/h at Sun 21-23h vs 1,170-1,460/h at weekday 21h-00h]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
how_to_model: Sunday profile plus airport-arrival layer weighted to Sunday evening

sub_box: Day type and day of week
name: Summer Fridays and getaway afternoons
description: Friday afternoons empty out in summer and before long weekends as people leave the city early.
values_or_range: Yellow Fri/Thu ratio 13-17h: Jul 0.91, Aug 0.87 vs 0.95-1.03 other months; Mon before July 4 at 0.69 of normal [corrected by fact-check: September 2023 computes to 0.90, an artefact of the 21-24 Sep 2023 data gap (R02-065)]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
how_to_model: Seasonal Friday-afternoon multiplier; outbound airport/Penn Station OD boost

name: Monthly seasonal demand index
description: How average daily demand varies by month.
values_or_range: HVFHV +/-7%: Jul-Aug 0.93-0.97, Dec 1.04-1.07. Yellow +/-15%: Jan 0.84-0.94, Aug 0.85-0.87, May 1.07-1.11, Oct 1.07-1.10 (2023-2025) [corrected by fact-check: values re-computed and confirmed, but yellow Sep 2023 reads 0.90 only because the TLC file lacks about 95% of trips from midday 21 Sep to 24 Sep 2023; Sep is 1.06-1.08 in 2024-25]
impact_evidence: [P*] TLC monthly row counts via SHA-256 catalog of CloudFront files (own calc)
how_to_model: Month multiplier per sector applied to base rates

name: Tourist season
description: Visitor numbers peak in summer and the December holidays and are lowest in January-February, shifting demand toward hotels, attractions and airports.
values_or_range: Low season Jan-Feb; peaks Jun-Aug and late Nov-Dec [U] [uncertain: no visitor statistics read]; yellow monthly index tracks business more than tourism
impact_evidence: [U] NYC Tourism + Conventions visitor statistics not read this session
data_source: NYC Tourism + Conventions, https://www.nyctourism.com/ ; Broadway League weekly grosses, https://www.broadwayleague.com/
how_to_model: Month multiplier on hotel/attraction zones and airport OD

name: Holiday shopping season
description: Late November to December brings shoppers, office parties and slow traffic in Midtown.
values_or_range: Weekday 00h yellow trips Dec 2,554/h (similar to Jun 2,537) vs Jan 1,671/h; Dec 17h speed 9.3 mph (slowest month); Fri before Christmas 0.84 of normal
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
how_to_model: Seasonal layer Black Friday-Dec 23 on Midtown retail zones and late-night parties

name: Summer recreation destinations
description: Warm-weather trips to beaches and parks (Rockaway, Coney Island, Orchard Beach) and out-of-town getaways pull cars to dead-end peninsulas where return trips are scarce. The zones are NYC-specific; any coastal city has an equivalent.
values_or_range: Yellow 2023 drop-offs into the Rockaway zones (27, 86, 117, 201): about 49/day in Jun-Aug vs 36/day in January (+35%). October also reaches 46/day, so part of the rise is a broad Apr-Oct season rather than beach days. Coney Island (55): 21/day in Jul-Aug vs 14 in January (+50%). Summer yellow pickups per drop-off: only 0.24 in Rockaway and 0.32 in Coney Island. The effect is likely concentrated on hot, dry weekends [U].
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on TLC yellow 2023 drop-offs by zone and month, re-run in this fact-check. September is depressed by the 21-24 Sep 2023 data gap (R02-065). Volumes are small (tens of yellow trips a day). App trips, which dominate outer-borough demand, are not measured.
applies_to: all; single car (stranding risk), fleet (rebalancing out)
data_source: NYC TLC trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page ; NOAA hourly weather; NYC Parks beach attendance (no machine-readable source found)
how_to_model: Season x temperature x weekend multiplier on drop-offs to beach zones. The low pickup rate there feeds destination re-dispatch value (R05-058).

name: Federal and civic holiday multiplier
description: Demand and speed on legal holidays compared with a normal same weekday.
values_or_range: Yellow 2023: Christmas 0.45, Thanksgiving 0.50, July 4 0.54, Memorial Day 0.73, NYD observed 0.77, Presidents 0.86, Columbus 0.86, Labor 0.87, Juneteenth 0.85, MLK 0.89; speeds +20-45% [corrected by fact-check: +14-45%; Presidents', Columbus and Juneteenth run +14-23%]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; OPM federal holiday list
how_to_model: Holiday day-type with its own hourly profile and speed multiplier

name: Bridge and holiday-adjacent days
description: Days next to holidays behave like partial holidays, with heavy airport flows before and after.
values_or_range: Black Friday 0.61; Wed before Thanksgiving 0.74; Sun after Thanksgiving 0.79; Christmas Eve 0.61; Dec 26 0.56; Dec 29 0.65; Christmas-New Year week AM trips -56%, speed +50%
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
how_to_model: Bridge day-type; airport OD boost on getaway and return days

name: Religious and cultural holidays
description: Observances that barely move citywide demand but shift it strongly in particular neighbourhoods and driver groups.
values_or_range: Citywide yellow ratio: Yom Kippur 0.92, Eid al-Fitr 0.95, Easter 0.90, Lunar New Year 1.01, Diwali 1.02; local effects (Flushing, Chinatown, Borough Park) not measured
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023; neighbourhood effects [U]
data_source: NYC TLC yellow taxi trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; interfaith calendars
how_to_model: Zone-level multipliers on dated observances (neighbourhood x holiday table)

name: Weekly Sabbath in observant neighbourhoods
description: Orthodox Jewish areas see almost no rides from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall.
values_or_range: Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall (~25 h); zones such as Borough Park, Williamsburg South [U] [uncertain: zone-level effect not measured]
impact_evidence: [U] not measured this session
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; sunset times
how_to_model: Zone multiplier near 0 within the sun-defined window

name: Party and dining nights
description: Non-federal dates with outsized bar and restaurant demand reshape the evening and late-night peaks: Halloween, Thanksgiving Eve, Valentine's Day, St Patrick's Day, Mother's Day and Super Bowl Sunday. The dates are US-specific; the method generalises.
values_or_range: Yellow 2023 pickups vs the median of the same weekday +/-4 weeks, excluding holidays and event days. Halloween (Tue): 17-22h 0.73-0.89 (23h 0.95); 00-03h next day 1.97. Thanksgiving Eve: 18-23h 0.56-0.57; 00-03h 1.40. Valentine's (Tue): 18-21h 1.10; 22-23h 1.21; 00-03h 1.39. St Patrick's (Fri): 12-17h 0.90; 00-03h 1.22. Mother's Day: 12-23h 1.12-1.19; 00-03h 0.86. Super Bowl Sunday (12 Feb 2023): 17-18h 1.13-1.24; 19-20h (game) 0.79-0.83; 22h 1.85; 23h 1.49. Cinco de Mayo: at most 1.16. SantaCon is in R03-035.
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on TLC yellow 2023 hourly pickups (g1/a4.py, a5.py), re-run in this fact-check. [corrected: Halloween 0.73-0.89 is 17-22h, not 18-23h]. Each ratio rests on one date, so expect a few percent of noise [design]. App (HVFHV) effects are not measured, since only Jan 2023 HVFHV is available locally.
data_source: NYC TLC yellow and HVFHV trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page ; NFL schedule (Super Bowl kickoff)
how_to_model: Date x hour multiplier table added to the day-type calendar (R02-002), tilted toward nightlife zones (R01-044). For Halloween, combine with the Village parade closure (R03-030).

name: Public school calendar
description: School terms and recesses change morning traffic and some family trips.
values_or_range: Recess weeks: yellow 7-10 am trips -3 to -14% [corrected by fact-check: the dossier's own §2.5 weeks give -3% (April) and -12% (February)], AM speed +7-11% (about 12.2 to 13.4 mph; Feb week includes Presidents' Day); school start Sept 2023: AM speed 13.6 to 10.9 mph (-20%), AM trips +39% vs late Aug [uncertain: the September jump also reflects offices returning after summer and Labor Day, not only schools]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023; DOE recess dates [U]
data_source: NYC DOE school year calendar, https://www.schools.nyc.gov/calendar
how_to_model: School-in-session flag modifies AM speeds and family demand

name: University terms
description: College move-in, term time, finals and commencement shift demand near campuses and luggage trips.
values_or_range: Move-in late Aug, commencement May, winter break mid-Dec to late Jan [U] [uncertain: academic calendars not read]
impact_evidence: [U] not measured
how_to_model: Campus-zone multipliers on dated windows

name: Hospital and healthcare shift changes
description: Large hospitals change shifts at fixed times, creating small pulses of staff trips.
values_or_range: Typical 12-h shifts 07:00/19:00, 8-h shifts 07/15/23h [U] [uncertain: no NYC hospital schedule read]
impact_evidence: [U] not measured
data_source: none found (hospital locations from NYC Open Data facilities)
how_to_model: Small pickups pulse at hospital zones at shift ends

name: Paydays and month-end
description: Spending may rise just after common paydays (1st, 15th, Fridays), lifting discretionary rides.
values_or_range: Possible small uplift on 1st/15th and Fridays [U]; not tested [uncertain: no evidence found either way]
impact_evidence: [U] no ride-hail evidence found
how_to_model: Optional day-of-month multiplier (default 1.0)

name: Taxi refuelling before shift handover
description: Yellow-cab drivers on driver-pays leases customarily hand the cab back with a full tank, so gas stations near the Queens garages queue up in the late afternoon.
values_or_range: Refuel stop of 10-25 min including the queue, between 15:30 and 17:00 [design]. If the owner supplies gasoline under the optional gas-surcharge lease ($13-31 per shift, set by the EIA New York City gasoline price index), the driver pays no fuel and does not refuel before handover (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(6)) [P*, added by fact-check]. Hybrids need about one fill per 1-2 shifts (R08-012) [design]. It deepens the 4-5 pm taxi supply dip (R02-044, R06-018).
impact_evidence: [U] full-tank custom, which is not in 35 RCNY 58-21; that rule only provides the optional owner-supplied gas surcharge [P*, re-read]. [S] A 2011 TLC count found cabs on the road fell from 6,688 to 5,452 between 4 and 5 pm (via R02-044).
applies_to: taxi (day-shift lease drivers); competitor taxi bots
data_source: 35 RCNY 58-21 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; OpenStreetMap amenity=fuel near garage zones; none found for queue times
how_to_model: A lease-type flag: gas-included (no refuelling) or driver-pays (must refuel before handover when the tank is below a threshold). Competitor taxi bots on driver-pays leases leave service 20-40 min earlier.

name: Airport arrival banks
description: Flights land in banks, so airport pickup demand rises and falls by hour differently at JFK, LGA and EWR.
values_or_range: HVFHV weekday JFK pickups/h: 60 at 04h, 409-428 at 06-07h, 593-682 at 14-17h, 747-799 at 21-23h; LGA ~0 at 02-06h, 500-760 at 09-24h [corrected by fact-check: LGA 11-28/h at 02-06h and 502-764/h at 09-24h]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [U] scheduled-arrival data not read
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; BTS on-time performance (scheduled arrivals), https://www.transtats.bts.gov/
how_to_model: Airport pickup arrivals driven by scheduled arrivals per hour x passengers x ground-transport share

name: Airport departure banks
description: Early-morning departure banks create long, high-fare trips to the airports before dawn.
values_or_range: Weekday drop-offs/h: JFK 1,137 and LGA 958 at 05h; LGA drop-offs end ~21h (37/h); 23.8-28.6% of all 04-05h trips go to airports
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; BTS scheduled departures
how_to_model: Airport-bound OD weight by hour from scheduled departures minus 1.5-3 h

name: Transit service schedule
description: Subway headways, last commuter trains and overnight service gaps shift demand to cars at night.
values_or_range: Overnight subway headways ~20 min [U]; last LIRR/Metro-North/PATH trains ~00:30-01:30 [U] [corrected by fact-check: PATH and the LIRR run all night with long gaps, so they have no last train; only Metro-North has a true overnight gap (last Grand Central departures roughly 01:00-02:00) [U]] [uncertain: MTA GTFS not read]; 2020-21 overnight subway closure 01-05h [U]
impact_evidence: [U] MTA GTFS not read this session
data_source: MTA GTFS feeds, https://new.mta.info/developers ; MTA ridership on NYC Open Data
how_to_model: Mode-choice term: car demand rises when transit wait or gap is long at that hour

name: Annual fixed-date civic events
description: Recurring yearly events with known dates and road closures (Macy's parade, Marathon, Pride, UNGA week, NYE ball drop, Fashion Week).
values_or_range: Pride Sunday 2023 yellow 1.11x; Marathon Sunday 1.03x (25-h DST day); UNGA Tuesday 0.94x with 10.9 vs 11.6 mph
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023; event sizes cross-link R03
data_source: NYC permitted event information (NYC Open Data); NYC DOT closure notices
how_to_model: Calendar of dated closures and demand pulses passed to R03 events engine

name: Event catalogue for the scenario day
description: The list of planned events active on the simulated day, each with type, venue, start, end, attendance and closure footprint.
values_or_range: Typical NYC evening: ~30-40 Broadway shows, 0-3 arena or stadium events, 0-2 conventions, dozens of permitted street events on weekends; peak days (NYE, Marathon, UNGA) add a citywide event [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, 2023 yellow trips: event days move venue-zone pickups from 0x normal (Times Sq after 17:00 on NYE) to 15x normal (Flushing Meadows during the US Open)
data_source: NYC Permitted Event Information (NYC Open Data tvpp-9vvx, next month only) and NYC Permitted Event Information - Historical (bkfu-528j, approved events from 2008) for replay dates [corrected by fact-check: tvpp-9vvx lists only approved events 'within the next month', so past scenario days need bkfu-528j; IDs and descriptions read from verbatim copies of the Socrata metadata, P*]; plus venue and league schedules (see R03-061)
how_to_model: Load event objects per scenario date; each adds arrival and let-out demand, closures and speed effects through the variables below

name: Venue registry and zone mapping
description: Fixed table of venues with location, taxi zone, capacity, pickup and drop-off nodes and taxi stands.
values_or_range: MSG/Penn zone 186 (~19-21k); Yankee Stadium zone 247 (46.5k); Citi Field and USTA tennis centre zone 93 (~42k; Ashe ~24k); Javits zone 246; Broadway zone 230 (~40 theatres); Randalls Island zone 194; Barclays zone 181 (Park Slope), at the corner with 189 (Prospect Heights) and 97 (Fort Greene) [corrected by fact-check: originally 'zone 25 or 189 (verify)'; point-in-polygon test on a GitHub copy of the TLC zone GeoJSON, S]; outside NYC: MetLife, UBS Arena, Prudential Center (zone 265). Capacities [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: Yankee night games lift zone-247 drop-offs 16-20h 4.7x (34.1 vs 7.2 per day) [corrected by fact-check: originally 4.5x (31.9 vs 7.1); the Sep 21-24 data-gap days are now excluded]; Mets and US Open lift zone 93, confirming the zone mapping
data_source: TLC taxi zone shapefile (NYC Open Data 755u-8jsi); OpenStreetMap venue polygons
how_to_model: Geocode each venue to a road node and taxi zone; attach capacity, pickup lot node and taxi stand

name: Broadway curtain and let-out pattern
description: Weekly theatre schedule that creates evening and matinee let-out waves around Times Square.
values_or_range: Tue 7pm curtain (let-out ~21:30); Wed and Thu a mix of 7pm and 8pm curtains; Fri-Sat 8pm (let-out ~22:30-22:45); matinees Wed and Sat 2pm (let-out ~16:30), Sun mostly 3pm (let-out ~17:30); most theatres dark on Monday [corrected by fact-check: originally 'Wed-Sat 8pm' and 'Sun 2pm'; own 2023 zone-230 15-min counts show a 21:30 peak on Thursdays (84 vs 57 on Mondays) as on Tuesdays, both 21:30 and 22:30-22:45 peaks on Wednesdays, and a Sunday bump at 17:30 (63 vs 47 at 17:15), P*; evening curtains 'typically 7pm or 8pm', S]; ~12M admissions a season [uncertain: about 12.3M in 2022-23 and 2023-24 from memory, and 2024-25 reportedly a record of about 14.7M; not re-checkable this session]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, zone 230 yellow pickups 22:00-23:00 in 2023: Mon 177/day vs Tue 270, Wed 331, Fri 298, Sat 285, Sun 129; Tuesday peak moves to 21:30 (88 vs 57 per 15 min on Mondays)
data_source: Broadway League weekly grosses and attendance (broadwayleague.com); show schedules (Playbill, IBDB) [U]
how_to_model: Recurring weekly event set per theatre with a let-out distribution; scale by the week's reported attendance

name: Pro sports home schedules
description: Home games of New York teams, which create arrival and let-out waves at stadiums and arenas, including playoff games whose dates are uncertain.
values_or_range: MLB Yankees and Mets: 81 home games each (2023: 63% and 69% at night); NBA Knicks and Nets, NHL Rangers ~41 each; Islanders at UBS Arena; NFL Giants and Jets at MetLife (NJ); MLS, WNBA; playoffs add home dates, and games 5-7 of a series are 'if necessary' and confirmed only 1-2 days ahead [corrected by fact-check: '0-11' had no basis; under current formats a team can host up to 14 MLB postseason games (Wild Card 3, Division Series 3, LCS 4, World Series 4) and up to 16 NBA or NHL playoff games, U]
impact_evidence: [P*] Retrosheet 2023 game logs + own calc: yellow drop-offs near Yankee Stadium 8.4 per 10k attendees on night games (Mets 4.9); corr(attendance, drop-offs) 0.53 for the Yankees [corrected by fact-check: originally 8.1 and 0.52, with two data-gap night games included]
data_source: Retrosheet game logs (github.com/chadwickbureau/retrosheet); MLB Stats API, NBA and NHL schedule feeds [U]
how_to_model: Import per-date games with start time, attendance and duration; generate waves through R03-011 to R03-016

name: Multi-session tournaments (US Open tennis)
description: Two-week events with day and night sessions every day, giving repeated arrival waves and late-night let-outs.
values_or_range: US Open: late Aug to early Sep, 14 days (2023: Aug 28-Sep 10) [uncertain: from 2025 the main draw reportedly starts on a Sunday, giving 15 days; not re-checkable this session]; day session ~11:00, night session ~19:00; night matches often end after midnight [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023: Flushing Meadows (zone 93) yellow pickups 188.7/day vs 12.5 on other days (15x); 21-24h 29x; 0-2h pickups up to 162 a night vs 0.7; these trips average 10.0 mi and a $45 fare
how_to_model: Daily two-session event with a heavy-tailed end time for the night session

name: Conventions and trade shows (Javits)
description: Multi-day exhibitions that add morning arrivals and evening departures at the convention centre, plus hotel and airport trips.
values_or_range: NY Comic Con ~200k over 4 days [U]; Auto Show 10 days; 100+ events a year at Javits [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023 zone 246: Comic Con (Oct 12-15) drop-offs 7-13h 1.97x and pickups 16-21h 1.39x the same weekdays a week before and after; Auto Show (Apr 7-16) pickups 1.22x
how_to_model: Daily open and close times with attendance and a business-traveller price profile

name: Concerts and music festivals
description: One-off or multi-day concerts and festivals at arenas, parks and islands, mostly with young, transit-heavy crowds.
values_or_range: Arena shows 15-20k; park festivals 30-60k a day (Governors Ball, Electric Zoo) [U]; stadium shows 50-80k
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023: Electric Zoo (Randalls Island, zone 194) drop-offs 12-22h 45-48 vs 5-8 on normal days; Governors Ball (zone 93) 1.85x; yellow taxis carry only a small share of these crowds
data_source: Ticketmaster Discovery API, SeatGeek API, setlist.fm (history) [U]
how_to_model: Event objects with an audience profile (young, transit-heavy) that gives a low car share

name: New Year's Eve in Times Square
description: The year's biggest single night: an afternoon-to-midnight frozen zone around Times Square, then a citywide after-midnight spike.
values_or_range: Times Sq vehicle access restricted from late morning on Dec 31 until after midnight [corrected by fact-check: originally 'closed to cars from ~16:00-17:00'; own data show zone-230 pickups already 75-86% below a normal Sunday from 12:00 (37-66 vs 238-277 an hour), 10 at 16:00 and zero from 17:00, P*; official closure times U]; citywide demand 1.4-3x normal 00:00-04:00; app prices ~1.8x
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: zone 230 yellow pickups fell to 0 from 17:00 on Dec 31 2023 (normal Sunday ~240/h); Jan 1 2024 0-4h citywide yellow pickups 1.4-3.2x, fare per trip $19.80 vs $15.80; HVFHV Jan 1 2023 1-3h fare per mile 7.97-8.40 vs 4.49-4.58, driver pay $97-101 vs $60-61 per engaged hour, waits 8.3-8.7 vs 4.7-4.9 min [corrected by fact-check: 8.40 vs 4.58 was the 01:00 hour only; re-run on the HVFHV file reproduced the rest]
data_source: TLC trip records; NYPD and NYC DOT closure notices [U]
how_to_model: Scripted closure polygon plus a citywide demand and surge multiplier after 00:00

name: Commencements and move-in days
description: University graduations at large venues and dorm move-in days that add family groups with luggage.
values_or_range: May-June graduations at Yankee Stadium, MSG, Barclays, Radio City; late-August move-in; 1-5 days a year per venue [U] [uncertain: not re-checkable this session; web search budget used up and source hosts blocked]
impact_evidence: [U] recurring venue and university calendars; not measured here
how_to_model: Small daytime events with high XL and luggage share

name: Events outside the city boundary
description: Large events just outside NYC (MetLife, UBS Arena, Prudential Center, Belmont Park [uncertain: the Belmont Stakes was run at Saratoga in 2024 and 2025 while Belmont Park was rebuilt; check the scenario year]) whose trips cross licence borders, so drivers drop off but rarely pick up there.
values_or_range: MetLife 82.5k; UBS Arena ~17k [U]; yellow and green taxis cannot take street hails outside NYC, and Newark airport is drop-off-only for NYC cars (R01); whether NYC-licensed app drivers may accept app requests in NJ or Nassau depends on those jurisdictions' rules [corrected by fact-check: originally 'NYC-licensed app cars generally cannot take street pickups outside the city'; app cars never take street hails, so the limit is on app dispatch, which is uncertain: not re-checkable this session]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: the Taylor Swift MetLife weekend (May 26-28 2023) left yellow drop-offs outside NYC unchanged (ratio 1.00), so taxis capture almost none of it; app share not measured
how_to_model: External event that creates outbound trips and only app-dispatched return trips; charge the empty return

name: Unlisted private events
description: Weddings, proms, quinceaneras, funerals and banquet-hall parties that no public calendar lists but that create local demand spikes, mostly on spring and summer Saturdays.

name: Precipitation state and hourly intensity
description: Whether it is dry, raining or snowing in each hour, and how hard; the master input that drives the demand, speed, risk and robotaxi rules.
values_or_range: dry; trace (<0.01 in/h); light (<0.10 in/h, ~2.5 mm); moderate (0.10-0.30 in/h); heavy (>0.30 in/h); extreme (>1 in/h, Ida 2021 ~3.15 in in one hour [U]). Central Park 2009-2025 per year: 126 days >=0.01 in, 80 >=0.1 in, 56 >=0.25 in, 34.5 >=0.5 in, 13.6 >=1 in, 2.5 >=2 in; mean 50.5 in/yr [P*]
impact_evidence: Brodeur & Nield 2018: Uber rides +25% per rainy hour vs taxi +4% [S] [uncertain: IZA/JEBO hosts unreachable and the search budget was exhausted, so the +25%/+4% figures were not re-read at source]; our TLC Jan 2023: Uber trips +6.3% on wet days (t=2.3), yellow -0.5% [P]
data_source: NOAA NCEI Local Climatological Data (hourly), Central Park USW00094728 https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/local-climatological-data ; GHCN-Daily https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/datasets/GHCND/stations/GHCND:USW00094728/detail ; IEM ASOS https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml
how_to_model: Hourly series per scenario day (replayed from LCD or generated), binned into 5 intensity classes that index the demand, speed, crash and robotaxi tables.

name: Rain demand uplift for app requests
description: Extra ride requests when it rains; completed app trips rise but completed taxi trips do not, because taxi supply is fixed and fully used [uncertain: an inference; TLC files cannot show taxi occupancy or unmet hails].
values_or_range: App ride volume +10-30% per rainy hour [design range anchored on Brodeur & Nield's +25% for Uber] [corrected by fact-check: was 'requests' tagged [S range]; no source gives this range, and Brodeur & Nield count completed rides, not requests]; daily, wet day (>=0.10 in) vs dry, Jan 2023: Uber +6.3% (t=2.3), Lyft +3.9% (t=1.5), yellow -0.5% (n.s.) [P]; heavy rain larger than light [U]
impact_evidence: Brodeur & Nield 2018 IZA DP 9986: Uber +25%/rainy hour vs taxi +4% [S] [uncertain: IZA/JEBO hosts unreachable and the search budget was exhausted, so the +25%/+4% figures were not re-read at source]; our own TLC x NOAA daily regressions with weekday and trend controls [P]
applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi, fleet; taxi (as latent hail demand)
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV and yellow trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page joined to NOAA LCD hourly precipitation
how_to_model: Multiply the zone x hour request rate by m_rain(intensity, hour, day type), fitted by Poisson regression of HVFHV counts on hourly rain with hour-of-week fixed effects.

name: Rain onset surge and decay
description: Demand jumps most in the first hour or two after rain starts, when people are caught out, then fades as trips are postponed or already made.
values_or_range: First-hour peak 1.2-1.6x, decay half-life 1-3 h [design guess]; 29 Sep 2023 flood: yellow trips +46% to +63% from 05:00-09:00, back to about -3% to +5% by 12:00-15:00 vs 4 reference Fridays [P]
impact_evidence: Our TLC hourly event study of 29 Sep 2023 [P]; curve shape is a [design guess]
data_source: TLC trip records + NOAA LCD hourly or IEM 1-minute ASOS for onset times
how_to_model: Multiplier = 1 + a*intensity + b*exp(-(t - onset)/tau); fit a, b, tau by event study on rain onsets.

name: Rain effect by hour, day type and trip purpose
description: The same rain raises demand more at some hours and on some day types (errands, evening, nightlife) and can cut discretionary weekend trips when heavy.
values_or_range: Uber, wet vs dry Tue-Thu, Jan 2023: +2% to +6% at 05:00-09:00, +14% to +25% at 10:00-23:00 [P, not trend-adjusted] [corrected by fact-check: 'wet' here means the 4 Tue-Thu days with >=0.4 in (3, 19, 25 and 26 Jan) against dry Tue-Thu days; hours 00:00-04:00 also show +13% to +27%, so part of the gap is the upward trend within January, not rain]; heavy-rain Sunday 30 Apr 2023: yellow -24% to -29% at 19:00-21:00 [P]
impact_evidence: Our TLC hourly comparisons [P]; R02 notes rain at 6 pm hits a market already short of cars [design]
data_source: TLC trip records + NOAA LCD hourly
how_to_model: Interact the rain multiplier with hour-of-week buckets and trip-purpose shares (commute vs discretionary) from R05.

name: Shift toward short trips in bad weather
description: Rain and cold add short trips that people would otherwise walk, changing the trip-length mix and the number of pickups per hour.
values_or_range: Yellow share of trips under 1 mile: 20.5% on dry days; +0.5 pp light, +1.2 pp moderate, +1.4 pp heavy rain; +2.5 pp on cold days (max <=35°F); Uber +1.1 pp on wet days (base 10%) [P]
impact_evidence: Our 2023 yellow daily regressions, t=2.7 to 6.2; Uber Jan 2023 t=3.7 [P] [corrected by fact-check: impact lowered from medium to low; the shifts are 0.5-2.5 points of the trip mix and the yellow fare per trip did not change significantly (heavy rain +$0.1, t=0.7), so the effect on profit per hour is small]
data_source: TLC trip records (trip_distance, trip_miles) + NOAA GHCN-Daily
how_to_model: Weather-dependent re-weighting of the trip-distance / OD distribution toward intra-zone and adjacent-zone trips.

name: Mode substitution from walking, cycling and transit
description: Bad weather moves trips off walking, Citi Bike, e-bikes and outdoor bus waits onto cars; this is the pool the extra car demand comes from.
