values_or_range: Citi Bike trips drop sharply on rainy days (order of -30% to -60%) [U]; subway ridership dips in storms [U]
impact_evidence: Background knowledge of Citi Bike and MTA ridership on rain days; not computed here [U] [corrected by fact-check: impact lowered from medium to low; this variable is only a calibration check, and its demand effect is already carried by R04-002]
data_source: Citi Bike System Data https://citibikenyc.com/system-data ; MTA Daily Ridership https://data.ny.gov/
how_to_model: Use Citi Bike and subway drops on weather days as a calibration check on the car-demand uplift, not as a separate generator.

name: Street-hail intensity in rain (taxi)
description: How many more people try to hail a yellow cab per mile cruised when it rains, mostly in high-foot-traffic zones.
values_or_range: Hail attempts +20-50% in rain in the Manhattan core [design guess]; completed yellow trips flat on wet days (-0.5%), so the cab is full rather than demand-limited [P]
impact_evidence: Our TLC: yellow completed trips flat while app trips rise [P]; Farber 2015 'Why You Can't Find a Taxi in the Rain' [U for rain result]
data_source: TLC yellow trip records; R01 pedestrian density
how_to_model: Raise the street-hail arrival rate per road segment by weather, scaled by pedestrian density, so the hail-encounter probability per cruising minute rises.

name: Pickup ETA inflation in rain
description: Rain lengthens the time from request to driver arrival; the curb dwell after arrival does not change.
values_or_range: Uber median request-to-on-scene +0.23 min on wet days (base 2.6 min, +9%, t=3.0); 17:00-20:00 wet 2.6-3.1 vs dry 2.0-2.5 min (+22% to +40%) [corrected by fact-check: this evening comparison uses the 4 Tue-Thu days with >=0.4 in against dry Tue-Thu days, without a trend control; only the +9% daily figure uses the >=0.10 in definition with weekday and trend controls]; on-scene-to-pickup dwell 0.79 min, unchanged (t=0.2) [P]
impact_evidence: Our TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 analysis [P]
how_to_model: Emerges from matching (R06) under slowed speeds and tighter supply; use +9% daily and +22% to +40% in the evening as validation targets.

name: Weather-driven cancellations and no-shows
description: Riders cancel when ETAs grow or they find another car; drivers cancel long or flooded pickups.
values_or_range: Cancellation rate +2 to +5 pp in heavy rain [design guess]; public TLC files contain completed trips only
impact_evidence: No public data found [design guess]
data_source: none found (TLC HVFHV has completed trips only)
how_to_model: Rider cancel hazard rising with ETA, scaled up in rain; driver-side cancel exposed as an agent action.

name: Surge response to weather
description: How much app prices and driver pay rise when rain creates a supply shortage; the yellow meter does not change.
values_or_range: Uber daily averages on wet days, Jan 2023: base fare per mile +$0.09 (+2%, t=1.4), driver pay per engaged hour +$0.46 (+0.8%, t=1.8) [P] (weekday controls only, no trend control); hourly peaks much larger [U]; yellow tariff fixed
impact_evidence: Our TLC HVFHV analysis [P]; Brodeur & Nield: surge lets app supply respond to rain [S] [corrected by fact-check: impact lowered from high to medium; the measured daily price and pay responses are only 1-2%, and the larger hourly surge peaks are unmeasured [U]]
how_to_model: Surge multiplier from zone demand/supply ratio (R07); weather enters only through demand and speed, not as a separate weather fee.

name: Snowfall rate and accumulation
description: How much snow falls per hour and in total, which slows traffic, changes demand and can stop robotaxis.
values_or_range: Central Park 2009-2025: mean 28.9 in/season (2.3 in 2022-23 to 61.9 in 2010-11); per year 10.8 days >=0.1 in, 6.9 >=1 in, 2.7 >=4 in, 1.4 >=6 in, 0.4 >=10 in; record 27.3 in on 23 Jan 2016 (fact-check: with 0.2 in on 22 Jan the storm total is 27.5 in [P*], the largest Central Park storm on record [U]); 2026: 11.4 in on 25 Jan, 19.7 in on 22-23 Feb [P*]
impact_evidence: NYC DOT sensor speed x0.51 in heavy snow [S]; 16 Jan 2024 (1.3 in): yellow trips -5%, morning speeds -14% to -23% [P]
data_source: NOAA GHCN-Daily Central Park (SNOW, SNWD) via GitHub copy https://github.com/toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data ; NOAA LCD present-weather codes
how_to_model: Hourly snowfall rate and running depth drive speed (R04-008), demand (R04-017), crash risk (R04-041) and robotaxi limits (R04-039).

name: Snow cover and plowing state after a storm
description: Snow left on roads and curbs for days after a storm: narrower lanes, blocked curbs and slow side streets.
values_or_range: Snow depth >=1 in on 22.5 days/yr at Central Park [P*]; side streets 1-3 days to clear [U]
impact_evidence: Depth statistics [P*]; clearing times [U]
data_source: GHCN-Daily SNWD; NYC DSNY snow-plow tracking (PlowNYC) [U, URL not verified]
how_to_model: Per-borough 'cleared' state that recovers over 1-3 days, adding speed and pickup-dwell penalties on uncleared streets.

name: Freezing rain, sleet and black ice
description: Icy precipitation and refreezing that make bridges and ramps slippery and raise crash risk more than snow does.
values_or_range: A few days per year [U]; highest crash multiplier of any weather type [U]; bridges and elevated roads ice first [U]
impact_evidence: Road-weather background knowledge; FHWA pages unreachable [U]
data_source: NOAA LCD present-weather codes (FZRA, PL); NWS winter weather advisories (IEM archive) https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/
how_to_model: Precipitation-type flag that applies the snow speed penalty plus a higher crash multiplier, larger on bridges and elevated links.

name: Snow-day demand mix
description: Snow changes who travels: closed schools and remote work cut commutes, while people who must travel switch from walking and buses to cars.
values_or_range: Small snows (0.1-1.3 in), 2023-24: yellow trips -3% (n.s.); 16 Jan 2024 -5% [P]; big storms likely -30% or more during the storm, rebound afterwards [U]; NYC public schools now go remote on snow days [U]
impact_evidence: Our TLC daily regressions [P]; big-storm effect [U]
data_source: TLC trip records + GHCN-Daily; NYC public school closure announcements
how_to_model: Snow multiplier on demand by trip purpose: commute down, airport and medical stable, short trips up.

name: Winter road damage and salt
description: Potholes, road salt and slush add tyre, alignment, corrosion and car-wash costs in late winter.
values_or_range: Pothole complaints peak Feb-Apr [U]; +$5-15 per week in washing and wear in winter [design guess]
impact_evidence: [U] and [design guess]
applies_to: human app driver, taxi, robotaxi, fleet
how_to_model: Seasonal maintenance cost-per-mile multiplier (cross-link R08).

name: Digging out after a storm
description: Street-parked cars get plowed in after snow, so drivers lose 30-90 minutes clearing the car before the first trip on high-demand snow days.
values_or_range: Delay of 30-90 min after >= 4 in of snow for street-parked cars; about 0 for garaged cars and depot fleets [design]. NYC suspends alternate-side parking during snow operations, while parking meters stay in force.
impact_evidence: [design]; [S] 311 and press (PIX11, Newsweek) on alternate-side parking suspensions for snow operations.
applies_to: human app driver; taxi (garages and robotaxi depots exempt)
data_source: NOAA GHCN-Daily snowfall (Central Park USW00094728); NYC 311 alternate-side parking status
how_to_model: Draw a shift-start delay when overnight snowfall passes a threshold, depending on parking type (R08-052).

name: Hourly air temperature, humidity and heat index
description: Outdoor temperature (with dew point for heat index and wind for wind chill) each hour.
values_or_range: Central Park 2009-2025 mean daily max 39.6°F (Jan) to 86.0°F (Jul); per year 62.9 days with min <=32°F, 18.1 days max >=90°F, 2.8 days >=95°F; highest 104°F on 22 Jul 2011 [P*] [corrected by fact-check: this is the 2009-2025 maximum in our copy, not the all-time record; the Central Park record is 106°F on 9 Jul 1936 [U]]
impact_evidence: Our climate statistics from GHCN-Daily [P*]; drives EV energy, demand and comfort
data_source: NOAA LCD hourly dry-bulb and dew point; GHCN-Daily TMAX/TMIN
how_to_model: Hourly series feeding the demand (R04-020), HVAC energy (R04-023) and EV range (R04-037) functions.

name: Temperature demand effect
description: How hot and cold days change the number of rides and how short they are.
values_or_range: Yellow trips vs 51-80°F days, with month and weekday controls, 2023: max >=90°F +22% (t=1.9), 81-89°F +11% (t=1.6), max <=35°F +4% (n.s.); short-trip share +2.5 pp on cold days (t=5.2), +1.3 pp on hot days (t=3.2) [P]
impact_evidence: Our 2023 TLC regressions, small samples (12 hot, 9 cold days) [P]
how_to_model: Temperature-band multipliers on demand and short-trip share, refitted on several years before use.

name: Heat waves and heat advisories
description: Multi-day hot spells with official advisories that raise short-trip demand, strain power and transit, and tire drivers.
values_or_range: NWS NYC heat advisory roughly heat index >=95°F for 2+ days or >=100°F [U]; 2.8 days/yr >=95°F [P*]; subway heat and A/C failures [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] frequency; effects [U]
data_source: NWS alerts (IEM archive) https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/ ; NOAA LCD
how_to_model: Heat-event flag raising short-trip demand, A/C energy and fatigue, with a small chance of correlated power or transit outages.

name: Extreme cold and wind chill
description: Very cold hours that cut EV range, slow charging, fail weak batteries and push people into cars.
values_or_range: Daily min <=20°F on 14.6 days/yr, <=10°F on 2.1 days/yr; lowest -1°F on 14 Feb 2016 [P*] [corrected by fact-check: this is the 2009-2025 minimum in our copy, not the all-time record; the Central Park record low is -15°F in Feb 1934 [U]]
impact_evidence: [P*] frequency; effects via R04-037/038 [S]/[U]
how_to_model: Cold flag triggering EV range and charging penalties, a small 12V battery failure chance [design guess] and the short-trip shift.

name: Thunderstorms and lightning
description: Short, intense, often local summer storms that cause sudden demand spikes, airport ground stops and street flooding.
values_or_range: Mostly May-Sep afternoons; 30-120 min; rain rates can exceed 1 in/h [U]; GSOD thunder flag shows 0 days in 2023 at Central Park, so station flags are unreliable [P*]
impact_evidence: [U]; station-flag check [P*]
data_source: NOAA LCD weather-type codes (TS); NEXRAD on AWS https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-nexrad/ ; NWS warnings (IEM)
how_to_model: Convective-cell generator: short heavy-rain bursts over a subset of zones, coupled to airport delays (R04-031).

name: Flash flooding and flooded roads
description: Extreme rain that floods parkways, underpasses and basements, closing links for hours.
values_or_range: Central Park extreme days: 7.13 in (1 Sep 2021, Ida), 5.48 in (29 Sep 2023), 4.45 in (21 Aug 2021); >=2 in on 2.5 days/yr [P*]; flood-prone FDR, BQE, Major Deegan, Grand Central and Bronx River parkways [U]
impact_evidence: 29 Sep 2023: yellow-trip average speeds at 08:00-09:00 -29% to -35% [P] [corrected by fact-check: all yellow trips citywide (mostly Manhattan), not a Manhattan-only measure]; Waymo fleet recall May 2026 after flooded-road incidents [S, via R06] [uncertain: not re-checked at source; news hosts unreachable]
data_source: FloodNet NYC street-flood sensors https://www.floodnet.nyc/ [U]; NYC 311 street-flooding complaints; GHCN-Daily
how_to_model: When hourly rain passes a threshold (e.g. 1.5 in/h [design guess]), close or slow a list of flood-prone links for 1-6 h; entering a closed link carries damage risk (R04-043).

name: Weather-driven transit disruption (weather cause of R03-046)
description: Subway and rail suspensions caused by flooding, snow, heat or storms, which push riders onto cars. R03-046 owns the subway-incident object; R04 supplies the weather trigger and its demand evidence.
values_or_range: 29 Sep 2023 flood with subway suspensions [uncertain: the suspensions are background knowledge; only the trip changes come from our data]: yellow trips +17% for the day and +46% to +63% from 05:00-09:00 [P]; full MTA shutdowns for Irene (2011), Sandy (2012) and the Jan 2015 blizzard [U]
impact_evidence: Our TLC hourly event study [P]
data_source: MTA ridership https://data.ny.gov/ ; MTA GTFS-realtime alerts (no historical archive found)
how_to_model: Disruption event that boosts car demand in the catchment of suspended lines (cross-link R03, R05).

name: Wind speed and gusts
description: Wind that brings down trees and branches and triggers bridge restrictions; little direct effect on cars otherwise.
values_or_range: Central Park mean daily wind 5.3 mph (sensor sheltered by trees; LGA/JFK windier); 2023: 5 days with gusts >=30 kn, max 34 kn (gusts reported on only 213 of 365 days); Sandy day mean 18.8 mph [P*]; bridge wind limits mostly hit trucks and motorcycles [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] station data; restrictions [U]
data_source: NOAA LCD (LGA USW00014732, JFK USW00094789); NOAA GSOD
how_to_model: Gust threshold triggers random tree-down link closures and bridge restrictions.

name: Hurricanes, tropical storms and nor'easters
description: Rare multi-hazard storms combining heavy rain, wind, storm-surge flooding, power cuts and transit shutdowns over 1-3 days.
values_or_range: About one major event every few years [U]; Irene 28 Aug 2011 (3.99 in; 6.87 in over 27-28 Aug), Sandy 29 Oct 2012 (mean wind 18.8 mph), Henri and Ida Aug-Sep 2021 [P*]; evacuation zones 1-6 [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] station data; scenario consequences [U]
data_source: NOAA NHC HURDAT2 https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/ ; NYC hurricane evacuation zones (NYC Open Data) [U]
how_to_model: Scripted scenario pack combining R04-025/026/029/030, with demand collapse during the storm and a surge afterwards.

name: Post-storm fuel and charging shortages
description: Fuel or charging scarcity after a major storm.
values_or_range: Odd-even gas rationing in NYC in Nov 2012 after Sandy [U]
applies_to: human app driver, taxi, robotaxi, fleet
how_to_model: Fuel-availability flag: refuelling takes longer or fails (cross-link R08).

name: Airport weather delays and cancellations (weather cause of R03-049)
description: Thunderstorms, snow, wind and low cloud cause ground stops and cancellations at JFK, LGA and EWR, shifting airport pickup demand in time. R03-049 owns the airport-disruption object.
values_or_range: Summer thunderstorm ground stops; mass cancellations in snowstorms [U]; airport pickup share did not change on rain days in 2023 (+0.2 to -0.4 pp, n.s.) [P]
impact_evidence: Our TLC airport share [P]; delay mechanisms [U]
data_source: BTS Airline On-Time Performance https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ ; FAA airport status (live)
how_to_model: Weather perturbs flight-arrival banks: delays shift airport demand later, cancellations remove it (cross-link R01-052, R05-063).

name: Weather cancellation and delay of outdoor events (input to R03-020, R03-021)
description: Rainouts, rain delays and postponed outdoor concerts move or remove event egress surges. R03-020/R03-021 own event cancellation and weather-at-let-out effects.
values_or_range: Baseball rainouts and delays; outdoor concerts and parades postponed [U]
data_source: Retrosheet game logs (rainouts) https://www.retrosheet.org/ [uncertain: game logs list games played; postponements and their reasons are recalled to sit in Retrosheet's schedule files, not re-read]; NYC permitted events (NYC Open Data)
how_to_model: Event cancel/delay probability conditioned on rain forecast and observed rain; shifts or removes the R03 egress surge.

name: Fog and low visibility
description: Fog and mist that slow traffic slightly, raise crash risk, limit robotaxis and delay flights.
values_or_range: Central Park 2023 (GSOD): fog flagged on 27 days; daily mean visibility <5 mi on 18 days, <3 mi on 2, never <1 mi [P*]
impact_evidence: [P*] station data; effects [U]
data_source: NOAA LCD visibility; NOAA GSOD FRSHTT flags
how_to_model: Visibility class adds a small speed and crash penalty and feeds robotaxi limits (R04-039) and airport delays (R04-031).

name: Wildfire smoke and air quality alerts
description: Smoke or ozone episodes that push people from walking and cycling into cars and cancel outdoor events.
values_or_range: 7 Jun 2023 Canadian smoke (AQI near 480 at worst [U]): yellow trips +4.8% for the day, +15% to +17% at 14:00-15:00 vs nearby Wednesdays [P]; NYS air quality health advisories on several summer days a year [S]
impact_evidence: Our TLC event comparison [P]; NYS DEC advisory texts in a public dataset [S]
data_source: EPA AirNow API https://docs.airnowapi.org/ ; EPA AQS https://aqs.epa.gov/aqsweb/documents/data_api.html ; Open-Meteo air-quality API
how_to_model: AQI series; above ~150, shift walking and cycling trips to cars, cancel outdoor events, raise driver discomfort.

name: Low-sun glare
description: Low sun shining straight down a street blinds drivers and cameras, especially along Manhattan's crosstown grid.
values_or_range: Sunset azimuth ~299° (grid-aligned) around 24-25 May and 17-18 Jul; sunrise ~119° around 2-3 Dec and 8-9 Jan (2026, our calculation) [P] (fact-check: reproduced with an independent NOAA solar-position calculation) [uncertain: these are dates for the sun at the geometric horizon; the published 'Manhattanhenge' dates, with the sun just above the real horizon, are about 28-30 May and 11-13 Jul, recalled not re-read; glare risk spans several days around both]; camera-based driving struggles in glare and low visibility (NHTSA probe) [S]
impact_evidence: Sun-angle calculation [P]; NHTSA FSD low-visibility probe reported in news [S] [uncertain: the cited GitHub source is near-empty on re-check; the probe was opened in Oct 2024 [U] and its later status was not re-checked]
data_source: astral sun position; OSM street bearings https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/new-york.html
how_to_model: When sun elevation <10° and street bearing within ±10° of sun azimuth, small speed and crash penalty on those links.

name: Cold-battery charging speed and preconditioning (see R08-010)
description: Cold batteries charge slowly unless warmed first; hot batteries can throttle. Shared with R08-010.
values_or_range: DC fast-charge power reduced with a cold battery; preconditioning 10-30 min uses energy [U]
data_source: AFDC station locator https://afdc.energy.gov/stations ; no public charging-curve-by-temperature data found
how_to_model: Charging-power curve scaled by battery temperature; agent may precondition while driving to a charger at an energy cost.

name: Weather crash-risk multiplier for the agent's car
description: Higher chance that the agent's own car crashes in rain, snow, ice or fog, with repair cost and lost days.
values_or_range: NYC crashes per hour in rainy vs dry hours at the same hour of day (2023-2025, not exposure-adjusted): about -1% to +5% at 08:00-17:00, about +10% at 00:00, 07:00 and 18:00, and +20% to +34% at most hours from 19:00 to 06:00 [S] [corrected by fact-check: was '10-35% higher' at every hour; the notebook output shows almost no difference in daytime, and its 'rain' hours include trace amounts]; snow and ice higher [U]; cost: deductible $500-2,500 plus 2-10 days off the road [design guess]
impact_evidence: Jususs/NYC_Big_Data notebook joining NYPD crashes to NOAA LCD [S] [corrected by fact-check: impact lowered from medium to low; crashes are rare per driver-hour, so even a 20-30% weather multiplier changes expected profit per hour very little, though one crash can dominate a single run [design guess]]
data_source: NYPD Motor Vehicle Collisions https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/Motor-Vehicle-Collisions-Crashes/h9gi-nx95 + NOAA LCD
how_to_model: Poisson crash hazard per mile x weather multiplier; a crash ends the shift and charges cost (cross-link R08, R10-025).

name: Flood water damage and stranding risk
description: Chance that driving into standing water stalls or wrecks the car.
values_or_range: About 6 in of water can stall a car; flood-damaged cars are often written off [U]
data_source: FloodNet depths https://www.floodnet.nyc/ ; no damage data found
how_to_model: If the route crosses a flooded link above a depth threshold, stochastic stall: car stuck for hours plus repair cost.

name: Tipping response to weather
description: Whether riders tip more in bad weather; in the data they barely do.
values_or_range: Yellow card tips 22.3% of fare on dry days; rain days +0.1 to +0.2 pp (n.s.); Uber tip incidence 19.6%, +0.3 pp on wet days (n.s.) [P]; sunnier days slightly higher tips (Devaraj & Patel 2017) [U]
impact_evidence: Our 2023 yellow and Jan 2023 HVFHV regressions [P]
data_source: TLC tip_amount (card trips) and HVFHV tips
how_to_model: Keep tip rates weather-independent by default; optional small multiplier.

name: Rider willingness to pay in bad weather
description: Riders accept higher prices when it is wet or very cold, so surge loses fewer of them.
values_or_range: Price elasticity 10-30% lower in rain [design guess]
impact_evidence: [U] general ride-hail pricing literature; none NYC-specific found
how_to_model: Weather term in the rider price-acceptance function (R05, R07).

name: Driver weather log-off thresholds
description: How human drivers (competitors and the agent's persona) cut hours in snow, ice or floods, which they do not do in ordinary rain.
values_or_range: Rain: taxi supply about flat (Farber 2015) [U]; heavy snow: supply -10% to -40% [U, as R06-050]; NYC cab drivers respond positively to higher earnings opportunities (Farber 2015 abstract) [P*]
impact_evidence: Farber 2015 QJE abstract via NBER metadata copy [P*] (fact-check: confirmed in the NBER w20604 metadata, Oct 2014; the abstract does not mention rain, so the rain result stays [U]); snow numbers [U]
applies_to: taxi, human app driver, competitor supply
data_source: TLC trip records (no driver IDs in current files); Farber used 2009-2013 TLC data
how_to_model: Weather-dependent log-off hazard in the competitor supply model (cross-link R06-050).

name: Driver comfort and fatigue in heat and cold
description: Extreme heat or cold makes a human driver tire faster.
values_or_range: Fatigue rate +10-20% on extreme-temperature days [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design guess]; cross-link R09-007
how_to_model: Temperature term in the fatigue accumulation function.

name: Seasonal climate mix per scenario day
description: How likely each weather type is in each month, which sets how often each effect appears in randomly drawn scenario days.
values_or_range: Central Park 2009-2025: wet-day (>=0.01 in) probability 0.28 (Sep) to 0.39 (May, Dec); snow-day probability Jan 0.11, Feb 0.13, Mar 0.05, Dec 0.06; days >=90°F per month Jul 8.1, Aug 4.8, Jun 2.7; freezing nights Jan 19.7 [P*]
impact_evidence: Our GHCN-Daily climate statistics [P*]
how_to_model: Scenario-day sampler stratified by month and weather type; report the weather class with every score.

name: Weather counterfactual and ablation pairs
description: Running the same demand day with and without weather effects, or with rain injected at a chosen time, to measure how much of an agent's earnings come from handling weather.
values_or_range: Weather on/off; rain injected at time t; information level L0-L3 crossed with weather on/off [design]
impact_evidence: [design]
how_to_model: Harness toggles weather multipliers while holding other random draws fixed.

name: Spatial resolution of weather
description: Whether one station represents the whole city or weather varies by zone.
values_or_range: One station (Central Park) / 4-5 stations (Central Park USW00094728, LGA USW00014732, JFK USW00094789, EWR USW00014734, Teterboro USW00094741) / 1-km radar grid [P* station IDs; design]; summer storms can be very local [U]
impact_evidence: Station list from a public NOAA LCD analysis [P*]; locality [U]
data_source: NOAA LCD for the listed stations; NOAA MRMS radar
how_to_model: Nearest-station or radar interpolation to taxi zones.

name: Temporal resolution of weather
description: Daily, hourly or minute weather data; coarse data hide most of the rain effect.
values_or_range: Daily (GHCN) / hourly (LCD routine reports at :51) / 1-5 min (ASOS); our daily estimate (+6% Uber on wet days) vs ~+25% per rainy hour in Brodeur & Nield [P, S] [uncertain: the Brodeur & Nield figure was not re-read at source]
impact_evidence: Comparison of our daily estimate with the hourly literature [P, S]
how_to_model: Hourly by default; finer only for onset dynamics.

name: Climate trend in extremes
description: Whether to include more frequent extreme rain in 'future NYC' scenarios.
values_or_range: 4 of the 12 wettest Central Park days in 2009-2025 fell in 2021-2023 (21 Aug, 1 Sep and 26 Oct 2021; 29 Sep 2023), 5 counting 23 Mar 2024 [corrected by fact-check: was '3 of the 12'; 3 of the 12 also fell in Aug-Sep 2011, so this clustering is weak evidence of a trend]; seasonal snowfall swings 2.3-61.9 in [P*]; heavier downpours in the Northeast long-term [U]
impact_evidence: [P*] ranking; trend [U]
data_source: NOAA GHCN-Daily; NYC Panel on Climate Change reports [U]
how_to_model: Optional scenario knob raising extreme-rain frequency.

name: Weather speed-penalty table (input to R10-006)
description: How much slower traffic moves in each weather class; R10 applies it to link speeds.
values_or_range: NYC DOT sensors 2023-2025, median speed vs dry baseline (same sensor, day type, hour): light rain 0.95, moderate 0.91, heavy 0.91; light snow 0.91, moderate 0.80, heavy 0.51 [S] [uncertain: the ratios were re-read in the notebook output (0.946, 0.914, 0.913; 0.908, 0.798, 0.513), but its bins use thresholds of 2.5 and 10 (rain) and 2 and 5 (snow) in undocumented units, probably mm per hour, with each sensor matched to its nearest LCD station, so its classes do not map exactly onto the in/h bins in R04-001]. Our TLC: heavy-rain days -0.4 mph (t=-2.2); 29 Sep 2023 08:00-09:00 7.5-8.4 vs 11.6-11.8 mph (-29% to -35%); snow 16 Jan 2024 08:00-10:00 -14% to -23% [P]
impact_evidence: Jususs/NYC_Big_Data notebook joining NYC DOT speeds to NOAA LCD [S]; our TLC hourly speeds [P]
data_source: NYC DOT Traffic Speeds NBE https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/DOT-Traffic-Speeds-NBE/i4gi-tjb9 + NOAA LCD; TLC trip speeds
how_to_model: Lookup multiplier by precipitation class x road class (highway vs street) x hour, applied on top of the R10 weekly profile.

name: Time-dependent link speed profile
description: Typical speed on each road segment for each time bucket of the week; the base layer from which every travel time is computed.
values_or_range: Manhattan south of 60th St 9.1 mph (2010) to 7.1 mph (2017) [S]; 2023 yellow trips within Manhattan below 60th St: weekday 6.8-7.6 mph from 9 AM to 6 PM, 8.5 mph at 8 AM [P*: own analysis of 38.3M TLC 2023 yellow trips]; CBD 8.2 to 9.7 mph after Jan 2025 [uncertain: 8.2 to 9.7 mph is +18%, not the +15% headline, and the mph pair could not be traced to the NBER paper]; overnight local streets ~15-25 mph [corrected by fact-check: TLC trip-average speeds at 0-5 AM are 11.6-13.6 mph within Manhattan below 60th St (yellow 2023) and about 20-25 mph citywide including highways (HVFHV Jan 2023); 15-25 mph fits the outer boroughs, not Manhattan]; expressways 30-50 mph off-peak [U]; 2016 five-minute buckets per week (Valhalla [P]) or 168 hourly buckets
impact_evidence: NYC DOT Mobility Report 2018: speeds south of 60th St fell 9.1 to 7.1 mph 2010-2017; trip time is the denominator of $/hour [S]; TLC 2023 trip speeds reproduce ~7 mph daytime [P*]
data_source: NYC TLC trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page ; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds NBE https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/DOT-Traffic-Speeds-NBE/i4gi-tjb9 ; MTA Bus Route Segment Speeds https://data.ny.gov/d/58t6-89vi
how_to_model: Per-edge weekly speed profile (Valhalla predicted-speed format) or road-class x zone x hour-of-week multipliers on OSM free-flow speeds, calibrated so zone-pair durations match TLC.

name: Core-versus-periphery speed gradient
description: How much slower the dense core (Midtown, Lower Manhattan) is than the rest of Manhattan and the outer boroughs at the same hour.
values_or_range: Midtown ~4.3-5 mph vs Manhattan south of 60th St ~6.9-7.1 mph (2017-2019) [S]; HVFHV Jan 2023 weekday 9 AM-6 PM trip speeds (both trip ends inside the area): Midtown core (zones 100, 161-164, 186, 230) 5.4-6.0 mph, Manhattan below 60th St 8.2-8.5 mph, citywide 12.3-15.1 mph [P*]; outer-borough arterials ~10-20 mph daytime [U]; core/citywide speed ratio 0.37-0.45 measured, ~0.3-0.6 as a design range [P*]
impact_evidence: Sam Schwartz report from taxi+FHV GPS: Midtown 4.8 mph vs Manhattan below 60th St 6.9 mph [S]
data_source: TLC trip records + taxi zone shapefile; MTA CBD Taxi and FHV Speeds (beginning Oct 2019) https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/mta-central-business-district-vehicle-speeds-beginning-october-2019 [uncertain: dataset title and URL not re-checked]
how_to_model: Zone-level speed multiplier by hour fitted from TLC intra- and inter-zone trip speeds; creates the core trade-off of high demand vs slow trips.

name: Peak-hour slowdown curve
description: Shape of the within-day speed curve (AM peak, midday plateau, PM peak, late-night free flow) applied to travel times.
values_or_range: Midtown to JFK median 38 min (10-11 AM) vs 64 min (4-5 PM) in 2009-2015 [S] [corrected by fact-check: 2023 TLC yellow weekday trips from the Midtown core to JFK took a median 29 min at 3-5 AM, 54 min at 10-11 AM and 75 min at 4-5 PM (P*); the 38-min figure is not reproduced and may reflect an older era or another hour]; CBD worst on weekdays 1-7 PM [S]; core Manhattan 8-9 AM ~9 mph (14.5 km/h) [S; consistent with 8.5-8.8 mph in TLC 2023 data, P*]; overnight ~1.5-3x faster than midday [corrected by fact-check: 1.6-2.2x in TLC 2023 data, e.g. Manhattan below 60th St 13.6 mph at 4 AM vs 6.8 mph at noon, Midtown core 11.8 vs 5.4 mph, P*]
impact_evidence: Schneider analysis of TLC taxi trips 2009-2015: Midtown to JFK median 38 vs 64 min depending on hour [S]; TLC 2023 yellow trips: 29-75 min by hour [P*]
data_source: TLC trip records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds NBE (i4gi-tjb9)
how_to_model: Hour-of-week multiplier per zone pair or edge class; the calendar that indexes it lives in R02.

name: Day-type and seasonal speed shifts
description: Speed differences between weekdays, weekends, holidays, summer and the December shopping season, including official Gridlock Alert Days.
values_or_range: 20 Gridlock Alert Days in 2025 (UNGA week 22-26 Sep; 19, 20, 25 Nov; 12 days in Dec) [S]; Midtown under 4 mph in UNGA week [S]; weekend mornings and holiday weeks faster [U]; TLC 2023 check: weekday daytime speed within Manhattan below 60th St fell from 8.3 mph (Jan) to 6.5 mph (Sep, Dec), a ~22% seasonal swing, and the slowest weekdays were 18-20 Sep (UNGA week), 21 and 29 Nov and 5-7 Dec [P*]
impact_evidence: NYC DOT 2025 Gridlock Alert Days announcement: Midtown average speeds fell under 4 mph during UNGA [S]
data_source: NYC DOT Gridlock Alert Days https://nyc.gov/gridlockalert ; TLC trip records by date
how_to_model: Day-type factor (weekday / Sat / Sun / holiday / gridlock-alert) multiplying the weekly profile; gridlock days flagged in the scenario calendar.

name: Congestion-pricing speed regime (since 5 Jan 2025)
description: The step change in speeds inside and around the Manhattan Congestion Relief Zone after tolling began, which shifts all calibrated travel times.
values_or_range: CBD speeds +15% vs synthetic control [S] (8.2 to 9.7 mph [uncertain: implies +18%, source not traced]; a later paper version reportedly +11% [uncertain: not re-read]); >20% gains weekday 1-7 PM; trips to/within CBD ~8% faster; 2025 vs 2024 AM-peak crossing times: Holland -36%, Williamsburg -23%, Queensboro -21%, Hugh Carey -16%, Brooklyn Br -13%, Lincoln -10% (some reposts -5%) [uncertain: conflicting secondary figures], Queens-Midtown -4%
impact_evidence: Cook et al. NBER w33584 (Google Maps data, synthetic control vs 5 cities) [S]; NY Governor release 9 Sep 2025 [S]
data_source: NBER w33584 https://www.nber.org/papers/w33584 ; MTA Congestion Relief Zone entries dashboard (data.ny.gov) [uncertain: exact dataset not re-checked]; TLC 2025+ trip records (HVFHV files carry a cbd_congestion_fee column, so post-pricing trips are identifiable [P*])
how_to_model: Calibrate speed profiles on post-Jan-2025 trips for current scenarios; keep a pre-2025 profile as a separate regime for historical or counterfactual scenarios.

name: Endogenous congestion from ride-hail volume
description: Feedback whereby the simulated fleet's own vehicles, and FHV traffic overall, slow the streets they use.
values_or_range: FHVs ~30% of Manhattan-core traffic (2019); SF weekday delay +62% 2010-2016 vs +22% counterfactual without TNCs; a benchmark fleet of 1-500 cars is tiny vs NYC's tens of thousands of FHVs [U]
impact_evidence: Erhardt et al. 2019 Science Advances [S]; TLC 23 Jul 2019 presentation [S]
data_source: none needed for small N; TLC FHV trip volumes for background
how_to_model: Ignore for N up to ~1,000; for stretch scenarios add fleet vehicles to zone-level background volume and apply a BPR-style volume-delay function.

name: Trip-level travel-time noise
description: Random deviation of a realised trip time from its expected time for the same origin, destination and departure time.
values_or_range: multiplicative lognormal with CV ~0.15-0.35 [design] [corrected by fact-check: TLC 2023 weekday zone-pair x hour cells (54k cells, 23M trips) give CV median 0.28 (P10 0.20, P90 0.46) and sd(log) median 0.26; sd(log) is 0.41 for trips under 1.5 mi, 0.29 at 1.5-3 mi, 0.23 at 3-6 mi and 0.21 above 6 mi; these include within-zone address spread, so they are upper bounds on traffic noise (P*)]; Midtown to JFK 4-5 PM P90 84 min vs median 64 (+31%) in 2009-2015 [S]; 2023: P90 94 vs median 75 min (+26%), daytime P90/median 1.26-1.33 [P*]; buffer index 20-60% on unreliable arterials [uncertain: no source given]
impact_evidence: Schneider TLC airport analysis: P90/median about 1.3 [S]; FHWA buffer-index definition (95th pct vs mean) [S]; TLC 2023 dispersion analysis [P*]
data_source: TLC trip records (dispersion of durations per zone pair x hour)
how_to_model: Fit quantiles per zone pair x hour from TLC; realised time = expected x lognormal(0, sigma_zone,hour), seeded identically across models.

name: Day-level and area-level correlated slowdowns
description: Shared shocks that make a whole day or area slower than typical, so errors on consecutive trips are correlated rather than independent.
values_or_range: day factor 0.8-1.25 [design; confirmed by TLC 2023: weekday daily speed factor within Manhattan below 60th St P5-P95 0.82-1.20, P1-P99 0.77-1.23, extremes 0.75 on 6 Dec and 1.40 on 3 Jul (bridge day), P*]; zone-hour factor 0.85-1.2 [design]; extremes on gridlock and storm days (the slowest 2023 weekdays were UNGA week and early December) [P*]
impact_evidence: [design] correlated shocks are what make a learnt 'today is slow' signal valuable; independent noise averages out; TLC 2023 day-level spread [P*]
data_source: TLC trip records (day-to-day variance of zone-hour medians)
how_to_model: Hierarchical noise: realised = typical x day_factor x zone_hour_factor x trip_noise, with AR(1) persistence within the day.

name: Airport-corridor tail risk
description: Heavy right tail of trip times to and from JFK, LGA and EWR via the Van Wyck, Grand Central Parkway, BQE and Hudson crossings.
values_or_range: Midtown to JFK median 38-64 min by hour, P90 up to 84 min (2009-2015) [S] [corrected by fact-check: 2023 weekday Midtown core to JFK median 29-75 min, P90 up to 94 min at 4-5 PM]; LGA ~20-50 min [U] [corrected by fact-check: 2023 Midtown core to LGA median 21 min (3-5 AM) to 44 min (4 PM), P90 up to 60 min; to EWR median 30 min (night) to 54 min (3-7 PM), P90 76 min; all P*]
impact_evidence: Schneider TLC airport analysis [S]; TLC 2023 yellow trips by hour [P*]
data_source: TLC trip records (taxi zones 132 JFK, 138 LGA, 1 EWR)
how_to_model: Separate per-corridor duration distributions with fatter tails (lognormal mixture) fitted on airport zone pairs.

name: Signal delay and cycle length
description: Average waiting time added at signalised intersections, set by cycle length and green split.
values_or_range: Manhattan avenue cycles ~90 s (2008 field note); ~10-40 s mean delay per signal [U]; ~20 short blocks per mile north-south [U]; OSRM's default car profile adds only 2 s per tagged traffic signal [P]
impact_evidence: Blog field note: Manhattan avenues timed in sequence, cycle ~90 s [S]; NACTO cites 60-90 s cycles [S]
data_source: NYC Open Data 'VZV Signal Timing/25MPH Signal Retiming' https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/vzv_signal-timing ; OSM highway=traffic_signals
how_to_model: Implicit in calibrated speeds for v1; optional node penalty = f(cycle, approach class) in a graph engine.

name: Directional progression (avenue green waves vs crosstown)
description: Avenues run coordinated signal progressions while crosstown streets do not, so north-south travel is much faster than east-west in Manhattan.
values_or_range: Avenues historically progressed at ~25-30 mph, retimed to 25 mph under Vision Zero; 3rd Ave 60th-96th St retimed to 15 mph in 2025 (one of 16 green waves citywide) [uncertain: segment and count not re-read]; Midtown crosstown 4.2-4.8 mph (2002)
impact_evidence: NY1 Feb 2025 on 3rd Ave retiming [S]; NYC DOT THRU Streets document: Midtown crosstown 4.8 EB / 4.2 WB mph [S]
data_source: VZV signal timing dataset; TLC trips (compare north-south vs east-west zone pairs)
how_to_model: Direction-dependent speed factor by edge bearing and class (avenue vs street) in Manhattan, calibrated on TLC.

name: Right-on-red ban
description: NYC prohibits right turns on red unless a sign allows it, adding signal wait to right turns.
values_or_range: banned citywide by default: turns on red only where a sign authorises them (34 RCNY 4-03(a)(3)(ii)) [P*]; 336 signed exceptions in 2019 (Manhattan 6, Staten Island 198) [S]
impact_evidence: 34 RCNY 4-03 [P*]; NY1 2019 count of right-on-red locations [S]
how_to_model: Right turns at signals carry red-phase wait (no free right) in a graph engine; NYC-specific since most US cities allow it.

name: One-way grid and turn restrictions
description: One-way streets, left-turn bans, no-U-turn rules and through-movement bans that lengthen paths relative to straight-line distance.
values_or_range: most Manhattan streets one-way; left turns off 14th St banned at all hours [S]; OSRM default turn penalty up to 7.5 s and U-turn 20 s [corrected by fact-check: 7.5 s is the maximum of an angle-based sigmoid, and turns across oncoming traffic add up to 2 s more, P]; U-turns banned in business districts (34 RCNY 4-05(b)) [P*]; network detour factor ~1.2-1.4 vs grid distance [U]
impact_evidence: NYC DOT 14th Street rules [S]; OSRM car.lua defaults [P]
data_source: OpenStreetMap (oneway, restriction relations) via Geofabrik New York extract https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/new-york.html
how_to_model: Edge-based routing graph with turn restrictions and turn costs (native in OSRM and Valhalla).

name: Wrong-side approach and around-the-block loop
description: Extra time when the vehicle arrives on the wrong side or direction of a one-way street for a pickup or drop-off and must circle the block.
values_or_range: 1-6 min in Midtown; under 1 min on two-way outer-borough streets [design]
impact_evidence: [design] follows from the one-way grid and long Midtown blocks; Uber reports opposite-side meetings often fail [S]
data_source: OSM one-way graph; no empirical loop-time data found
how_to_model: Snap pickup to a curb side and route to that side with turn costs; the loop time emerges from graph routing.

name: Turning delay from pedestrians
description: Delay to turning vehicles that yield to heavy crosswalk volumes and leading pedestrian intervals, especially in Midtown.
values_or_range: 5-30 s per turn at busy Midtown corners [design]
impact_evidence: [design] a known contributor to Midtown slowness; no public NYC measurement found
how_to_model: Zone-hour turn-penalty multiplier in a graph engine; otherwise implicit in calibrated speeds.

name: River-crossing chokepoint delay
description: Queue delay at bridges and tunnels into Manhattan and between boroughs, which dominates many inter-borough trip times.
values_or_range: Holland Tunnel inbound 12 min 48 s (Jan 2024) vs 4 min 27 s (8 Jan 2025); AM-peak crossing times 4-36% lower in 2025; RPA cites >20 min saved via Lincoln Tunnel
impact_evidence: MTA figures via City & State (Jan 2025) and Governor release (Sep 2025) [S]
data_source: Congestion Pricing Tracker (Google Maps every 15 min, 19 routes); TLC trip records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds NBE
how_to_model: Dedicated chokepoint edges with hour-of-week delay curves plus stochastic queue shocks.

name: Highway versus local-street speed gap
description: Speed difference between expressways (FDR, West Side Hwy, BQE, LIE, Van Wyck, Major Deegan) and surface streets, which drives route choice on longer trips.
values_or_range: expressways ~30-50 mph off-peak, can drop under 15 mph in peaks [U]; Manhattan surface streets 5-10 mph daytime
impact_evidence: NYC DOT real-time speed feed covers mainly highways and major arterials, updated several times a minute [S]
how_to_model: Road-class-specific weekly profiles: expressways from the DOT feed, surface streets from TLC calibration.

name: HOV-lane eligibility when carrying riders
description: A car with enough riders aboard may use peak HOV lanes, while an empty car, and a robotaxi carrying a single rider, may not.
values_or_range: The LIE HOV lane in Nassau and Suffolk (about 40 miles [U]) is HOV-2+ on weekdays 6-10 am and 3-8 pm; a violation is a ticket of up to $150 and up to 2 licence points. The Clean Pass solo-EV exemption ended on 30 Sep 2025 [S]. Inside NYC the HOV lanes are HOV-3+: the LIE approach to the Midtown Tunnel in Queens (7-10 am), the Staten Island Expressway and the Gowanus Expressway, with hours varying by lane [S, 511NY page via search snippet; corrected by fact-check, was 'SIE and Gowanus HOV/bus lanes [U]']. So an app car or taxi with ONE rider (2 occupants) qualifies only on the Long Island HOV-2 lane, and inside the city needs 2+ riders. 511NY says Uber, Lyft and taxis may use HOV lanes when they meet the occupancy rule [S]. A robotaxi with one rider has one occupant and qualifies nowhere [design].
impact_evidence: [S] PIX11, CBS New York and News 12 (2025) on the LIE HOV rule and the end of Clean Pass; [S] 511NY HOV page (snippet). It affects only peak Long Island trips and group rides on the SIE, Gowanus or Midtown Tunnel approach, a small part of the ~4% of trips that end out of the city (G2-031).
applies_to: human app driver, taxi; robotaxi (not eligible with one rider); fleet (routing)
data_source: 511NY Rideshare HOV lane page https://511nyrideshare.org/hov-lanes (host not reachable from this session; snippet only); OpenStreetMap hov=* tags
how_to_model: Link speeds depend on occupancy: an HOV link is usable when occupants are at or above its threshold (2 or 3) and its time window is active, so loaded and empty cars get different travel times on the same road. Generalises to HOV/HOT lanes in LA, the Bay Area, etc.

name: Pickup dwell time
description: Time from the vehicle reaching the pickup point until the rider is seated and the trip starts.
values_or_range: median ~1-2 min [U] [corrected by fact-check: Uber trips in Jan 2023 (13.6M) show pickup minus on-scene median 0.8 min (47 s), mean 1.0 min, P75 1.8 min; 17% of trips sit at 2.0-2.2 min and only 3.8% exceed 2.1 min, so the field looks censored at the 2-minute wait clock (P*)]; Uber/Lyft wait fees start 2 min after arrival (5 min for premium) [S] [uncertain for Lyft: not re-read]; Waymo waits up to 5 min (4 min at Phoenix airport) then charges a no-show fee; luggage or mobility aids add ~30-120 s (bus analogue: 15-19 s ordinary vs 28-137 s encumbered)
impact_evidence: Platform wait-fee policies and Waymo help page [S]; HVFHV records carry on_scene and pickup timestamps [P*]; on_scene_datetime is filled for 100% of Uber (HV0003) but 0.14% of Lyft (HV0005) trips in Jan 2023, despite the dictionary's 'accessible vehicles only' label [P*]
data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (pickup_datetime minus on_scene_datetime where populated: Uber only)
how_to_model: Lognormal dwell by zone type (airport, station, residential), hour and luggage flag, calibrated on HVFHV on-scene to pickup gaps.

name: Drop-off dwell and payment time
description: Time from arrival at the destination until the vehicle can leave, including payment (taxi), unloading and door closing.
values_or_range: app trips 15-45 s [design]; taxi card or cash payment +30-90 s [design]; airport curb with luggage 1-3 min [design]
impact_evidence: [design] no public NYC measurement found
data_source: none found (TLC trip end is the drop-off time, not the departure time)
how_to_model: Add a dwell draw after each drop-off before the vehicle becomes available.

name: Curb availability and stopping search
description: Extra time to find a legal or safe spot to stop at busy curbs (no-standing zones, bus lanes, bike lanes, double-parked trucks).
values_or_range: 0-3 min in Midtown and FiDi peaks; ~0 in residential outer boroughs [design]
impact_evidence: [design] Manhattan has few loading docks so curbs are saturated [S on freight]; 34 RCNY 4-11(c): taxis and FHVs may stop briefly to pick up or drop off where standing is banned, must be within 12 in of the curb, and may double-park only if no curb space is free within 100 ft; never in bike lanes, crosswalks or no-stopping zones [P*]
data_source: NYC DOT parking regulation signs dataset [U]; OSM
how_to_model: Zone-hour 'curb friction' delay added to each pickup and drop-off, higher on bus-route blocks.

name: Double parking and delivery lane blockage
description: Background lane capacity lost to double-parked delivery and service vehicles, peaking midday.
values_or_range: corridor capacity -6 to -12% (Manhattan parcel-delivery simulation); a travel lane blocked ~25% of the day on Church Ave, Brooklyn; delivery stops ~21 min, two-thirds double-parked [S]; 34 RCNY 4-08 lets commercial vehicles double-park up to 20 min while loading when no curb space is free on the block [P*]
impact_evidence: BTS/ROSAP Manhattan delivery study [S]; NYC DOT Church Ave analysis [S]
data_source: none direct; captured in TLC-calibrated speeds
how_to_model: Implicit in calibrated midday speeds; optional explicit blockage events on curb-lane edges.

name: Rider pin accuracy and meeting friction
description: Delay or failed pickups because the rider's GPS pin, the vehicle's position or the agreed side of the street is wrong.
values_or_range: GNSS error can reach 50 m or more in urban canyons; shadow matching roughly doubled accuracy [uncertain: not re-read]; 0.5-3 min extra or a cancellation [design]
impact_evidence: Uber Engineering 'Rethinking GPS' and GPS World coverage [S]
data_source: none public for NYC error rates
how_to_model: Draw pin error (sigma 10-20 m outer boroughs, 30-60 m Midtown/FiDi [design]); if past half a block or on the opposite side, add search time or a cancellation chance.

name: Hotspot curb queues
description: Queues of pickup vehicles at concentrated pickup points (stations, venues, airports) that grow with the number of cars converging, including the agent's own fleet.
values_or_range: 2-10 min approach and queue at Penn Station, Port Authority and venues at peaks [design]; airport lots can be longer (R06)
impact_evidence: [design] no public queue-time data found within the search budget
how_to_model: M/M/c queue at designated pickup nodes with service rate from curb length; fleet vehicles join the same queue.

name: Airport pickup access path
description: Extra driving and waiting to reach designated airport pickup areas (FHV lots, taxi holds) rather than the terminal curb.
values_or_range: +3-15 min [U]; Waymo at Phoenix airport limits terminal wait to 4 min
impact_evidence: [U] JFK and LGA send FHV pickups to designated areas; Waymo PHX airport rules [S]
how_to_model: Airport nodes with a mandatory staging-lot detour and service-type-specific access rules.

name: Night garbage-truck blockages
description: Private carters and city sanitation trucks stop on narrow streets, mostly 22:00-06:00, and hold up traffic for minutes on one-lane streets. Daytime delivery blockage is R10-038. The Commercial Waste Zones are NYC-specific; night refuse blockage generalises.
values_or_range: 1-5 min per encounter; 2-10% chance per late-night trip on one-lane Manhattan and Brooklyn streets [design]. Commercial Waste Zones: 20 zones. The first (Queens Central) moved over between 3 Sep 2024 and 2 Jan 2025, with contracts with a zone carter required from 3 Jan 2025. The Bronx zones followed in late 2025, and Lower Manhattan sign-up opened on 1 Apr 2026. Full rollout is expected by the end of 2027 [S]. Fewer private trucks per street should follow [U].
impact_evidence: [S] DSNY CWZ rule and rollout-schedule pages via search snippets. [corrected: first-zone dates]. [uncertain: the claim 'about half of zones by Dec 2026' was not found]. Night timing [U]; delays [design].
data_source: DSNY Commercial Waste Zones https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/resources/reports/commercial-waste-zones-plan.page ; rollout schedule https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/businesses/cwz/rollout-schedule.page ; DSNY collection schedules (NYC Open Data) [U]
how_to_model: Blocking hazard on local one-lane edges by hour. It is absorbed in calibrated night speeds unless traffic is modelled at link level.

name: Navigation ETA error shown to agent
description: Difference between the ETA the agent is shown and the realised travel time.
values_or_range: multiplicative error with MAE ~10-25% [design]; optimistic bias in peaks [design]
impact_evidence: Uber builds ETAs as routing-engine segment sums plus an ML residual correction (DeepETA, judged by MAE), implying raw router ETAs are biased [S]
data_source: derived from the R10-008 noise model
how_to_model: Shown ETA = expected time x (1 + bias + noise); realised time drawn separately from the true distribution.

name: Dynamic re-routing
description: Whether routes are recomputed en route when conditions change, by a navigation autopilot or by the agent.
values_or_range: none / autopilot every N min / agent-controlled
impact_evidence: [design]
how_to_model: Re-plan the remaining path at each traffic update tick.

name: Vehicle localisation and missed turns
description: Navigation errors such as missed turns in urban canyons where the driver's own GPS drifts.
values_or_range: missed-turn probability 1-5% per Midtown trip for humans [design]; near zero for a robotaxi with lidar and HD-map localisation [U]
impact_evidence: Uber: GNSS errors of 50 m or more in dense cities [S]
how_to_model: Small probability of a 1-4 min loop detour on Midtown and FiDi trips.

name: Map staleness
description: Mismatch between the map the agent sees and the true network (recent turn bans, closures, new bus lanes).
values_or_range: 0-2% of edges stale [design]
impact_evidence: [design] robustness test
how_to_model: Agent map built from an older OSM snapshot, simulator from a newer one.

name: Driver phone reliability and signal dead zones
description: Phones overheating on summer dashboards, battery drain, lost signal in tunnels and under elevated tracks, and app freezes cause missed or timed-out offers.
values_or_range: 0-2% chance of missing an offer, higher in hot sun above about 30 C and in tunnels and under elevated tracks [design]. A second phone for multi-apping doubles the exposure [design].
impact_evidence: [U] driver-forum reports. Missed offers hurt the acceptance rate (R09-040) and can lose an airport queue place (R06-042). R03-045 covers only network-wide outages.
applies_to: human app driver, taxi e-hail; robotaxi connectivity drop-outs are R03-056
data_source: none found (carrier coverage maps are a weak proxy [U])
how_to_model: An offer-delivery failure hazard set by temperature (R04-019) and link type (tunnel, under elevated track); a failure counts as a timeout.

name: Pickup deadhead (en route to rider)
description: Time and distance driven empty from accepting a request to reaching the rider.
values_or_range: NYC HVFHV average wait 4.4-6.6 min by borough (2018-Jan 2026) [S; consistent with a Jan 2023 check: mean request-to-pickup 4.3 min Manhattan, 4.7 Brooklyn, 4.8 Bronx, 5.0 Queens, 5.5 Staten Island, 4.6 citywide; Uber request-to-on-scene (pure en-route time) mean 3.0-4.3 min, median 2.4-3.7 min by borough, P*]; ~10% of ride-hail VMT is driving to pickups (six US metros); SF pickup ETAs late 2025: Waymo 5.74 min, Uber 3.15, Lyft 5.14
impact_evidence: TLC license pause report Feb 2026 [S]; TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 [P*]; Fehr & Peers 2019 [S]; Obi via Axios [S]
data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime; on_scene filled for Uber only)
how_to_model: Same travel-time engine from vehicle position to pickup; logged per trip for utilisation metrics.

name: Repositioning travel cost
description: Time and distance to move empty to a better zone, which the agent weighs against expected demand there.
values_or_range: 5-40 min depending on distance and hour [design]
impact_evidence: [design] repositioning is the core single-car and fleet decision and its cost is pure travel time
how_to_model: Engine returns time and distance for any reposition order; optionally show the estimate before the agent commits.

name: Empty return from airports and outer areas
description: Deadhead back toward demand after a drop-off at an airport or a low-demand area when no return trip is available.
values_or_range: JFK to Midtown roughly 38-64 min by hour (occupied-trip benchmark) [corrected by fact-check: 2023 Midtown core to JFK weekday medians were 29-75 min by hour, LGA 21-44 min (P*)]
impact_evidence: Schneider airport trip times [S]; TLC 2023 yellow trips [P*]
how_to_model: Same engine; the agent chooses between the airport queue (R06) and deadheading back.

name: Depot and charger deadhead
description: Empty travel to depots, cleaning or chargers, which takes vehicles out of service.
values_or_range: 5-30 min each way [design]; 1-3 trips a day for EVs [U]
impact_evidence: [design] cross-link R08 charging
how_to_model: Same engine to charger or depot nodes; charge time from R08.

name: Empty-vehicle speed bias
description: Empty and repositioning vehicles may move at different speeds than occupied trips, but trip data only observe occupied legs.
values_or_range: empty speed 0.8-1.0 x occupied speed [design]
impact_evidence: [design] TLC data record only paid trips, so deadhead speeds are unobserved
how_to_model: Apply occupied-trip calibration to empty moves with an optional factor.

name: Travel-time engine architecture
description: How the simulator computes travel time from A to B: zone-to-zone lookup, road-graph routing with time-dependent speeds, or a hybrid.
values_or_range: (a) 263-zone OD x hour table (lookup IDs 264-265 are Unknown and outside NYC) [P*]; (b) OSRM or Valhalla on OSM with speed profiles; (c) graph geometry for visuals plus OD-calibrated times
impact_evidence: TLC trip files carry only taxi-zone IDs since July 2016, no coordinates [P*]
data_source: TLC trip records; taxi zone shapefile; OpenStreetMap
how_to_model: Recommend (c): Valhalla or OSRM path for geometry and the live map, edge times scaled so zone-pair x hour medians match TLC.

name: Time resolution of speed profiles
description: Bucket width for time-dependent speeds and how the chosen router supports it.
values_or_range: Valhalla: 2016 five-minute speeds per edge per week (DCT-II compressed) plus free-flow (night) and constrained (7 AM-7 PM) speeds; OSRM: no native time dependence, reload a segment-speed CSV with osrm-customize (MLD) per bucket; options 5 / 15 / 60 min
impact_evidence: Valhalla historical-traffic and speeds docs [P]; OSRM command-line docs [S], and docs/tools.md read on GitHub [P] (osrm-customize applies --segment-speed-file and --turn-penalty-file to an MLD graph; the release line is 26.x, package.json 26.10.0)
how_to_model: Valhalla predicted traffic with depart_at times, or 168 hourly OSRM datasets switched by the simulation clock.

name: Router default-speed bias
description: Out-of-the-box router speeds assume free flow and badly underestimate dense-city travel times unless calibrated.
values_or_range: OSRM car.lua: primary 65 km/h, secondary 55, tertiary 40, residential 25 on roads without a maxspeed tag; where OSM has maxspeed it uses 0.8 x maxspeed (25 mph gives ~32 km/h) and adds 2 s per signal; turn penalty up to 7.5 s, U-turn 20 s [P]; Valhalla uses the maxspeed tag directly as routing speed [P]; vs real Midtown ~7-9 km/h daytime, so a 2-5x underestimate [corrected by fact-check: about 3.5x on 25-mph-tagged streets and up to ~7x on untagged primaries, derived]
impact_evidence: OSRM car.lua defaults [P] vs Midtown 4.8 mph [S] and TLC 2023 Midtown core 5.4-6.0 mph [P*]
how_to_model: Never ship raw router ETAs; replace speeds with calibrated profiles and validate.

name: Time-dependent routing consistency (FIFO)
description: Long trips cross speed buckets, so travel time must be integrated over time and a later departure must never arrive earlier.
values_or_range: buckets 5-60 min; trips up to 90+ min
impact_evidence: [design] standard requirement for time-dependent shortest paths
how_to_model: Time-dependent Dijkstra evaluating each edge at its entry time, with smoothed bucket boundaries.

name: Routed vs recorded distance ratio
description: The gap between the router's shortest-path distance and the distance real trips record for the same OD pair and hour. It scales fares, the per-mile pay floor and energy cost.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, OD x 4-hour cells (>= 200 trips, median >= 3 mi; 7,190 cells): median trip_miles is 1.20x the 10th percentile and 1.27x the 5th; p90/p10 = 1.52 (includes address spread within zones). Yellow trips are about 4% shorter than app trips on the same OD: median ratio 0.96 (IQR 0.93-0.99) over 2,199 OD pairs; trip-weighted 0.98. The router-vs-record ratio still needs to be measured with an OSM router.
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV and yellow Jan 2023 (g1/a6.py), re-run in this fact-check. Part of the taxi-app gap may come from different odometers (taximeter vs app GPS) [U]. Router comparison [design].
applies_to: all (separate factors for taxi and app)
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trip_miles, trip_distance); OpenStreetMap with OSRM or Valhalla
how_to_model: Detour factor per OD-hour = recorded median / routed distance, applied to paid distance and energy, separately for taxi and app. Validate on a held-out month.

name: Same travel-time source for replayed and simulated trips
description: Whether replayed background trips use recorded durations while the agent's trips use the engine's travel times, and how the two are reconciled.
values_or_range: Engine times for all trips (default) / recorded times for all replayed trips / a hybrid that scales engine times to match recorded ones per origin-destination pair and hour [design].
impact_evidence: [design] Mixing sources gives the agent a built-in speed edge or handicap over the bots, and breaks the displacement rule (R06-067) when the agent takes a replayed trip. R06-066 does not say which source to use.
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trip_time); NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9
how_to_model: Every vehicle uses one travel-time function; replayed durations are used only for calibration (R10-062).

name: Base request rate by zone and hour
description: Expected number of ride requests starting in each taxi zone in each hour, split by day type, which is the main input that drives all earnings.
values_or_range: Citywide ~18M HVFHV trips in Aug 2024 [corrected by fact-check: 19.13M raw HVFHV rows in Aug 2024, about 617k/day rather than ~580k/day; TLC's '>18M' is consistent] plus ~3M yellow (~97k/day; confirmed, 2.98M rows = 96k/day); Jan 2023: 18.48M HVFHV trips (~596k/day). Per zone-hour (HVFHV Jan 2023): median 64, p99 ~560, max 1,625 pickups/hour [corrected by fact-check: the busiest zone-hours are East Village (zone 79) at 00:00-02:00 on weekend nights and Midtown Center (zone 161) at 19:00-21:00, not generic 'Midtown peaks']; 263 taxi zones plus code 264 (Unknown) and 265 (Outside of NYC)
impact_evidence: [S] TLC testimony 27 Sep 2024: HV sector >18M trips in Aug 2024 (~90% of 2019), yellow ~3M (~50% of 2019); [P*] monthly row counts from a SHA-256 catalog of the TLC files (R02 data folder) and own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (HVFHV Jan 2023)
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (yellow, green, HVFHV; PULocationID x pickup hour) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
how_to_model: Non-homogeneous Poisson rate per zone x 15-min slot x day type, fitted from served trips, then lifted for unserved demand (R05-066)

name: Day-to-day demand randomness (overdispersion)
description: How much realised demand in a zone-hour scatters around its average, beyond pure Poisson noise, because of shared daily shocks.
values_or_range: Coefficient of variation 10-30% per zone-hour on comparable days [fact-check: confirmed. HVFHV Jan 2023, Tue-Thu, zone-hours with >=50 trips: median CV 15% (IQR 12-20%) vs 9% from Poisson noise alone, variance about 2.6x the mean; citywide daily total CV ~11%]; one citywide daily shock plus zone-level shocks
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (HVFHV Jan 2023): variance ~2.6x Poisson, so Poisson alone understates spread; matters for robustness across 100 runs
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (daily counts by zone)
how_to_model: Gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) mixture: daily city multiplier x zone multiplier x Poisson arrivals, seeded per run

name: Bursty, clustered request arrivals
description: Requests arriving in bursts within minutes when crowds leave a venue, a flight bank lands or a train line stops, rather than spread evenly.
values_or_range: Bursts of 5-500 requests within 10-30 min at one zone [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design] arrivals cluster at event end times; cross-link R03 Events
data_source: Event schedules (R03), flight schedules (BTS), MTA service alerts
how_to_model: Batch or Hawkes-process arrivals triggered by scheduled event end, flight arrival and outage times

name: Platform share of city demand
description: The fraction of all city ride demand that reaches the platform the simulated driver or fleet works on.
values_or_range: Uber 73.5%, Lyft 26.5% of HVFHV trips in Jan 2023 [fact-check: confirmed from data, HV0003 13.58M vs HV0005 4.90M trips; earlier '~70-75% [U]' holds]; yellow and green taxis are separate channels; robotaxi operator share is a scenario knob 0.01-0.5
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies, field hvfhs_license_num (HV0003 Uber, HV0005 Lyft), HVFHV Jan 2023
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, field hvfhs_license_num
how_to_model: Thin total demand by platform share before matching; cross-link R06 for competitor capture

name: Induced demand and rider retention
description: Better service (short ETAs, few cancels) brings more requests later, and bad trips drive riders away.
values_or_range: Zone demand multiplier 0.9-1.1 responding to recent ETA [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design]; [corrected by fact-check: Frechette et al. 2019 show increasing returns to scale in taxi matching, which supports density effects but says nothing about rider retention]
how_to_model: Zone demand multiplier tied to moving-average served ETA; rider churn after bad trips

name: Modifier composition and saturation rule
description: How base demand and the hour, day-type, weather, event, holiday and transit-disruption effects are combined (multiplied, added or fitted jointly), and where combined demand is capped.
values_or_range: Modes: (1) product of separately fitted multipliers; (2) one joint negative-binomial GLM on zone x 15-min counts, with main effects plus selected interactions (rain x hour, event x weather, holiday x hour); (3) additive event residual on a multiplicative base. Cap per zone-hour at an observed ceiling (max 1,625 HVFHV pickups per zone-hour, R05-001) or a surge-implied ceiling.
impact_evidence: [design guess] Stacked days (rain + event + holiday) are likely the most profitable scenarios, so the stacking rule sets the biggest payoffs. [P, from list] R04-002 plans a Poisson regression with hour-of-week fixed effects; its only fitted result so far is a daily wet-day regression (Uber +6.3%). [corrected: it was described as already fitted hourly].
data_source: NYC TLC trip records; NOAA hourly weather (LCD); event calendar (R03)
how_to_model: Fit one log-link GLM jointly and validate it on held-out stacked days. Apply the ceiling as a soft cap, and record the composition rule used in each scenario.

name: Re-requests and duplicate requests
description: Whether a rider who is not matched, or whose driver cancels, requests again on the same or another app, and whether one person can hold requests on two apps at once.
values_or_range: After a failed match or a driver cancellation: 40-70% request again on the same app within 5 min, 10-30% switch app, the rest leave [design]. Requests open on two apps at once: 5-15% at peaks [design].
impact_evidence: [P*] HVFHV files hold completed trips only, with no failed or cancelled requests (R05-066); [S] rider multi-homing (R05-023). Without this, the censoring uplift counts some people twice [design].
how_to_model: Riders persist after a failure, with probabilities of requesting again or switching app. When a duplicate request is matched on one app, the other app's request is cancelled, which shows up there as a rider cancellation.

name: Within-day persistence and spatial correlation of demand shocks
description: How much a zone's demand deviation carries over from hour to hour within a day and is shared with nearby zones, on top of the citywide day factor.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023 non-holiday weekdays, zone-hours averaging 20+ trips: a date x hour factor explains 41% of the log-residual variance (0.050 to 0.030), and borough x date x hour explains 48%. The remaining zone residual has autocorrelation 0.35-0.36 at 1 h, 0.28 at 2 h, 0.22-0.23 at 3 h and 0.11-0.13 at 6 h [P, replicated by fact-check]. Poisson noise is about 58-62% of that residual variance, so the underlying shock persists more: about 0.85-0.9 at 1 h, about 0.55 at 3 h and about 0.3 at 6 h [design inference]. Morning (7-10 h) and evening (16-19 h) residuals of the same zone-day correlate 0.22-0.23 [P].
impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file (the critic's method gave 0.40 at 1 h and 0.26 at 3 h; the fact-check's complete-grid version gave 0.35 and 0.22). Persistent shocks are what make watching the first hours worthwhile; R05-002 keeps one zone multiplier per day.
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (pickups by zone, date and hour)
how_to_model: Zone log-multiplier follows an hourly AR(1) process with rho about 0.8-0.85, optionally plus a small zone-day component, a borough x day x hour factor and the citywide day factor, with Poisson arrivals. [Corrected by fact-check: a pure AR(1) at 0.85-0.9 implies 0.61-0.73 at 3 h and 0.38-0.53 at 6 h, above the ~0.55 and ~0.3 implied by the data.] Validate against the autocorrelations above.

name: Destination choice matrix
description: Probability that a request from a given zone at a given hour goes to each destination zone.
values_or_range: 263 x 263 zone matrix (~69k cells) per hour band and day type, very sparse outside Manhattan
impact_evidence: [P*] PULocationID and DOLocationID confirmed in local HVFHV and yellow Parquet files; destination sets where the driver ends up
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (PU/DO zone pairs)
how_to_model: Empirical conditional OD with Bayesian smoothing; gravity-model fallback for sparse pairs

name: Trip distance distribution
description: Spread of trip lengths, from short Midtown hops to long airport and out-of-city runs.
values_or_range: Yellow Oct 2019: mean 3.05 mi, median 1.67 mi, 85% of trips 5 mi or less, 81% both 5 mi or less and fare $18 or less (confirms the '~80%' claim); yellow 2023: mean 3.5 mi, median 1.8 mi, 82% 5 mi or less; HVFHV Jan 2023: mean 4.8 mi, median 2.9 mi, 70% 5 mi or less, p99 ~26 mi [fact-check: all recomputed from TLC files; the earlier [U] means are confirmed]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (yellow Oct 2019 and 2023, HVFHV Jan 2023); [S] NYC Data Science 2019; trip length sets fare per trip versus time between trips
how_to_model: Emerges from OD plus routing; calibrate against empirical distance histograms by hour

name: Directional imbalance by zone and hour
description: Net flow of trips into versus out of each zone, such as morning inflow to Midtown and late-night outflow from bar districts.
values_or_range: Drop-off to pickup ratio 0.3-3 per zone-hour [corrected by fact-check: in HVFHV Jan 2023, weekday zone-hours averaging >=50 pickups/day have a ratio of 0.45-1.45 (5th-95th percentile, IQR 0.78-1.11); values near 0.3 or 3 occur only in small zones, at airports or in event hours]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (PU vs DO counts by zone and hour); imbalance drives deadhead and stranding
how_to_model: Emerges from OD matrix; harness exposes it as a derived heatmap and tracks the agent's deadhead

name: Return-trip coupling (tour chains)
description: People who travel out for a concert, dinner or flight later make a predictable return trip.
values_or_range: P(return by car within 2-8 h) 0.3-0.6 for leisure trips [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design] reverse wave after events; cross-link R03
data_source: none found (infer from paired OD flows in TLC data)
how_to_model: Rider tours home-activity-home, or an event-linked return wave scheduled at event end

name: Exact pickup and drop-off point within a zone
description: Where in a taxi zone the rider actually stands or is dropped, since TLC data gives only zone IDs.
values_or_range: Zones ~0.3-2 mi across [U]; points weighted by buildings, foot traffic and historic GPS [corrected by fact-check: coordinates were dropped from July 2016 onward; yellow and green files up to June 2016 carry GPS points]
impact_evidence: [P*] Schneider nyc-taxi-data README: 'Starting in July 2016, the TLC no longer provides pickup and dropoff coordinates'
data_source: OSM buildings; NYC DOT pedestrian counts (NYC Open Data); pre-2016 yellow GPS points as prior
how_to_model: Sample a point in the zone weighted by address density and historic pickup GPS; snap to curb (cross-link R01)

name: Trip purpose mix
description: Share of requests that are commutes, airport, nightlife, shopping, medical, business or tourism trips, by hour and zone.
values_or_range: All-mode NYC: ~1/5 commute, ~1/7 social, ~1/8 shopping; hidden labels per request
impact_evidence: [S] NYC DOT Citywide Mobility Survey 2017 [uncertain: shares not re-checked, nyc.gov blocked]; purpose drives OD, group size, tips and price sensitivity
data_source: NYC DOT Citywide Mobility Survey reports and microdata https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/downloads/pdf/2024-cms-report.pdf [uncertain: URL not opened]; OSM POIs
how_to_model: Tag each request with purpose from P(purpose | origin and destination land use, hour)

name: Rider segment mix
description: Mix of locals, tourists, business travellers, students, elderly and disabled riders, each with different habits.
values_or_range: US: 36% of adults used ride-hail (2018); 51% of 18-29 vs 24% of 50+; 45% urban; ~35% of New Yorkers use ride-hail [uncertain: NYC figure seen only via secondary coverage of the 2018 NYC DOT Mobility Report]
impact_evidence: [S] Pew Research Jan 2019; [S] NYC DOT Mobility Report 2018 coverage
data_source: Pew Research; NYC DOT Citywide Mobility Survey; US Census ACS
how_to_model: Segment attribute per request with zone and hour priors; segment sets price, wait, tip, luggage and group size parameters

name: Tourist and visitor demand layer
description: Extra demand from visitors around hotels and attractions, varying by season.
values_or_range: 65M visitors in 2025 (52.4M domestic, ~12.3-12.6M international); 66.3M forecast 2026 (World Cup) [uncertain: report not re-opened; business.nyctourism.com unreachable]
impact_evidence: [S] NYC Tourism + Conventions annual report Mar 2026
data_source: NYC Tourism + Conventions reports https://business.nyctourism.com/press-media/press-releases/NYC-Tourism-Annual-Report-March-2026; OSM tourism=hotel
how_to_model: Tourism layer scaled by month and hotel/attraction density; tourists less price-aware, more luggage

name: Commute demand layer
description: Home-to-work and work-to-home trips in AM and PM peaks, strongest where transit is poor.
values_or_range: Weekday peaks 7-10 and 16-19; larger share in outer-borough to Manhattan pairs with poor transit [design guess]
impact_evidence: [S] Hall, Palsson & Price 2018: Uber fills transit gaps and complements transit (+5% ridership after 2 years)
data_source: LEHD LODES OD https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/; US Census ACS journey to work
how_to_model: Commute layer from LODES OD weighted by transit travel-time penalty

name: Nightlife demand layer
description: Late-night demand from bar and club districts, peaking around closing time.
values_or_range: Fri/Sat 22:00-04:00; NYC last call 4 AM [U]; [corrected by fact-check: the earlier 'spike 01:00-04:00' is wrong. In nightlife zones (East Village 79, Lower East Side 148, West Village 249) Sat/Sun HVFHV pickups peak at 00:00-02:00 (~3,500/h for the three zones), are ~2,000 at 03:00 and ~950 at 04:00 (Jan 2023); there is no closing-time spike at 4 AM]
impact_evidence: [U] NY on-premises alcohol sales end 4 AM; [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (HVFHV Jan 2023 hourly profile); also raises mess and incident risk (R05-054)
data_source: NYS Liquor Authority active licenses (data.ny.gov); TLC trips
how_to_model: POI-weighted layer from liquor-licence density, peaking 00:00-02:00 and tapering to 04:00 (fit the shape from TLC hourly counts)

name: Medical and paratransit trips
description: Trips to and from hospitals and clinics, including MTA Access-A-Ride trips sent to app drivers.
values_or_range: access_a_ride_flag trips are a small share (<1%) [corrected by fact-check: no HVFHV trip is flagged in Jan 2023 (Uber leaves the field blank, Lyft reports 'N' on every trip), so the flag cannot measure paratransit volume]; daytime weekday peak [design guess]
impact_evidence: [P*] access_a_ride_flag exists but is empty in Jan 2023 (own calc on local TLC Parquet copies); hospital-trip layer is [design]
data_source: NYC Open Data hospital locations; MTA Access-A-Ride statistics [U]; TLC HVFHV access_a_ride_flag (empty in Jan 2023)
how_to_model: Small daytime layer around hospitals; longer boarding times

name: Student and campus demand
description: Demand around universities that follows the academic calendar (move-in, finals, breaks).
values_or_range: +/-10-30% in campus zones by term vs break [design guess]
impact_evidence: [design] cross-link R02 calendar
how_to_model: Campus-zone multiplier keyed to academic calendar

name: Business traveller and premium demand
description: Weekday travellers from Midtown and Financial District hotels and offices who often choose premium products and care less about price.
values_or_range: Higher premium-product share and lower price elasticity on weekdays [design guess]
impact_evidence: [U] expense-paid riders are less price sensitive
how_to_model: Segment flag that lowers elasticity and raises premium product choice

name: Persistent rider population across days
description: Whether riders are fresh random draws each day or a synthetic population with home and work anchors, repeat commutes and stable traits such as tipping, no-shows and rating.
values_or_range: Fresh draws (default) / a synthetic population in which 20-50% of weekday commute trips repeat [design]; a stable tipper type (R05-047).
impact_evidence: [design] It gives the 10-day learning protocol regular patterns to learn and makes rating or blocking riders (R09-065) meaningful. R05-047 already assumes a persistent tipper type.
data_source: US Census LEHD LODES home-work flows https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/ [U]; NYC Citywide Mobility Survey [U]; TLC records (no rider IDs)
how_to_model: Generate a rider pool per zone with home and work anchors and traits. Each day's demand samples trips from the pool and matches the R05-001 totals.

name: Price elasticity to surge or fare level
description: How much demand falls when the quoted price rises.
values_or_range: Elasticity about -0.5 near 1.2x surge and below 1 in magnitude at higher surges (UberX, 2015, Chicago, LA, NYC, SF) [uncertain: point value comes from course notes; the paper is usually summarised as inelastic demand of roughly -0.4 to -0.6 across surge levels [U]; NBER unreachable]
impact_evidence: [S] Cohen, Hahn, Hall, Levitt & Metcalfe 2016 (NBER w22627), number via Berkeley course notes; demand more inelastic than expected
data_source: Published estimates only (no public NYC data)
how_to_model: Conversion probability as constant-elasticity or logistic function of price multiplier, by segment

name: Sensitivity to quoted pickup ETA
description: How much fewer people request a ride when the app shows a longer wait.
values_or_range: Price elasticities ~4x waiting-time elasticities (ride-hail auctions) [uncertain: ratio not re-read; Buchholz et al. use Prague (Liftago) data, not NYC]; one NYC study claims +1.5 min delay cuts demand ~37% (unverified)
impact_evidence: [S] Buchholz, Doval, Kastl, Matejka & Salz (value of time); [S] Paithankar, Kockelman & Gurumurthy 2026 (not verified)
how_to_model: Multiply conversion by exp(-beta x ETA) per segment; key for fleet positioning

name: Rider cancellation after match
description: Chance that a rider cancels after a driver accepts, rising as the wait drags or the car moves the wrong way.
values_or_range: 5-15% of matched requests [design guess]; many cancels in the first minute; free window ~2 min then fee
impact_evidence: [S] Spare 2019: many cancels come very quickly; [S] Wang, Zhang & Zhang 2024 (Operations Research): long pickups cause cancels [uncertain: citation not located]; [corrected by fact-check: impact lowered from high to medium. At 5-15% of matches and ~2-5 min lost per cancel, partly repaid by fees, the loss is about 1-3% of driver time [design arithmetic]; kept core because cancels feed fleet ETA and conversion]
applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi, fleet, taxi e-hail
data_source: none found (TLC data holds completed trips only)
how_to_model: Hazard model over time since match with ETA-slip term; pays cancel fee per R07 rule

name: Cross-platform price comparison (multi-homing)
description: Riders who check several apps or hail a cab instead when one platform surges.
values_or_range: Share of riders comparing 2+ options 20-50% [design guess]
