impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023: Christmas 2023 had 45% of a normal Monday's yellow trips; NYE night pays +60% per engaged hour [P*]
how_to_model: Harness picks dates from a stratified day-type list; same date and seed across models (common random numbers)

name: Rule-set vintage matched to the replay date
description: The fares, fees, pay floors and caps used must match the date of the demand being replayed, or be a declared counterfactual.
values_or_range: Key dates: taxi fare 18 Dec 2022; HVFHV distance-factor reset 13 Mar 2023; CBD toll 5 Jan 2025; HVFHV floor and access rules 1 Aug 2025; CPI step each 1 March; Green Rides step each 1 Jan; HVFHV wrongful-deactivation law 28 Jul 2026; CRZ step-up 2028 [U] [corrected by fact-check: 'lease caps 2 May 2025' removed; that date is a later amendment to 58-21, not a change in the cap amounts]
impact_evidence: [P*] amendment histories in the rules archive; mismatch can bias revenue by 5-15% [design guess]; cross-link R10-064
how_to_model: Versioned rule tables with effective dates; harness asserts data date and rule date agree

name: Data era
description: Which period's data calibrates demand, prices and speeds.
values_or_range: 2019 (pre-COVID) / 2022-2024 / 2025 onward (after congestion pricing started on 5 Jan 2025)
impact_evidence: [P*] TLC catalog row counts (team R02 data, re-verified): yellow raw rows per day rose from 123,670 (Oct 2024) to 142,861 (Oct 2025); [S via R10] congestion pricing changed CBD speeds, so every module must share one era.
how_to_model: Era tag on every calibrated parameter; mixing eras fails validation.

sub_box: Information ladder and the public vs insider line
name: Calendar awareness given to the agent
description: Whether the agent is told the date, weekday, holiday name and known calendar effects, as an experiment arm like event awareness.
values_or_range: None / weekday+hour only / full calendar incl. holidays / calendar plus historical hourly profile
impact_evidence: [design] mirrors the team's with/without event-info test; holiday and weekday effects of 0.45-1.11x shown in TLC data
how_to_model: System-prompt variants; same world, different information

sub_box: Information ladder and the public vs insider line
name: Traffic information level
description: How much traffic information the agent receives: none, typical map times, live speeds, or live speeds plus incidents and closures.
values_or_range: L0 none / L1 typical times / L2 live speeds / L3 live + incidents + gridlock alerts
impact_evidence: [design] mirrors the team's with/without public event information test
how_to_model: Harness flag selecting which traffic layers enter the observation.

sub_box: Information ladder and the public vs insider line
name: Information level ladder
description: Which public information the agent can query, set as ordered levels so the value of each layer can be measured.
values_or_range: L0 own state and offers only; L1 + map and historical aggregates; L2 + calendar and weather forecast; L3 + public event calendar; L4 + in-app market signals; Oracle = true future demand (upper bound only, never scored)
impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-verified against the script output): zone-hour pay per engaged hour from the six prior non-holiday weekdays correlates 0.84 with the day-11 values (5,528 zone-hours), so L1 already carries most of the learnable spatial signal; event layers matter mainly on event days [design].
data_source: TLC trip records; NOAA/NWS; NYC Open Data events (see data sources)
how_to_model: Each level is a set of enabled query tools; runs at several levels on the same seeds.

sub_box: Information ladder and the public vs insider line
name: Public vs insider boundary rule
description: The written rule for what counts as fair, public input at decision time, for each role.
values_or_range: Allowed: public sources, the driver-app view, own history (a robotaxi operator may also use its own fleet logs). Not allowed: future requests, unserved demand, rival platforms' internal data, the replayed day's own TLC records, realised weather
impact_evidence: [P*] TLC monthly files arrive with about a 2-month lag (the team catalog lists files through Aug 2026 as of mid-Oct 2026; verified), so a real driver never has the day's trip records at the time.
how_to_model: Every tool is tagged allowed or disallowed per role and checked by the harness.

sub_box: Information ladder and the public vs insider line
name: Driver information networks
description: Driver-run chat groups and crowd apps that share airport queue counts, police and tow activity, crashes and venue let-outs in near real time, separate from official alerts and the platform app.
values_or_range: Off, or a noisy community feed: delay 2-15 min, 10-30% of items wrong or stale, covering airports and big venues only [design]. The same feed can also go to 0-50% of rival bots [design].
impact_evidence: [S] Chris Blattman blog (Feb 2016), summarising a New Yorker piece: 'the Drivers Report', a WhatsApp group started by LaGuardia drivers to share airport traffic and demand. [S] The Outline on NYC cabbies' private group chats (title seen only). [S] Gridwise crowdsourced queue counts (R06-040). The size of the edge is a [design guess].
applies_to: human app driver; taxi (sharing inside one's own fleet is R11-016)
data_source: none found (private chats; Gridwise data proprietary). Generate the feed from sim state.
how_to_model: Make feed items from true sim state (queue lengths, incidents, let-outs) with delay, dropout and error. Treat as allowed community information under the public-info rule (R12-021) [design]. Cross the agent's access with the bots' access.

name: TLC timestamp and DST artefacts
description: TLC timestamps are local time without zone, so DST nights create impossible or inflated durations that must be cleaned before calibration.
values_or_range: Fall-back night 2023: 795 of 8,435 trips at 01h with zero/negative duration; spring: 992 trips starting 01h with ~84 min mean duration inflated by the skipped hour [added by fact-check: the yellow 2023 file, whose SHA-256 matches TLC's, is missing about 95% of trips from about 13:00 on 21 Sep to 24 Sep 2023 (4,633-5,732 trips/day vs about 105,000); flag or drop these days]
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
how_to_model: Localize with tz rules, flag ambiguous hour, drop or repair durations before fitting

name: Event residual extraction (calibration)
description: Method to learn event demand signatures from TLC data by subtracting a zone x hour x weekday baseline.
values_or_range: Residual per 15 min within ~2 km of the venue; templates per venue type
impact_evidence: [P*] the calculations in this dossier (US Open, NYE, Broadway, MSG)
data_source: TLC yellow and HVFHV records; Retrosheet; event calendars
how_to_model: Robust baseline (median of the same weekday +/- 4 weeks) and residual templates per venue type

name: TLC data gaps that look like events
description: Missing days in the trip files that look like demand collapses if replayed.
values_or_range: Yellow 2023: Sep 21 at 33% of normal, Sep 22-24 at ~4-5% of normal
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: daily counts of the SHA-256-verified yellow 2023 files
how_to_model: Flag and exclude or impute days below 60% of the same-weekday median unless a known event explains them

name: Weather data join and cleaning rules
description: Rules for turning raw weather files into simulator inputs aligned with trip records.
values_or_range: LCD 'T' = trace precipitation; report types FM-15 (routine hourly), FM-16 (special), SOD (daily summary); LCD exports in metric or imperial units [uncertain: not re-checked; NOAA host blocked]; align to America/New_York local time [P*]
impact_evidence: Public LCD cleaning notebooks [P*]
how_to_model: Pipeline step with unit tests: hourly bins aligned to TLC pickup hour; trace treated as 0.001 in.

name: Latent vs observed demand (censoring)
description: Trip data shows only served trips, so real demand in busy, short-supplied places is higher than the records.
values_or_range: Unserved share 5-20% at peaks [design guess]; zero cancelled requests in TLC files
impact_evidence: [S] Gammelli et al. 2020 censored Gaussian processes; [P*] local HVFHV Parquet schema has no cancel or unserved-request field
how_to_model: Lift demand where supply was tight (long waits, surge) using a censored model; expose uplift as a scenario knob

name: Driver-level behaviour data
description: Datasets with persistent driver IDs, used to fit shift lengths, stopping rules and airport choices.
values_or_range: 2010-2013 NYC yellow trips with hashed medallion and licence IDs (FOIL); Chicago TNP Drivers monthly (trips per driver, MULTIPLE_TNPS).
impact_evidence: Chris Whong used the 2013 FOIL data for airport waits [S]; Chicago dataset documentation [S].
how_to_model: Fit hazard models offline; carry the parameters to 2025 with a drift adjustment.

name: Trip-record cleaning rules
description: Filters applied to TLC records before fitting speeds (bad timestamps, zero distance, impossible speeds).
values_or_range: drop duration under 60 s or over 3 h, speed over 60 mph or under 1 mph, zero distance [design]; in 2023 yellow data these rules remove 1.15% (<60 s), 0.09% (>3 h), 2.02% (zero distance), 0.06% (>60 mph) and 0.18% (<1 mph) of trips [P*]
impact_evidence: Published NYC travel-time studies drop trips under 10 s or over 24 h [S]
how_to_model: Documented filter step in the data pipeline with counts removed per rule.

name: As-of timestamp discipline
description: Every piece of information carries an issue time no later than the sim clock, and the harness enforces it.
values_or_range: Strict (issue time <= now) / lagged (issue time <= now minus the real publication lag)
impact_evidence: [design] look-ahead leakage is a standard failure of backtests and of LLM forecasting evaluations [U].
how_to_model: Data store keyed by (valid time, issue time); unit tests that no tool returns rows issued in the future.

name: Data licence filter
description: Only data whose terms allow use, and ideally redistribution, in a public benchmark may feed the simulator.
values_or_range: Allowed: NYC and NY State open data, US federal data (NOAA, EIA, NLR, formerly NREL), OpenStreetMap (ODbL, share-alike on derived databases), Open-Meteo (data CC BY 4.0; free API non-commercial only). Excluded: Google-Maps-derived travel times, paid feeds (e.g. PredictHQ), scraped app data
impact_evidence: [P] Open-Meteo README: data CC BY 4.0, APIs 'free for open-source developers and non-commercial use', code AGPLv3; [P*] NREL is now the National Laboratory of the Rockies and its developer API moved to developer.nlr.gov (developer.nrel.gov stopped resolving 29 May 2026) [corrected by fact-check]; the other terms are [U] and must be checked on portals that were blocked here.
how_to_model: Licence field in the data catalog; the build fails on unknown licences; ship fitted parameters where raw redistribution is unclear.

name: Supply-constrained bias in fitted weather and event effects
description: Rain, event and holiday uplifts estimated from completed trips understate the real jump in requests, because extra requests in busy hours are capped by the cars available. This applies the censoring in R05-066 to effect estimates; merge candidate with R05-066.
values_or_range: Correction factor 1.0-1.5x on fitted uplifts in tight hours [design]. Diagnostic (HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays): daily trips vs median request-to-pickup wait r = +0.62 raw and +0.81 after removing day-of-week means, so busier days are tighter.
impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check (g1/a7.py plus a de-meaned check): raw 0.62, de-meaned 0.81 (the gap critic had 0.80). Part of the correlation is the post-holiday ramp within January. [S] Brodeur & Nield, IZA DP 9986 (2016) and JEBO 152 (2018): Uber rides per hour about 25% higher in rain vs about 4% for taxis, explained by surge-induced supply. A 2017 working-paper version with Uber data to Dec 2016 reports about 18% vs 5%. [uncertain: which pair the JEBO article reports; snippets conflict and iza.org was unreachable].
data_source: HVFHV request, on-scene and pickup times; NOAA hourly weather
how_to_model: Estimate uplifts with wait-adjusted or censored (Tobit-style) regressions, or back out requests by inverting the sim's matcher. Cross-link R05-066.

name: Sparse cells and smoothing of rates
description: How rate tables estimated from few observations (outer-zone x 15-min demand, pay ratios, travel times) are smoothed, so that noise does not create fake hotspots that the agent learns.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays: 11.3% of zone x hour cells average under 5 trips/h and 5.4% under 1 (counting all 263 zones; 10.6% and 4.7% over the 261 zones with any trip). 48.6% of the ~55.6k observed OD pairs average under 1 trip/day. Methods: empirical-Bayes pooling toward borough-hour means, neighbour averaging, gravity fallback. OD smoothing is already in R05-006; R10-062 uses OD neighbour averaging for travel times.
impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check on the local HVFHV file (55,618 OD pairs vs the critic's 55,974; shares agree within 0.1 point). [P, from list] R05-006 (Bayesian OD smoothing) and R10-062 (neighbour averaging of travel times).
how_to_model: Shrinkage estimator per table, with a documented prior and strength. Test that a model with memory gains nothing from cells that smoothing removes.

name: Demand timestamp basis (request vs pickup time)
description: Whether demand is fitted on request time (app trips only) or pickup time (all trips; yellow taxis have no request time), and how taxi demand is shifted back to request time.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: request-to-pickup median 3.85 min and p90 7.92 min (Uber 3.72/7.42, Lyft 4.22/9.80). Binned by request time instead of pickup time, 30.6% of trips fall in a different 15-min bin and 7.7% in a different hour [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check]. on_scene_datetime is filled for 13.59M of 18.48M trips, essentially Uber only [P]. Yellow has no request time: street hails are close to pickup time, and e-hails need an imputed wait [design].
impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file (18,479,031 trips, request_datetime filled for all). Fitting on pickup time moves let-out waves and rush peaks later by the wait.
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
how_to_model: Fit app demand on request_datetime; for yellow, use pickup time for hails. Check that simulated waits reproduce the observed pickup-time profile.

name: Population sampling fraction and density scaling
description: Whether the simulator runs all riders and background cars in the agent's area or only a sample, and if a sample, how the matching radius, queues and road capacity are rescaled.
values_or_range: 100% / 25% / 10% sample [design]. With cars placed at random, the distance to the nearest idle car scales with 1/sqrt(density), so a 10% sample gives about 3.2x longer pickups unless rescaled. Real data are much flatter across places: across weekday zone-hours, the elasticity of the median Uber on-scene ETA to trips per hour is about -0.03 to -0.10 depending on controls (pooled -0.08, within hour of day -0.09, within borough x hour -0.03) [P]. The median of zone-hour medians is about 3.3-3.9 min on Staten Island vs 2.0-2.3 min in Manhattan, depending on the minimum-trips filter [P; corrected by fact-check, was 3.45 vs 2.12, which is one filter choice]. Within the same zone and hour of day, busier days have LONGER waits (elasticity about +0.2), because demand shocks drain idle cars [P, added by fact-check].
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays, Uber trips (on-scene time is filled for Uber rows only). [S] Frechette, Lizzeri & Salz 2019 (AER 109(8)): increasing returns in taxi matching (via R05-042). [U] MATSim rescales flow and storage capacity for sampled runs. R11-068 covers runtime only. The cross-sectional slope mixes density with supply response, so it is a calibration target, not a causal density law.
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime and on_scene_datetime; Uber rows only)
how_to_model: Prefer full density in the agent's region. If sampling, shrink map distances by sqrt(f) or rescale the matcher. Require a calibration test showing that pickup ETA vs demand matches BOTH the cross-sectional TLC slope and the positive within-zone-hour slope.

sub_box: With vs without public info (events, weather, incidents)

values_or_range: Off / mention only / mention plus event-calendar tool

sub_box: With vs without public info (events, weather, incidents)
name: Weather forecast as issued
description: The forecast the agent sees must be the one published before the decision, never the weather that actually happened.

sub_box: With vs without public info (events, weather, incidents)
name: Public event calendar content

values_or_range: None / NYC permitted events (name, type, borough, location, start and end, street closure; about one month of lead time) / + ticketed venues (MSG, Barclays, Yankee Stadium, Citi Field, USTA) / + pre-event attendance estimates
impact_evidence: [S via GitHub copies of the Socrata metadata] NYC Permitted Event Information (tvpp-9vvx) lists approved events 'that will occur within the next month', with 13 columns (event id, name, start and end, agency, type, borough, location, street side, closure type, community board, police precinct, CEMS id); ticketed events on private property are generally not street permits, so they need venue schedules [corrected by fact-check: scope and columns added]; the most frequent event types are youth and adult sports permits and farmers markets [S], so filtering for large events matters (cross-link R03).

sub_box: With vs without public info (events, weather, incidents)
name: News, alerts and incident feed
description: Time-stamped public alerts the agent may read: traffic incidents, subway outages, severe-weather warnings, news headlines.

impact_evidence: [S, GitHub copies of the 511NY developer docs] the 511NY developer API gives incidents and events; it needs a developer key and is throttled to 10 calls per 60 s (verified); subway disruptions push riders into cars [U] (cross-link R03, R05).

name: Weather replay vs synthetic generator, and seeds (see R03-064)
description: Whether a scenario replays the real weather of a historical day (matched to its TLC demand) or uses generated weather, and how weather randomness is shared across runs. Pair with the R03-064 memorisation guard.
values_or_range: Replay (realistic; models may remember famous days such as Ida) / stochastic (Markov chain on hourly classes fitted to Central Park) / hybrid; same weather seed for all models in a comparison [design]

name: Demand source mode
description: Whether riders come from an exact historical day, a resample of it, a fitted generator, or a hybrid.
values_or_range: Exact replay / bootstrap resample / parametric synthetic / replay plus perturbation
impact_evidence: [U] TLC records hold completed trips only, so replay caps demand at served trips (cross-link R05-069, R05-066); [P] tabmemcheck README shows GPT-4 completing random rows of Iris and GPT-3.5 completing Titanic and UCI Wine rows, so exact replay of well-known data invites recall.
how_to_model: Generator fitted per zone x hour of week with day effects; exact replay kept for validation.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Rival visibility
description: What the agent can see about other cars: nothing, a busy or surge heat map, airport queue counts, or live rival positions.
values_or_range: None | heat map (as in driver apps) | queue counts | full positions (unrealistic).
impact_evidence: Uber app shows queue position and drivers ahead at JFK [S]; driver apps do not show rivals' cars [U].
how_to_model: Observation levels in the API; realistic default = surge or busy heat map plus own queue position.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Cost and vehicle-state information shown to the agent
description: Which cost and vehicle data the agent can see: fuel or charge level, live fuel and charging prices, charger queues, maintenance warnings, cost per mile.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Demand forecast given to the fleet controller
description: The demand outlook supplied to the model at each call.
values_or_range: none / historical mean by zone and hour / noisy forecast / oracle (true future requests).
impact_evidence: fleetsim: an oracle forecast gave the same wait as the historical mean but ordered 20-30% more moves and empty miles [S].

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state

values_or_range: None (world knowledge only) / zone list with names and adjacency / + travel-time matrix tool / + points of interest (airports, venues, hospitals, chargers)

how_to_model: Map tools backed by the R01/R10 engine.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: In-app market signals
description: What a real driver app would show: surge or bonus heatmap, busy areas, airport queue length.

impact_evidence: [U] Uber and Lyft driver apps show surge heatmaps and airport queues; the surge rules and queues are R06/R07, showing them is an information choice [design]; the high rating is a design judgement because the signal reveals current local demand.
data_source: none found (platform data is not public; the simulator generates the signal from its own state)
how_to_model: Render from the simulator's matching state with display lag and spatial coarsening.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Own-history log access
description: Whether the agent can query a structured log of its own past trips, earnings and idle spells, beyond its own notes.
values_or_range: None / current shift / all earlier days in the run

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Agent-visible history consistent with the sim's demand
description: Whether the historical summaries shown to the agent are raw TLC numbers, or come from the same pipeline (censoring uplift, smoothing, era) that generates the sim's demand.
values_or_range: Options: raw TLC aggregates / pipeline-consistent aggregates from non-test days (default) / the generator's exact rates (unrealistically perfect, close to an oracle) [design].
