how_to_model: Compute the agent's history by running the sim's demand generator on held-out days, or apply the same uplift and smoothing to raw data. Log which version each arm uses.

sub_box: What the agent sees: history, app signals and own state
name: Price-checking zones in the public rider app
description: Drivers open the public rider app to see the quoted price, pickup ETA and nearby car icons for a zone before deciding whether to move there.
values_or_range: Settings: off / quote plus ETA for any zone, 1-3 min stale with +/-10-20% noise / capped at N checks per hour [design]. Car icons on rider apps are approximate [U].
impact_evidence: [U] described in driver guides and forums. It is a public, legal reading of local surge and supply that R12-019 (driver-app signals) does not cover [design].
applies_to: human app driver; taxi (to read app competition); fleet operator (watching competitor prices)
data_source: none (generated from the simulator's own matching state)
how_to_model: Tool rider_quote(zone) returns a price multiplier and ETA from the sim state with delay, coarsening and noise. Each call costs simulated seconds and counts against the tool budget (R12-028).

name: Data release lag and contamination
description: TLC posts data about two months after the month ends, and models may already know past dates, which matters for fair 'public info only' tests.
values_or_range: Lag ~2 months [U] [uncertain: TLC page unreachable; the checksum catalog lists files to Aug 2026, consistent with a lag of about two months]; replay dates before vs after model knowledge cutoff
impact_evidence: [U] lag per repo catalog note; [design] contamination concern
how_to_model: Tag each replay date relative to each model's cutoff; optionally shift dates or perturb

name: Memorisation guard for real events
description: Controls that stop a model from using pretraining memory of famous real events in the no-information arm.
values_or_range: Date shift (present 2023 as an unnamed year), renamed venues and events, injected synthetic events, held-out dates after the model's cutoff
impact_evidence: [design] validity requirement; complements R12-046 (contamination probes)
how_to_model: Scenario obfuscation layer; check the no-information arm on days with events removed

name: Counterfactual event injection
description: Adding synthetic events to quiet replay days, or removing real ones, so the true event effect is known.
values_or_range: 0-5 injected events a day, 1k-80k attendance
impact_evidence: [design]
how_to_model: Add event-demand residual templates learned from TLC to baseline demand

name: Out-of-NYC event scenario (Coachella-style)
description: A portable event module for a festival town with no public trip data, to test whether event skill generalises.
values_or_range: Coachella: Empire Polo Club, Indio CA, two April weekends, ~125k a day, rideshare lot with long waits [U]; alternative calibration: Chicago TNP trips plus Lollapalooza [U] [uncertain: Coachella site, dates and capacity not re-checkable this session]
data_source: Chicago Transportation Network Providers - Trips (data.cityofchicago.org m6dm-c72p; ID S via the City of Chicago developer blog on GitHub; later years may sit in a successor table, uncertain)
how_to_model: Synthetic town graph plus event templates from NYC and Chicago residuals

name: City rule pack (generalisation beyond NYC)
description: Swappable bundle of fare, fee, pay-floor and hailing rules so the same engine can run other cities.
values_or_range: NYC default; stubs for e.g. Seattle and Minnesota per-mile/per-minute floors, California Prop 22 engaged-time guarantee, Chicago ground-transport tax [U]; Seattle local rule requiring a human driver in AVs [S]
impact_evidence: [design]; values for other cities not verified this session [U]; [S] Vital City (Seattle AV rule)
how_to_model: Config files per city with the same schema as the NYC tables

name: Seeds and common random numbers
description: Separate random streams per component so every model faces the same riders, traffic and shocks.
values_or_range: One seed per scenario with streams for demand, travel time, rider behaviour, rivals and shocks; optional antithetic pairs
impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays (re-verified): daily trips vary with CV 12.4% but pay per engaged hour only 1.4%, so unpaired day draws would swamp model gaps of a few percent; [P* via D11] CEO-Bench uses independent RNGs per simulator component. Impact is on ranking reliability, not on expected profit.
how_to_model: Streams keyed by (component, entity, period); the same seed list for every model.

name: Runs per model and statistical power
description: How many seeds and repeats per model and scenario are needed to separate models.
values_or_range: 5-100 runs per model; report means, paired differences and clustered confidence intervals
impact_evidence: [S via D11, inference] observed run-to-run CVs of 0.07-1.0 in business sims mean 5 unpaired runs detect only gaps of about 0.12-1.8x the mean (about 1.77 x CV at 80% power) [corrected by fact-check: was 0.35-1.8x, which is the CV 0.2 to 1.0 range]; [P] Anthropic: clustered standard errors 'can be over three times as large as naive standard errors'; use power analysis. Impact is on ranking reliability, not on expected profit.
how_to_model: Pilot on a dev model to estimate variance, then size the run count by power analysis.

name: Scenario day-type mix
description: Weights of ordinary, weekend, holiday, rain or snow, event and shock days in the test pool.
values_or_range: e.g. 50% ordinary weekdays, 20% weekends, 10% holidays, 10% bad weather, 10% big-event days
impact_evidence: [P] own computation (re-verified): HVFHV pay per engaged hour was $72.15 on 1 Jan 2023 (holiday, median wait 6.05 min) vs about $54 on ordinary weekdays, so the mix shifts absolute levels.
data_source: TLC trip records; NOAA weather; NYC permitted events
how_to_model: Stratified scenario sampler; scores reported per stratum and pooled with fixed weights.

name: Date and identity masking
description: Hiding the real date, and optionally the real zone names, so the model cannot recall what happened on that day.
values_or_range: Real date / weekday and season only / shifted year / renamed or mirrored zones
impact_evidence: [P] tabmemcheck (Bordt et al., 'Elephants Never Forget', COLM 2024): GPT-3.5/4 completed rows of famous public tables; [S] NYC taxi data is heavily reused, e.g. the Kaggle 'New York City Taxi Trip Duration' competition data reappears in public code [fact-check: was U], so recall of specific days is plausible but untested.
how_to_model: Masking layer renames dates and, in an anonymised track, zones; a real-name track keeps credit for legitimate world knowledge.

name: Post-cutoff fresh test months
description: Test scenarios built from TLC months published after each model's training cutoff.
values_or_range: Test months at least one month after the model cutoff; refreshed every season
impact_evidence: [P] the TLC Jan 2023 files used here are byte-identical (SHA-256 recomputed by fact-check) to the TLC originals in the team catalog, which lists months through Aug 2026 by Oct 2026, so new months keep arriving with about a 2-month lag.
how_to_model: Pipeline pulls each new month, refits the generator and adds a fresh test season.

name: Private hold-out pool, canary and contamination probes
description: Keeping test seeds private, marking files so they are kept out of training data, and testing models for recall before scoring.
values_or_range: Public development seeds / private test seeds; canary GUID in every file; probes asking for the scenario day's weather, trip counts and event outcomes
impact_evidence: [P via D10] AppWorld ships encrypted test bundles with a canary string; [S via D08] ARC Prize calls its API-evaluated set 'semi-private' because of leakage risk; [P] tabmemcheck provides header, row, feature completion and first-token tests.
how_to_model: Private seed list held by maintainers; probe suite run per model; flagged days dropped.

name: Difficulty preset and noise scale
description: Bundled settings from easy to hard, plus a multiplier on randomness.
values_or_range: Easy: Manhattan only, deterministic travel times, no rivals, full information / Medium: whole city, stochastic travel, bot drivers / Hard: shocks, EV range, fatigue, difficult riders; noise scale 0-1.5x calibrated
impact_evidence: [P via D11] CEO-Bench exposes competitor strength as a difficulty knob; [P] tomslee/ridehail ships village / town / city presets (plus game and game-big); [P] own computation: real zone-hour day-to-day error is WAPE about 0.12 for a plain 19-weekday mean [corrected by fact-check: a reference level, not a proven floor].
how_to_model: Preset files over module switches; leaderboard per preset.

name: Generalisation city
description: Running the same agent in another city to test transfer beyond NYC knowledge.
values_or_range: NYC (default) / Chicago (TNP trips; taxi trips with anonymised taxi ID) / synthetic grid city
impact_evidence: [S via GitHub copies] Chicago publishes TNP trips (m6dm-c72p, 2018-2022; n26f-ihde, 2023-2024) and taxi trips (wrvz-psew, 2013-2023; ajtu-isnz, 2024 onward) [corrected by fact-check: the cited tables are closed series; newer IDs added]; [S] the Chicago taxi table carries a taxi_id column (GitHub schema copies; was U), allowing the shift reconstruction NYC data no longer permits.
how_to_model: City pack (map, zones, demand, rules) behind the same interfaces.

name: Solo vs shared-city arena mode
description: Whether each model drives alone among scripted bots, or several models drive in one city at once and compete for riders.
values_or_range: Solo plus bots / arena with 2-5 models, seat rotation and mirrored seeds
impact_evidence: [P* via D11] Vending-Bench Arena: agents sharing one location formed price cartels; [S via R06/D07] rankings differ from solo play (cross-link R06-060) [uncertain: D07's fact-check found mixed evidence; Andon says Claude models were historically worse in multiplayer, but its Arena page shows Claude winning rounds 2, 4 and 6 of the first six].
how_to_model: Arena scheduler rotates start zones and seeds; scores per seat and pooled.

name: Shared day-level shock across modules
description: One hidden day-and-area factor that moves demand, travel speed, rider waits and surge together, instead of separate random draws in each module. It couples R05-002 (demand overdispersion) and R10-009 (day-level slowdowns).
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays, day-of-week means removed: trips vs median wait r = +0.81; trips vs Manhattan-internal speed r = -0.86; wait vs speed r = -0.86 (raw: +0.62, -0.68, -0.79). Modes: independent draws / one shared factor with a loading per module / Gaussian copula.
impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check: all six correlations reproduced within 0.01 (speed = Manhattan-internal miles / trip time). Only 20 days are used, and part of the correlation is the post-holiday ramp within January (trips rose from 478k on 3 Jan to 701k on 27 Jan); validate on more months. [corrected: impact high -> medium. R12-040 finds pay per engaged hour varies only 1.4% across these days, so the shock moves volume, waits and variance more than profit per hour. Its effect on profit per online hour is unmeasured].
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9
how_to_model: Draw a latent daily factor z ~ N(0,1) per area: demand x exp(a z), speed x exp(-b z), bot log-on x exp(c z). Fit the loadings on several months, and seed z in the common-random-number stream (R12-040).

name: Tie-breaking and deterministic execution
description: A seeded rule for equal-ETA or simultaneous claims on one request, deterministic tie-breaks in batched assignment, and no dependence on thread order or floating-point quirks.
values_or_range: Tie rule: seeded random / rotate by seat / lowest car ID (to avoid) [design]. The same seed and the same actions must give an identical log [design].
impact_evidence: [design] Without it, the same seed does not reproduce a run and arena seats (R12-049) get hidden advantages. It affects ranking reliability and common random numbers (R12-040) rather than expected profit.
how_to_model: Resolve ties with a seeded draw per request from a dedicated random stream, iterate in sorted order everywhere, and have a CI test re-run a seed and diff the event log.

name: Warm-up and starting state of the background world
description: A burn-in period, or a start from replayed in-progress trips, so that bots, airport queues, open requests and surge are in a steady state when the agent starts.
values_or_range: Burn-in of 2-4 h of simulated time before the agent enters [design], or start from the trips in progress at t0 and historical airport queue lengths. JFK taxi holding-lot waits have been reported at about 2-3 h (R06-041, NBC New York) [S] [uncertain: R01-052 flags the figure as not re-checked].
impact_evidence: [design] Starting with empty queues and idle bots hands the agent free airport fares and easy offers in the first hours. R11-005 and R11-006 set only the agent's own fleet.
data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trips in progress at t0)
how_to_model: Run the world with bots only from t0 minus the burn-in, then insert the agent, checking queue lengths and idle shares against hour-of-day targets at that point.

name: Side-channel leakage audit
description: Checks that hidden state does not leak through the harness: sequential request IDs, wake-up triggers, error messages, tool latency, offer order, log timestamps, or heat maps built from the true hidden rates.
values_or_range: Pass or fail for each channel: random opaque IDs, wake-ups only on events the public could see, uniform error text, constant tool latency, and heat maps built from observed rather than true demand [design].
impact_evidence: [design] Even with strict as-of rules (R12-022), a request-ID counter can reveal total demand, and an event-triggered wake-up can reveal an incident before the public would know.
how_to_model: An audit script compares what the agent sees across seeds that differ only in hidden state; any difference flags a leak.

name: Time compression and day-night lighting
description: How fast simulated time runs in the live map and how lighting follows the sun for the social-media visualisation.
values_or_range: Speed-up 60x-1440x; lighting from sun elevation (civil dusk to dawn)
impact_evidence: [design] from team visualisation notes
how_to_model: Renderer maps sim clock to frame time; sky colour from sun elevation

name: Event visual overlays
description: Map overlays that show events, closures and alerts in the live visualisation.
values_or_range: Venue pulse sized by attendance; closure polygons; subway status ticker
impact_evidence: [design]
how_to_model: Render event objects on the map timeline

name: Weather and daylight rendering on the live map
description: Showing rain, snow, fog, floods and night lighting on the live map so clips show why earnings jumped.
values_or_range: Rain/snow overlay, fog dimming, night lighting by sun elevation, flooded links highlighted [design]
impact_evidence: [design]; team notes on night/day cycle and clippable visuals
data_source: Simulator weather state; astral sun elevation
how_to_model: Visualiser reads the same weather state as the simulator.

name: Sub-trip position trace
description: Second-by-second position along the route, needed for the live map and for meter time and distance accounting.
values_or_range: tick 1-10 s of simulated time [design]
impact_evidence: [design] team notes ask for a live map with moving cars and sped-up time
how_to_model: Interpolate along the route polyline using edge-level times and emit positions to the visualiser.

name: Fleet visual encoding
description: How the live map shows fleet cars: colour by model, status, revenue ticker and own-car density against demand.
values_or_range: 5 statuses (busy, idle, repositioning, charging, out of service); 1-5 model colours.
impact_evidence: [design]; visualisation plan in the meeting notes.
how_to_model: The event log feeds a map layer; time-lapse with day and night shading.

name: Vehicle state log for the live map
description: The per-vehicle, per-tick record the visualisation reads.
values_or_range: Vehicle id, model id, timestamp, lon/lat, heading, status (P1 / P2 / P3 / charging / offline), battery or fuel, cumulative revenue, costs and net; event markers
impact_evidence: [P] deck.gl TripsLayer (MIT) animates trips from per-trip path and timestamps arrays coloured by a categorical attribute (vendor); its demo view is centred on New York (-74, 40.72) (verified in app.tsx).
how_to_model: Simulator emits path plus timestamps per vehicle segment and a ledger stream.

name: Playback speed, lighting and clip export
description: How fast simulated time plays on screen, how day and night are shown, and how clips are cut for social media.
values_or_range: 1 sim-hour = 10-60 s; trail length; sun-position lighting vs fixed; automatic clips around surges, storms and event egress
impact_evidence: [P] deck.gl trips example defaults (verified): loopLength 1800, trailLength 180, fixed ambient light plus one point light with no time of day; sun position from the NOAA solar calculator [S via sibling dossier].
how_to_model: Renderer maps the sim clock to light level; clip exporter keyed on the event log.

name: Model colour coding and live revenue overlay
description: Visual encoding that lets viewers follow each model's cars and money in real time.
values_or_range: One colour per model (colour-blind-safe palette); per-model revenue and net-profit tickers; leaderboard panel
impact_evidence: [design] team visual plan; [P] TripsLayer colours trips by a categorical attribute (vendor in the example).
how_to_model: Colour map from the run manifest; overlay reads the ledger stream.

name: Replay and audit log
description: Everything needed to re-simulate and audit a run.
values_or_range: Seeds, config hashes, model ids, every observation, tool call, response and token count, ledger entries
impact_evidence: [P via D10] reproducibility comes from re-simulating a logged action stream because LLM sampling is not deterministic: [P] batch_invariant_ops README: 'out of 1000 random length 100 completions we see 18 unique samples' with vLLM, and one after the batch-invariant fix [uncertain: that the requests used an identical prompt is implied, not stated; model not named].
how_to_model: Append-only JSONL per run plus a sealed scoring step.

name: Event-window scoring metrics
description: Measures of how well the agent used event information.
values_or_range: Profit per hour overall; profit within +/- 2 h and 2 km of let-outs; value of information = L1 - L0; information-use efficiency = (L1 - L0)/(L3 - L0)
impact_evidence: [design]; event-window version of R12-061 (information-value metric)
how_to_model: Tag each trip with its event window; report per arm with paired seeds

name: Emissions and carbon accounting (optional)
description: Optional score term for CO2 from fuel and electricity, to test green goals or Green Rides compliance.
values_or_range: Gasoline about 8.9 kg CO2 per gallon [P*: EPA tailpipe CO2 x combined mpg gives a median 8,880 g/gal across 2,960 gasoline models from 2015 on]; NYC grid about 0.25-0.35 kg CO2 per kWh [U] [uncertain: EPA eGRID's NYC/Westchester subregion (NYCW) is recalled at about 0.40 kg/kWh because in-city generation is mostly gas, while the NY state average is nearer 0.2-0.25; read eGRID before use]; carbon price $0-200 per tonne [design].
impact_evidence: [U] EPA emission factors; gasoline factor [P*].
data_source: EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub https://www.epa.gov/climateleadership/ghg-emission-factors-hub [U]; EPA eGRID https://www.epa.gov/egrid [U]
how_to_model: Emissions per mile by powertrain; optional penalty in the score.

name: Reference rebalancing baselines
description: Non-LLM fleet policies run on the same scenarios to anchor model scores.
values_or_range: no repositioning; greedy nearest dispatch; proportional LP (Pavone-style); model predictive control; a published RL policy.
impact_evidence: AMoDeus ships about ten unit-capacity dispatch and rebalancing algorithms plus four ride-sharing ones (GPL-2.0, LICENSE.txt checked) [P, README]; FleetPy ships Alonso-Mora, Pavone and linear-hailing repositioning modules (MIT) [P, code: src/misc/init_modules.py re-read by fact-check]; FleetPy's optimisation modules use Gurobi, free only under an academic licence [P, README, added by fact-check].
how_to_model: Port 2-3 baselines into the harness; report model profit as a % of the best baseline at the same N.

name: Fleet objective function
description: What the fleet is scored on.
values_or_range: total profit / profit per car / profit with a service floor (e.g. served at least 95%, p90 wait at most 10 min) / weighted profit and service.
impact_evidence: fleetsim: raising its fairness weight cut unserved requests from 9.66% to 8.17% but raised median wait from 9.0 to 16.9 min [S], so the best policy flips with the objective.
how_to_model: Harness scoring function; robotaxi own-app mode includes a service floor, platform-driver mode scores profit only.

name: Fleet KPI panel
description: Standard fleet statistics reported beside profit.
values_or_range: utilisation, trips per car-day, empty-mile share, riders served, wait p50 and p90, charging deadhead, availability, compute cost.
impact_evidence: fleetsim and offpeak report these [S]; Waymo about 20 trips per car-day (R06-057) [S].
how_to_model: Harness logs per car per minute and summarises per run.

name: Scale ladder and normalisation
description: Running the same model at several fleet sizes and against baselines, to separate skill from scale.
values_or_range: N in {1, 10, 100}; score = profit / best-baseline profit at the same N.
impact_evidence: [design].
how_to_model: Harness sweep; plot profit per car against N for each model.

name: Passive and random floor baselines
description: Simple policies that set the score floor.
values_or_range: Passive: stay where dropped and accept every offer; random repositioning; for taxis, random cruising
impact_evidence: [P via D10, README re-read] ABC checklist: 'A trivial do-nothing agent scores 38% pass@k and pass^k' on tau-bench (a benchmark flaw since fixed), so floors must be measured before claiming skill; impact is on the normalised score because the passive run is the floor.
how_to_model: Scripted policies run on every seed; the passive score is the normalisation floor.

name: Heuristic baselines
description: Rule-based strategies a competent human might use.
values_or_range: Heatmap follower (go to the best historical zone-hour); surge chaser; taxi rules (Manhattan core and airports, head back after outer-borough drop-offs); go home at the end
impact_evidence: [P] own computation: zone-hour pay ranks are stable day to day (r = 0.84), so a heatmap follower should be a strong baseline; [design]. [corrected by fact-check: impact was high; a reference baseline does not change the agent's profit or the normalised score unless used as the normalisation anchor]
how_to_model: Scripted policies that use only allowed information.

name: Operations-research planner baseline
description: An optimisation policy that plans on expected demand without seeing the future.
values_or_range: Single car: dynamic programming over zone x 5-min time on expected earnings; fleet: min-cost flow or batched bipartite matching with rebalancing
impact_evidence: [S via R01] Buchholz (2022, Review of Economic Studies) models NYC taxi search as a dynamic spatial equilibrium; [U] MDP methods for taxi driver revenue (e.g. Rong et al., CIKM 2016). [corrected by fact-check: impact was high; a reference baseline not used for normalisation does not change the measured profit]
how_to_model: Solver reads the generator's expected rates and re-plans every 5 sim-min.

name: Hindsight oracle
description: The best achievable profit on the realised day with perfect knowledge of every request, used as the score ceiling.
values_or_range: Exact longest path over a time-expanded graph (single car); ILP or min-cost flow (fleet); approximations for long horizons
impact_evidence: [P via D11] Magentic Marketplace reports an 'Optimal (theoretical upper bound)' and Supply_Chain_Bench scores against reference policies including a best-found feasible one; [design]; impact is on the normalised score because the oracle is the ceiling.
how_to_model: Computed offline per seed after the run; never shown to agents.

name: Human reference
description: How people do, from players using the same interface and from real driver earnings.
values_or_range: Expert NYC drivers or trained players on the UI (5 or more); real-world anchor: HVFHV driver pay about $54 per engaged (passenger-on-board) hour (weekdays, Jan 2023) before idle time, the drive to pickups and costs
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 had one human (5 h, $844.05) who beat every model's worst run (best model minimum $476; verified); [P] own computation of pay per engaged hour from TLC driver_pay and trip_time.
how_to_model: Human UI over the same tool API at the same information level.

name: Learned RL baseline
description: A policy trained by reinforcement learning on the simulator, which shows how hard and how exploitable the world is.
values_or_range: Tabular Q-learning over zone x time, or deep RL (PPO); trained on development seeds only
impact_evidence: [P] LPSim provides a 'Gymnasium environment wrapper for training dispatch/pricing policies' (verified); [U] RL dispatch is used in production ride-hailing. [corrected by fact-check: impact was medium; a stretch reference policy not used for scoring]
how_to_model: Gymnasium wrapper around the simulator; evaluated on private seeds.

name: Headline metric
description: The single number used for ranking.
values_or_range: Net profit per online hour after all costs (fuel or energy, maintenance, depreciation, insurance, tolls, fees, commission); fleet: net profit per vehicle-hour and in total
impact_evidence: [P] own computation: citywide HVFHV pay per engaged hour is stable (CV 1.4%), so profit per online hour mostly measures utilisation and positioning, the skills under test; [design] team goal.
how_to_model: Ledger computes net profit; online hours come from the status log.

name: Normalisation and aggregation
description: How profits from different scenarios are combined into one score with uncertainty.
values_or_range: Per scenario (agent - passive) / (oracle - passive); aggregate with the interquartile mean and stratified-bootstrap CIs; per-family profiles
impact_evidence: [P via D11] IQM with stratified-bootstrap CIs (rliable, Agarwal et al. NeurIPS 2021) recommended for business sims; [P] day levels differ ($72 holiday vs $54 weekday per engaged hour), so raw dollars are not comparable across days.
how_to_model: Scoring script runs after runs are sealed.

name: Risk and consistency panel
description: Measures of bad days and reliability shown next to the mean.
values_or_range: CVaR of daily profit (worst 10-20% of seeds), worst run, SD across seeds, stranding rate (battery or fuel out), pass^k (all k runs beat the human median)
impact_evidence: [P via D11] tau-bench's pass^k; [P*] Vending-Bench 1: Claude 3.5 Sonnet's worst run was $476 against a mean of $2,217.93 (verified).
how_to_model: Computed from per-run ledgers.

name: Compliance, safety and service panel
description: Penalties and side metrics for rule-breaking and for how riders are served.
values_or_range: TLC rule violations (taxi refusals, hours-of-service, illegal stopping), unsafe instructions, discriminatory declines; acceptance and cancellation rates; outer-borough service share; rider wait (fleet); for a fleet or robotaxi operator only, an optional Manhattan-core cruising-cap toggle
impact_evidence: [P via D11] Business Arena logs fines and violations and conduct panels are standard in business sims; the rules themselves are R07. [corrected by fact-check: the HVFHS cruising cap (35 RCNY 59D-21, at most 31% of available time cruising below 96th St) binds app companies, not drivers, and was reported annulled by a state court in Dec 2019 [U]; the 2025 access rules (59D-22(c)) also bind platforms]
data_source: Rules of the City of New York Title 35 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive (see R07)
how_to_model: Rule engine scans the event log; severe violations disqualify, others deduct.

name: Efficiency diagnostics
description: A breakdown of how time and miles were used.
values_or_range: P1 / P2 / P3 time shares, empty miles per paid mile, trips per hour, average wait for the next offer
impact_evidence: [P] tomslee/ridehail's P1/P2/P3 split; [S via R10] about 41% of FHV time in Manhattan below 96th Street was without a passenger in 2019; the TLC's cruising definition counts the drive to a pickup as cruising, so this is P1 + P2 [fact-check note].
how_to_model: Computed from the status log and shown on the dashboard.

name: Information-value metric
description: The profit difference caused by giving one more layer of information, on the same seeds.
values_or_range: profit(level k) - profit(level k-1) per model and day type; event-day subset for the event arm
impact_evidence: [design] team plan to test with vs without event information; paired design per Anthropic's evaluation guidance [P].
how_to_model: Paired runs across information levels, reported per model.

name: Jackpot-trip variance and luck-adjusted scoring
description: How the score handles rare high-value trips that dominate a single day's profit, for example by subtracting a baseline run on the same seed (control variate) or by scoring the expected value of the trips offered.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: the top 1% of trips by driver pay (>= $68.72) earn 5.5% of all pay; the top 5% (>= $43.04) earn 17.7%; 0.27% of trips pay >= $100; 91% of top-1% trips touch an airport or leave NYC. Mean pay is $17.05 per trip (median $12.81), so at ~20-25 trips a day one $100 trip is about 23-29% of daily pay. Methods: none / paired baseline on the same seed / control variate on offered-trip value / both.
impact_evidence: [P] Own re-run on HVFHV Jan 2023 (18.19M trips with pay; g1/a7.py), repeated in this fact-check. [corrected: share of daily pay was 15-25%]. Trips per day [U]. [U] Control variates are standard (Law & Kelton).
applies_to: all; matters most for single-car runs (a fleet averages over N cars)
how_to_model: Log the value of every offered trip. Score = profit - beta x (offered jackpot value - its expectation), with beta fitted across runs. Report raw and adjusted scores.

name: Real vs nominal dollars
description: Whether fares, costs and profits from scenarios in different years are converted to one price year before scores are pooled.
values_or_range: Options: nominal / deflated to a base year with CPI-U (New York-Newark-Jersey City) / normalised per scenario only (R12-057). NY-area CPI-U rose about 20% from 2019 to 2024 (2019 annual 278.2; 2024 mean of monthly values 334.2). The US city average rose about 23% [U]. TLC pay factors are re-indexed each March by NY-NJ-PA CPI-W (R07-028).
impact_evidence: [S] BLS monthly NY-area CPI values for 2024 via search snippets. [uncertain: the 2019 annual average is from memory; bls.gov was not read]. [P*, from list] R07-028 indexation. [corrected: the ~23% figure is the US average, not the NY-area index].
data_source: BLS CPI-U New York-Newark-Jersey City, series CUURS12ASA0 https://www.bls.gov/regions/new-york-new-jersey/ (bls.gov not read from here)
how_to_model: Deflator table by month. The ledger stores both nominal and real values; the headline uses real values whenever eras are pooled.

name: Uncertain parameters and ranking stability
description: Run the leaderboard over a set of plausible draws of the guessed parameters and report whether model rankings hold, with each parameter tagged by where its value came from.
values_or_range: Parameters to vary: unserved demand 5-20% (R05-066), supply elasticity 0.2-1.0 (R06-010), price elasticity (R05-020), bot strategy mix (R06-017). Use 10-30 draws and report Kendall's tau of rankings across them [design]. Give wider ranges to values borrowed from SF, Chicago or pre-2019 studies.
impact_evidence: [design]; [U] domain randomisation (Tobin et al. 2017, IROS) is standard sim-to-real practice. If rankings flip within these ranges, the benchmark measures the guess, not the model.
how_to_model: Latin-hypercube draws over the flagged parameters, run first with cheap development models (R12-006), and a rank-stability panel published next to the headline score.

name: Exploit and degenerate-strategy audit
description: A red-team pass with scripted probes and the RL baseline to find strategies that profit from simulator artefacts rather than real skill.
values_or_range: Checklist: free or instant repositioning, zone-centroid shortcuts, zero-time trips within one zone, farming cancellation fees, resetting queues by logging off and on, gaming the displacement rule, bots that never adapt, and loopholes in end-of-day valuation. Target: no probe beats the best honest heuristic by more than a few percent [design].
impact_evidence: [U] specification-gaming examples (Krakovna et al., DeepMind blog 2020). R12-055 says RL shows 'how exploitable the world is', but there is no audit step.
how_to_model: Scripted exploit probes in CI plus periodic RL runs on development seeds; each exploit found becomes a regression test.

name: Compute and token budget per run
description: Cap on model calls, tokens or dollars for one evaluation run, which limits how many cars can get individual attention.
values_or_range: about $20 per run (team estimate); per-car control of 100 cars at one call per 5 min is 28,800 calls a day [design].
impact_evidence: Team cost estimate of $10K for 5 models x 100 runs x $20 (meeting notes) and arithmetic [design].
how_to_model: Harness meter; when the budget runs out, cars fall back to a default policy; report profit per dollar of compute.

name: Simulator scale and runtime
description: How fast the engine must run so that N-car fleets and 100 runs per model stay affordable.
values_or_range: one day with 5,000 cars in about 3 s (greedy, Manhattan); model calls dominate run time.
impact_evidence: fleetsim cut runtime from 37.3 s to 2.8 s per simulated day at 5,000 cars by using matrix indices [S].
how_to_model: Vectorised zone-matrix engine with cached travel-time matrices.

name: Compute-cost accounting
description: Whether API spend is only reported or also charged inside the game.
values_or_range: Reported only ($ and tokens per run) / in-world charge (e.g. $100 per million output tokens, as in Vending-Bench 2) / cost-adjusted score
impact_evidence: [P* via D11] Vending-Bench 2's prompt charges '$100 per million output tokens' weekly; [P via D11] HAL argues for 'accuracy and cost by default'.
how_to_model: Token meter per call; optional deduction in the ledger.

name: Tokens per decision and cache hit rate
description: Input and output tokens per model call and the share read from the prompt cache, which together set the cost of a run.
values_or_range: 8k-40k input and 0.5k-3k output tokens per call; 40-150 calls per sim-day; cache hits 0-90%
impact_evidence: Low on in-sim profit unless charged, high on budget: [design, P prices, arithmetic re-verified] at 85% cache hits, 80 calls x 20k in / 1k out per sim-day costs about $3.1 (Opus 5.5), $1.7 (Sonnet 5.5) or $7.3 (Fable 5.1); Opus 5.5 cache reads cost $0.20 vs $4 per MTok uncached; 5-minute cache writes cost 1.25x input.
how_to_model: Append-only conversation to keep cache hits high; token meter per call.

name: Campaign budget, parallelism and wall-clock
description: Total spend across models and runs, and how fast runs finish.
values_or_range: 5 models x 100 runs x $20 = $10k (team estimate); concurrency limited by provider rate limits; hours of wall-clock per run
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 runs took 5-10 real hours for 2,000 messages and about 25M tokens (verified); [design calc, re-verified] 100 runs x 11 sim-days at the standard cadence would cost about $3.4k per model on Opus 5.5 and about $8k on Fable 5.1.
how_to_model: Run scheduler with rate-limit-aware concurrency and a budget ledger per model.

name: Simulator correctness checks
description: Automatic invariant checks in every run: each car is in exactly one state, each request is served at most once, nothing changes the past, energy is never negative, and the money ledger balances.
values_or_range: Invariants: rider payment = driver pay + platform take + taxes, fees and pass-throughs (to the cent); car-state conservation; request life cycle; monotone clock. Checked on every event in development and every 1,000 events in evaluation [design]. Any violation voids the run.
impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R07-015 and R07-066 define ledgers but no balance checks.
how_to_model: Assertion layer in the event loop, end-of-run ledger reconciliation, and property-based tests in CI.

name: Handling API failures and run validity
description: What happens on API timeouts, 5xx errors, rate limits, refusals or truncated outputs: how many retries, whether the sim clock keeps running, and when a run is voided rather than scored.
values_or_range: 3 retries with backoff. The sim clock is frozen during infrastructure errors (headline track) or charged (latency track). Refusals and truncations count as model behaviour (no-op). Void and re-run on the same seed if more than 2% of calls fail for infrastructure reasons [design].
impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] Runs take hours of wall-clock time under provider rate limits (R12-065), and the serving provider changed Vending-Bench scores (R12-002).
how_to_model: A harness wrapper classifies each error as infrastructure or model, retries infrastructure errors with the clock frozen, logs counts, and voids runs above the threshold (malformed actions stay in R12-029).

name: Benchmark version freeze and re-scoring rule
description: Simulator code, calibrated parameters, data snapshot and rule tables are versioned together. Scores are compared only within a version, and older models are re-run after an upgrade.
values_or_range: A version number per release (v1.0, v1.1, ...). Major bump on any calibration or rule change. Re-run the top-k models on each major release. The leaderboard shows the version [design].
impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R12-072 records config hashes per run but has no release or re-scoring rule.
how_to_model: A release manifest hashes code, parameters, data and rules; the leaderboard is keyed by version.

name: Checkpoint, resume and fork
description: Save the full simulator state, including the position of every random stream, so an interrupted run resumes identically and counterfactual branches can fork from the same mid-day state.
values_or_range: Checkpoint every 15-60 simulated minutes [design]. Fork arms such as with vs without event info, or alternative prompts, from one shared state.
impact_evidence: [P* via list] Vending-Bench runs took 5-10 real hours (R12-065). Forking measures the value of information more precisely than rerunning whole days [design].
how_to_model: Serialise the world, agent memory, random-stream states and pending events. A resume test must give an identical log, and a fork API supports paired value-of-information tests (R12-061).

name: Model under test
description: The LLM or agent system whose decisions drive the car or fleet; the main independent variable of the benchmark.
values_or_range: 5 frontier models for the headline board (e.g. Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI and Google flagships) plus cheap development models; one model per run, or several per city in arena mode
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 2 end balances spread from about $9.2k to $15.5k across the top 7 of 66 entries, and about $7.5k-$15.5k across the top 10 (29 Sep 2026 capture, D01/D11) [corrected by fact-check: was 'across top models']; Vending-Bench 1: 'All models exhibit very high variance across their five runs' (verified in the paper text).
how_to_model: One provider adapter per model behind an identical tool schema, observation and budget.

name: Model snapshot and serving provider
description: The exact model version string and the API or host that serves it, pinned and recorded for every run.
values_or_range: Dated snapshot vs moving alias; first-party API vs third-party host vs self-hosted weights; quantisation level for open models
impact_evidence: [S via team phase-1 dossier B, GitHub copy of the Vending-Bench 1 leaderboard] Kimi K2 Thinking averaged $1,296 net worth via Moonshot's own API vs $649 via a third-party API; on the leaderboard's minimum-net-worth metric the order flips ($418.54 third-party vs $354.00 Moonshot) [corrected by fact-check: source was misattributed to D11, and the flip was omitted].
how_to_model: Run manifest records model id, provider, region, quantisation and date; leaderboard refuses unpinned aliases.

name: Reasoning effort and sampling settings
description: The thinking or effort level and sampling parameters used on every call.
values_or_range: Effort low / medium / high / xhigh / max (Claude Opus 5.5 defaults to medium); temperature only where the API accepts it; max output 1k-16k tokens per call
impact_evidence: [P] Claude API reference (cached 6 Oct 2026): effort levels, Opus 5.5 default 'medium', non-default sampling rejected on current Claude models (verified); [P* via team phase-1 notes, GitHub copy of Andon Labs posts] Opus 4.8 scored much higher at High than at Max effort on Vending-Bench 2, which Andon attributes to less context compaction [corrected by fact-check: benchmark version specified].
how_to_model: Fixed per leaderboard track; an effort x model ablation on a subset of seeds.

name: Context-management policy
description: How much run history the model sees at each step, and how older history is trimmed, summarised or moved into memory.
values_or_range: Sliding window of 10k / 30k / 60k tokens; server-side compaction (Claude default trigger 150k tokens, beta); memory tool on or off
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: GPT-4o mini with a 60k-token memory did worse than with 30k, and collapse was not explained by the context filling up (Pearson r = 0.167 between days until sales stop and days until full memory) (verified in the paper text); compaction default 150k verified in the bundled Claude API reference.
how_to_model: Harness-level policy fixed in the frozen track; token counts logged per step.

name: Frozen harness vs bring-your-own agent
description: Whether every model runs inside one fixed agent loop (measures the model) or teams may bring their own scaffold (measures the whole system and its cost).
values_or_range: Frozen: fixed tools, prompts, context policy and budgets / BYO: any scaffold, reaching the simulator only through the same metered tool API
impact_evidence: [P via D10] SWE-bench bash-only and Terminal-Bench's separate --agent and --model flags exist because scaffolds move scores enough to need separate tracks.
how_to_model: Two leaderboard tracks; BYO tool calls metered by the tool server.

name: Development model tier
description: Cheap models used to build, debug and red-team the simulator and harness before paying for frontier runs.
values_or_range: Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok for prompts of 100K tokens or fewer; $0.50 / $2.50 above), Sonnet 5.5 ($2 / $10), open-weight Qwen models self-hosted or hosted; also usable as bot drivers
impact_evidence: [P] Claude price table (cached 6 Oct 2026): Haiku 5.5 costs 1/40 of Opus 5.5 per token, but its tokenizer counts the same text as about 30% more tokens, so it is about 1/31 per unit of text [corrected by fact-check: long-prompt tier and tokenizer added]; the team's '80-90% of the intelligence at 1/100 of the cost' for Qwen is unverified [U].
data_source: Claude pricing https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing; Qwen model cards (Hugging Face, not reachable here)
how_to_model: Dev configuration profile; never mixed into headline results.

name: Base system prompt and paraphrase set
description: The fixed instructions that set the task, rules and tools, plus a few paraphrases to check that rankings do not hinge on wording.
values_or_range: Minimal / standard / detailed-rules prompt; 2-3 meaning-preserving paraphrases per variant
impact_evidence: [P] Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov and Suhr 2023 (arXiv 2310.11324), FormatSpread repo: LLM results shift with meaning-preserving prompt formatting; the README gives no magnitude, and the size of the effect for long agentic runs is [U].
how_to_model: Prompts versioned with the benchmark; headline uses the standard prompt; paraphrases run on a seed subset.

name: Objective statement and cost framing
description: What the prompt says to maximise and which costs it makes salient.
values_or_range: Net profit per online hour / total daily net profit / gross revenue; costs itemised in the prompt vs only in the ledger; optional constraint text such as 'be home by 02:00'
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: setting the $2 daily fee to zero did not raise sales; without cost pressure GPT-4o mini 'appears to get stuck in loops' (verified in the paper text).
how_to_model: One canonical objective for the headline (net profit per online hour after all costs); others as ablations.

name: Strategy hints
description: Whether the prompt includes driver know-how such as airport runs, the Manhattan core at rush hour, or avoiding drop-offs that strand the car.
values_or_range: None / generic tips / NYC-specific playbook
impact_evidence: [P via D10] Project Vend 2: 'Among the most impactful changes we made was forcing Claudius to follow procedures'; [S via R01] Haggag, McManus and Paci (2017, AEJ: Applied): neighbourhood experience raises NYC taxi drivers' productivity.
how_to_model: Hints off for the headline so the benchmark measures the model's own strategy; hints as an ablation.

name: Role framing
description: Which operator the model plays, which fixes its rules, costs and allowed actions.
values_or_range: Human app driver (Uber/Lyft, NYC HVFHV) / yellow or green taxi (street hail plus e-hail) / robotaxi operator (no driver; usually fleet level)
impact_evidence: [P] own computation, TLC Jan 2023 weekdays: HVFHV driver pay $54.04 per engaged hour vs yellow $109.84 gross per engaged hour (total_amount incl. surcharges, tolls and card tips only, not driver take-home; 'engaged' = passenger on board), so roles face different economics [corrected by fact-check: cash tips are not recorded in total_amount].
how_to_model: Role selects a rule pack (fares, fees, hours rules, actions) from R07-R09; persona details are R09-004.

name: Simulation disclosure
description: Whether the model is told it is in a benchmark simulation or framed as doing a real job, which can change its conduct.
values_or_range: Disclosed / neutral / framed as real
impact_evidence: [P* via D01/D11] Andon Labs: Claude Fable 5 skipped paying a customer because 'customers are part of the simulation anyway'; effect on profit unmeasured [U].
how_to_model: Framing twins on a seed subset; conduct metrics reported by framing.

name: Observation content per step
description: The state fields shown to the agent each time it is asked to act.
values_or_range: Clock, zone and coordinates, status (idle / en route / occupied / charging / offline), fuel or battery, earnings and costs so far, hours online, the pending offer (fields per R05-036), nearby signals
impact_evidence: [P] tomslee/ridehail reports vehicle time as P1 (waiting for a trip), P2 (en route to pickup) and P3 (with passenger), the standard state split (verified in README); [design].
how_to_model: Fixed observation schema versioned with the benchmark.

name: Observation and action format
description: How the state is rendered to the model and how its actions come back.
values_or_range: JSON / natural-language summary / ASCII grid map / rendered map image (multimodal); actions via strict tool schemas vs parsed free text
impact_evidence: [P] the MIT-licensed LPSim (Large-scale Parallel Simulator, GitHub Xuan-1998) exposes get_state(), a to_prompt_context() natural-language view and a TOOL_DEFINITION for OpenAI/Anthropic function calling, for LLM fleet control [corrected by fact-check: '(MIT)' was the licence, not the institution].
how_to_model: Default JSON plus a short text summary with strict tool schemas; image map as an ablation.

name: Action space and granularity
description: The set of moves the agent can make and their spatial and time resolution.
values_or_range: Accept / decline offer; reposition to a zone (263 TLC zones) or a point; wait N minutes; cruise loop (taxi); go offline or take a break; go home; refuel or charge; set destination filter; optional route choice (R10-042)
impact_evidence: [P] MaaSSim models drivers who 'reject/accept incoming requests', 'strategically re-position while being idle' and 'opt-out of the system' (verified in README); [design]; the spatial unit itself is R01-009.
how_to_model: Typed tools with validation; the same set for every model within a role.

name: Decision cadence and wake-up rule
description: When the model is called: on each event, on a fixed tick, or when it asks to be woken.
values_or_range: Event-driven (offer, drop-off, arrival, idle timer every 5 / 10 / 15 sim-min) / fixed tick of 1 / 5 / 15 min / agent-set wait(until)
impact_evidence: [P via D10] YC-Bench jumps to the next event and Vending-Bench clones charge sim-minutes per call; [design] calls per sim-day set both how much skill can show and the run cost (R12-063).
how_to_model: Discrete-event core (SimPy-style priority queue) wakes the agent on events plus an idle heartbeat.

name: Wall-clock coupling and model latency
description: Whether simulated time stops while the model thinks, or slow answers cost sim time and missed offers.
values_or_range: Paused (turn-based) / latency-charged (sim time advances by measured latency x factor) / real time
impact_evidence: [S via R06-024] real ride offers time out after about 10-15 s; long reasoning calls can exceed that [U], so latency modes would heavily penalise slow models.
how_to_model: Headline paused; latency-charged as a separate track; latency recorded on every call.

name: Tool-call time cost and per-step budget
description: How much sim time information queries take, and how many tool calls are allowed per decision.
values_or_range: 0 or 1 sim-min per query; 3-10 tool calls per step; optional daily query cap
impact_evidence: [P via D10] ProsusAI vending-bench charges 5-75 sim-min per tool call inside a working day (5 for reads, prices and notes; 25 for email, search and payments; 75 for stocking and cash collection) [corrected by fact-check: was 5-45]; [design] without any cost an agent can query everything every step for free (cross-link R09-067).
how_to_model: Per-tool time-cost table and a call counter enforced by the harness.

name: Invalid or malformed action policy
description: What happens when the model returns an illegal, malformed or impossible action.
values_or_range: No-op with error message / up to K retries / default safe action (wait) / penalty per invalid call
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 runs fell into 'meltdown' loops (verified in the paper text); [design] cheap models break format more often, so this policy can dominate their scores.
how_to_model: Validate against the tool schema, return the error, count invalid calls as a reported metric.

name: Within-step update order
description: The fixed order in which request arrivals, surge updates, batch matching, bot moves, agent actions and state updates run when events share a timestamp.
values_or_range: A fixed, documented order, e.g. arrivals -> surge computed from the pre-match state -> matching -> bots -> agent -> state. Ties broken by a seeded random draw or by entity id. Sensitivity test with 2-3 alternative orders [design].
impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R12-026 specifies a SimPy-style priority queue but no ordering for events with the same timestamp.
how_to_model: Priority classes in the event queue; a unit test that results do not depend on container order; report the score change under alternative orders.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Episode horizon and shift window
description: The length of one scored episode and when it may start and end.
values_or_range: One shift (8-12 h) / one day (24 h, agent picks its shift) / 10-day block / week; start at home at a fixed or chosen time; starting fuel or charge
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: agents often stopped selling after some sim-days (mean days until sales stop 8-102 by model; verified in Table 1), so long horizons expose derailment that short ones hide.
how_to_model: Scenario config sets horizon and start state; shift start inside a day is an agent action.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: End-of-episode valuation and go-home rule
description: How the final position, charge and unfinished trips are valued, so the agent cannot game the last hour.
values_or_range: End at home required, or penalised by the deadhead cost home; leftover charge valued at energy cost; trip in progress completed or prorated
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 valued inventory at cost and its highest-net-worth run prioritised storage over cash; [design] the team's 'take me home' feature needs a terminal rule (cross-link R09-020).
how_to_model: Terminal settlement step in the ledger.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Memory carry-over scope
description: Which notes and learnings persist between days and between runs.
values_or_range: None / within one 10-day run / across runs (lifelong notes) / across models (not allowed)
impact_evidence: [design] the learning test only works if notes persist across days; [P] own computation: a 10-day window already holds most of the learnable weekday pattern (WAPE 0.134 vs 0.120 for a plain 19-weekday mean) [corrected by fact-check: 0.120 is a reference level, not a proven floor].
how_to_model: Memory store snapshotted at day boundaries and cleared per protocol arm.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Memory format, size cap and reflection step
description: The form and size of stored learnings, and whether the agent gets an end-of-day turn to write them.
values_or_range: Free-text notes capped at 2k / 8k / 20k tokens; key-value store; table; end-of-day reflection turn on or off
impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 gave a scratchpad, key-value store and vector database (verified); [P via D11] YC-Bench found scratchpad use 'the strongest predictor of success'.
how_to_model: Memory tool with a hard size cap; reflection prompt at the end of each sim-day.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Training window composition (days 1-10)
description: Which calendar days make up the learning days.
values_or_range: 10 consecutive days including weekends and holidays / weekdays only / matched day types; same month vs mixed seasons
impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-verified): predicting 11 Jan from all of 1-10 Jan (including the New Year holidays) gives zone-hour WAPE 0.238 vs 0.134 from the six non-holiday weekdays, so the window decides what can be learned.
how_to_model: Scenario builder picks windows from a calendar table with holiday flags (R02).

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Test day choice (day 11)
description: Which day the learned agent is tested on.
values_or_range: Next day / same weekday a week later / weekend / event day / shock day / different season
impact_evidence: [P] own computation (re-verified): in the previous 10 days a weekday target has 5-8 same-type days but a weekend target only 2-3; rolling day-type-aware zone-hour WAPE ran 0.11-0.28 for HVFHV (median 0.174) and 0.14-0.34 for yellow (median 0.198).
how_to_model: Test pool stratified by day type; learning gain reported per stratum.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Repetition design (the 'x100')
description: How the team's '10 days x 100 runs' is read: 100 independent 10-day runs, or 100 passes over the same days with accumulating notes.
values_or_range: Independent replicates (fresh memory each) / repeated epochs with persistent memory / epochs with demand redrawn each pass
impact_evidence: [design] repeated exact replays let notes memorise specific requests, which is overfitting, not learning; [P] own computation: even a 19-weekday mean leaves zone-hour WAPE of about 0.12, so accuracy well beyond that on replayed days is a warning sign of memorisation [corrected by fact-check: was 'gains beyond that are memorisation'; covariate-aware learners could beat a plain mean somewhat].
how_to_model: Protocol config; demand redrawn from the generator on every epoch.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: Learning-gain control arms
description: Comparison runs that turn 'score on day 11' into a measure of learning.
values_or_range: Day 11 with memory vs (a) the same model with empty memory, (b) with expert-written notes, (c) with notes written by another model
impact_evidence: [P] Anthropic, 'A statistical approach to model evaluations' (read directly): report paired differences on shared items; [design].
how_to_model: Same seeds across arms; learning gain is the paired difference.

sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
name: What state carries over between days
description: Which physical and account states persist from days 1-10 into day 11: car position, fuel or charge, rating, acceptance and cancellation rates, weekly quest progress, weekly lease, weekly hours used and fatigue.
values_or_range: Options: reset everything daily / carry position and energy / carry account standing / carry everything (default for the learning test) [design]. Weekly items: quests (R07-033), leases (R02-045), and the TLC passenger-time cap of 10 h per 24 h and 60 h per week (R09-005).
impact_evidence: [S, from list] Weekly quests, leases and hour caps; [design]. R12-033 covers memory notes only. [corrected: the TLC cap counts passenger time only].
how_to_model: State snapshot at each day boundary, with a carry flag per field. The learning protocol (R12-033) declares which flags are set.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Hourly rider wait (market tightness)
description: Time from request to pickup by hour, a public proxy for how short of drivers the market is.
values_or_range: Median request-to-pickup 3.3 min (weekday 10-11h) to 5.2 min (Sat 23h, Sun 06h); 8.6 min on NYE 01h; JFK pickups 9.6 min at 22-23h
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; on-scene times only for Uber (HV0003)
how_to_model: Calibration target for supply model (R06); simulate driver supply per hour so waits match

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Surge frequency calibration target
description: How often, when and how strongly app prices rise above normal, estimated from public trip fares and used to calibrate the surge module.
values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays, non-shared trips of normal duration (<= 1.1x the OD median time): 6.9-7.8% priced >= 1.3x the median fare for the same platform and OD pair, and 2.6-3.0% >= 1.6x (the range covers two filters). By request hour: 12.4-13.0% at 07-08h, 8.4-9.0% at 17-18h, 3.2-3.9% at 02-04h (our re-check vs the critic). Drivers get a lower share of surged fares (median pay/fare 0.67-0.68 vs 0.72).
impact_evidence: [P] Own calc (g1/a2.py), re-run in this fact-check, plus an hourly re-check with holidays excluded; it agrees with the gap critic within 1 point. This is a proxy: the duration filter keeps faster-than-median trips, and the fare ratio includes upfront-price noise and route differences.
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV records (base_passenger_fare by OD and time)
how_to_model: Tune surge thresholds (R07-020) until the simulated distribution of fare ratios by hour matches the target. Calibration fails if it is off by more than a set number of percentage points.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Trip duration distribution (validation target)
description: Distribution of in-car time per trip, used to check that simulated trips take as long as real ones.
values_or_range: Yellow 2023: median 12.8 min, mean 16.5 min; HVFHV Jan 2023: median 15.0 min, mean 18.1 min [fact-check: confirmed from data, was [U]]; longer in PM peak
impact_evidence: [P*] own calc on local TLC Parquet copies (trip_time, pickup/dropoff times); time per trip is the denominator of profit per hour; cross-link R10
how_to_model: Not generated directly; harness compares simulated vs empirical duration by OD and hour

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Supply calibration targets
description: Public statistics the background supply must reproduce.
values_or_range: TLC monthly: unique drivers, unique vehicles, vehicles per day, hours per day per vehicle and per driver, trips per day, minutes per trip; HVFHV: on-scene minus request by zone and hour (Uber rows only; Lyft leaves on_scene_datetime empty) [corrected by fact-check], driver_pay per trip-hour (no driver ID, so not per online hour); FHV base report: trips and unique vehicles per base; Schaller empty share and idle gaps.
impact_evidence: TLC monthly report columns [S, read in GitHub import code; re-read by fact-check: trips_per_day, farebox_per_day, unique_drivers, unique_vehicles, vehicles_per_day, avg days and hours per vehicle and per driver, avg_minutes_per_trip, trips_per_day_shared]; HVFHV columns [S].
data_source: TLC monthly CSV; HVFHV records; FHV Base Aggregate Report
how_to_model: Fit log-on curves and the archetype mix by simulated method of moments; hold out months for validation.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Calibration target and acceptance error
description: Which observed statistic the travel-time model must match and how closely.
values_or_range: zone-pair x hour-of-week median and P90 of TLC durations; target MAPE 15-20% or better on a held-out month [design]; OD neighbour averaging beat route-based methods and map APIs on 173M 2013 NYC trips
impact_evidence: Wang et al. 2016 SIGSPATIAL, arXiv 1512.08580 [S]
data_source: TLC yellow, green and HVFHV trip records
how_to_model: Hold out a month; report MAPE by distance band, hour and borough; fail the build above threshold.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Calibration targets and sim-to-real validation
description: Real-world statistics the simulator must reproduce before any model is scored.
values_or_range: Zone x hour pickups (sim-vs-real WAPE near the real day-to-day reference of 0.12-0.13); HVFHV pay about $54 per passenger-on-board hour (weekdays, Jan 2023); median request-to-pickup 3.5-4.2 min (weekdays, Jan 2023); speeds by hour (R10)
impact_evidence: [P] own computation on the TLC Jan 2023 HVFHV and yellow files (re-verified against the script output; 0.12-0.13 is a reference level, not a proven floor [corrected by fact-check]).
data_source: NYC TLC trip records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9 (minute-level data; portal update frequency listed as Daily)
how_to_model: CI suite runs scripted policies and checks the targets on held-out days.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Back-tests on real policy changes and shocks
description: Checks that the sim, calibrated on data from before a real policy change or shock, reproduces the change observed after it.
values_or_range: Candidate tests: the CBD toll from 5 Jan 2025 (speeds and trips, R10-005); HVFHV lockout rules (R07-030); the distance-factor reset on 13 Mar 2023 (R07-028); storms such as 29 Sep 2023 (R04-025). Pass if the predicted change is within +/-30-50% of the observed one [design].
impact_evidence: [P, from list] Congestion-pricing speed regime (R10-005); yellow trips +19% from 2024 to 2025 (R02-033); [design].
data_source: NYC TLC trip records before and after each change; NYC DOT traffic speeds; MTA CBD toll data (data.ny.gov)
how_to_model: Calibrate on the pre-period, switch the rule or shock on, and compare simulated vs observed changes in trips, speeds, waits and pay.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Leftover easy-profit gap (no-free-lunch check)
description: The largest allowed gap between the best simple fixed strategy, such as always waiting at zone X at hour Y, and the average background driver's net hourly earnings.
values_or_range: Target: the best fixed heuristic beats the median bot by no more than 10-15% in net $/h [design]. Real-world reference: across 20 non-holiday weekdays in Jan 2023, HVFHV driver pay per engaged hour stayed between $52.42 and $55.82 ($55.43-59.30 with tips) while daily trips ranged from 478k to 701k (r = -0.16) [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check].
impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file; [S] Buchholz 2022 (REStud) on the spatial equilibrium of NYC taxi search; [S] Hall, Horton & Knoepfle 2023 (NBER w30883) on re-equilibration (via R06-012).
data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (driver_pay, tips, trip_time)
how_to_model: A CI test grid-searches simple fixed policies (zone x hour waits, always-airport) against the bots, and calibration fails if any beats the target margin persistently across seeds.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
name: Fare and pay engine validation
description: Recompute fare components and driver pay for replayed trips from the rule tables and the simulated route, and compare them with the recorded TLC fields against a threshold.
values_or_range: Target: median absolute error under 5% per trip for base fare and driver pay, and an exact match for fixed fees (congestion surcharge, airport fee, black car fund) [design].
impact_evidence: [P] TLC files itemise fares (schemas re-read by fact-check from local 2023 files): HVFHV base_passenger_fare, tolls, bcf, sales_tax, congestion_surcharge, airport_fee, tips, driver_pay; yellow fare_amount, extra, mta_tax, tip_amount, tolls_amount, improvement_surcharge, congestion_surcharge, Airport_fee. R12-066 checks only pay per hour.
data_source: NYC TLC yellow and HVFHV trip records
how_to_model: Run a sample of trips through the fare engine, using the rule vintage for the date (R07-065) and the simulated route. Report error by component and fail CI above the threshold.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Driver-level outcomes (utilisation, idle gap, pings, cruising share)
name: Ping rate per idle hour
description: How many offers an idle driver gets per hour in a given zone and hour.
values_or_range: About 1.8 trips per online hour citywide, so about 4-8 offers per idle hour; 1-15 by zone [design].
impact_evidence: [design] from ~667k trips/day [S] and ~58% utilisation [S]; arithmetic re-checked by fact-check (667k trips / ~363k online vehicle-hours = ~1.8).
data_source: Derived from HVFHV trips and the supply field
how_to_model: Emerges from the matcher; report as a metric; check against TLC trips per vehicle per hour.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Driver-level outcomes (utilisation, idle gap, pings, cruising share)
name: Utilisation rate
description: Share of online time with a passenger; the main multiplier on hourly pay and an input to the TLC pay formula.
values_or_range: About 59% in the Manhattan core (app cars empty 41% of the time south of 96th St, 2019) and about 58% citywide (2024) [S]; platforms held to at least 50-53% (2024) [uncertain: not re-checked]; since 1 Aug 2025 the pay floor divides by fixed applied rates of 53.3% (per minute) and 68.5% (per mile) instead of each company's actual utilisation [corrected by fact-check: P*, 35 RCNY 59D-22(b)].
impact_evidence: TLC data cited in the 2019 cruising-cap ruling [S]; 2024 city deal (Lyft utilisation at least 50%) [S]; 2024 citywide ~58% (Bloomberg, via R07) [S]; TLC defines utilisation as the share of available time or distance spent carrying passengers [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-03(j)].
how_to_model: Track per driver; platform-wide utilisation drives lockouts (R06) and pay (R07).

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Driver-level outcomes (utilisation, idle gap, pings, cruising share)
name: Idle gap between trips
description: Minutes from one drop-off to the next pickup.
values_or_range: Manhattan core: 8 min (yellow) and 11 min (app cars) in 2017; longer in the outer boroughs.
impact_evidence: Schaller 2017 [S].
data_source: Schaller report; TLC trip records (cannot be chained per car publicly)
how_to_model: Emergent; validation target.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Driver-level outcomes (utilisation, idle gap, pings, cruising share)
name: Cruising and idle share
description: Share of time or miles without a passenger while waiting for the next request.
values_or_range: ~41% of HVFHV time without a passenger in Manhattan below 96th St (2019); TLC cap adopted Aug 2019 (35 RCNY 59D-21: 36% from Feb 2020, 31% from Aug 2020, weekdays 6 AM-11 PM and weekends 8 AM-11 PM in the Congestion Zone; en-route time to pickups counts as cruising; WAVs exempt) [P*], still printed in the rules but annulled by a state court in Dec 2019 and not enforced [U]; ~33% of ride-hail VMT waiting or cruising (six US metros)
impact_evidence: 35 RCNY 59D-21 [P*]; TLC 2019 cruising rule documents [S]; Fehr & Peers 2019 [S]
data_source: TLC reports; HVFHV records lack a vehicle ID so gaps between trips cannot be rebuilt [P*: no vehicle or driver ID in the HVFHV schema]
how_to_model: Emerges from the simulation; report it as a metric and use the 41% figure as a sanity check for baseline policies.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Fleet-level outcomes (empty miles, clustering, saturation, availability)
name: Robotaxi trips per car per day
description: Trips per robotaxi per day, a realism ceiling for the robotaxi agent.
values_or_range: About 19-24 trips per car per day (about 500k rides/week across 3,000-3,800 cars, Mar 2026) [corrected by fact-check: arithmetic range; 2025 figures of 450k+ rides/week on ~2,500 cars give ~26, S, GitHub company profile].
impact_evidence: Waymo 500k paid rides/week (Mar 2026) [S]; division [design].
data_source: Waymo statements; CPUC quarterly AV reports [U]
how_to_model: Validation target for robotaxi runs.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Fleet-level outcomes (empty miles, clustering, saturation, availability)
name: Empty miles from rebalancing
description: Unpaid miles the fleet drives to pickups, repositioning and charging, which cost energy, wear and tolls.
values_or_range: about 0.9-1.0 empty miles per trip without repositioning [corrected by fact-check: greedy pickup deadhead was 0.90-1.10 mi per trip across 1,500-6,000 cars and 0.85-0.87 with batching; 0.906 at 5,000 cars] and about 1.7 with it (Manhattan robotaxi sim); about one third of Manhattan cars empty at any moment (R06-002).
impact_evidence: fleetsim: repositioning raised empty miles per trip 87% (0.906 to 1.697), about 11% more empty miles per 1% of wait removed [S].
data_source: TLC trip records (trip miles) for calibration
how_to_model: Summed per car; cost per mile from R08; empty-mile share reported as a KPI.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Fleet-level outcomes (empty miles, clustering, saturation, availability)
name: Own-car clustering (herding)
description: Fleet cars piling into the same hotspot because they react to the same signal, leaving gaps elsewhere.
values_or_range: own idle cars per zone vs forecast requests; dispersion index from 0 (spread) to 1 (all in one zone).
impact_evidence: [U] DiDi's multi-agent RL for fleet repositioning (Lin et al., KDD 2018) was built to stop agents chasing the same orders [uncertain: paper not re-read this session]; surge chasing herds human drivers (R06-011) [S].
how_to_model: Compute a dispersion metric every epoch; show it on the map.

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
sub_box: Fleet-level outcomes (empty miles, clustering, saturation, availability)
name: Fleet saturation curve (value of the N-th car)
description: How revenue and utilisation per car fall as the fleet grows in a fixed market.
values_or_range: Manhattan robotaxi sim: utilisation 57% at 1,500 cars, 50% at 3,000, 34% at 5,000, 28% at 6,000.
impact_evidence: fleetsim greedy sweep [S]; own-fleet cannibalisation (R06-062); Vazifeh et al. 2018: about 30% fewer cars could serve NYC taxi demand (R06-062) [S].

box: Calibration targets and KPIs (outputs, not inputs)
